ACHIEVEMENTS OF NeGP, CSCs AND DeGS 
 
*149. SHRI GANESH SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a) the major achievements of the National e -Governance Plan (NeGP), Common Service 
Centres (CSCs) and District e-Governance Societies (DeGSs) since their inception; 
(b) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of their impact on digital 
inclusion, ease of access to Government services, transparency, citizen satisfaction and rural 
service delivery and if so, the details thereof;  
(c) the number of CSCs currently operational, services delivered and beneficiaries covered, 
State and district-wise including Madhya Pradesh particularly Satna district; 
(d) the details of role played by DeGS in implementing e-District and Digital India initiatives 
at the district level along with the outcomes achieved thereof; and 
(e) the steps being taken by the Government to further strengthen CSCs and DeGS as last -
mile digital service delivery institutions under the vision of Digital India? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF ELECTRONICS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI ASHWINI VAISHNAW) 
 
  
(a) to (e):  A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 

 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN THE REPLY TO LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *149 FOR 29.07.2026 REGARDING “ACHIEVEMENTS OF NeGP, 
CSCs AND DeGS” 
****** 
 
(a) to (e):  National e-Governance Plan (NeGP): 
The National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was approved by the Government in May 2006 with 
the vision of making all Government services accessible to the common man in his locality, 
through common service delivery outlets, and to ensure efficiency, transparency  and 
reliability of such services at affordable costs. The foundational digital infrastructure created 
under NeGP includes: 
 
● State Data Centres (SDCs), 
● Statewide Area Networks (SWANs), 
● State Service Delivery Gateways (SSDGs) and 
● Common Services Centres (CSCs). 
● NeGP also resulted in Mission Mode projects such as Passport, Land Record 
Management, e-Office, Computerisation of Public Distribution System, etc. 
 
Digital India Programme: 
The Government launched the Digital India Programme in July 2015, under which the 
National e-Governance Plan (NeGP) was subsumed. At its core, the programme promotes 
three interconnected goals: strengthening digital infrastructure, delivering government 
services digitally, and empowering citizens through digital literacy and employment. 
During the recent AI Impact Summit, President Macron of France stated that India has built 
foundational DPI which no other country in the world has built. 
Key Digital Public Infrastructure initiatives: 
India has developed the unique digital public infrastructure which has enabled large scale 
digital solutions for our people.  
  
Aadhaar: 
● Over 1.44+ billion Aadhaar numbers have been generated. 
● Through Aadhaar-linked Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT), cash benefits from various 
welfare schemes (318 Schemes of 56 Ministries) are directly transferred into 
beneficiaries' bank accounts. This has done with the requirement of multiple 
documents and eliminated duplicate or fake beneficiaries. Over Rs. 52 lakh crore has 
been transferred through DBT nationwide. 
 
Unified Payments Interface (UPI): 
● UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 
banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. 
● UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real -time 
digital payments. 
 
DigiLocker. The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with more than 936.03 crore 
documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. 
 

Unified Mobile Application for New -age Governance (UMANG): The platform offers 
2,575 services for individuals, including 48 services integrated by the Government of Madhya 
Pradesh. 
 
e-Sanjeevani facilitates quick and easy access to doctors and medical specialists directly from 
your smartphone. The platform has served over 48 crore patients across the country. 
 
MeriPehchaan/National Single Sign -On (NSSO) is a user authentication service wherein 
single set of credentials can provide access to multiple online applications or services. 
Currently, 17,540 services of various Ministries/States have been integrated with NSSO. 
 
Assisted delivery of services through Common Service Centres (CSCs) 
● The CSC Scheme, a strategic cornerstone of NeGP approved in September 2006, was 
restructured as CSC 2.0 in August 2015 under Digital India, with the objective of 
establishing at least one CSC in each of the approximately 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats 
in the country. 
● CSCs are delivering a wide range of Government -to-Citizen (G2C), Business -to-
Citizen (B2C), financial, educational, healthcare, utility, agriculture and other digital 
services. Over 800 digital services are being delivered through the CSC network, 
benefiting crores of citizens every year. 
● State-wise (including MP) and district -wise (including Satna) list of CSCs may be 
seen at www.csc.gov.in. Total functional CSCs are as follows: 
●  
  As of May, 2014 As of May, 2026 
Number of CSCs 83,950 5,01,731 
  
● 2,56,743 Gram Panchayats have been covered with CSCs. 
● During the financial years 2025-26, a total of 4854.03 lakh transactions were carried 
out through the CSC network while during 2014-15, a total of 457.29 lakh transaction 
was carried out, reflecting the scale of citizen -centric services availed through CSC  
network 
● State-wise transaction details are enclosed at Annexure-I while district -wise 
transaction details for Madhya Pradesh, including Satna district, are enclosed at 
Annexure-II. 
 
e-District Mission Mode Project (MMP): The e -District MMP has enabled electronic 
delivery of high-volume citizen-centric services such as certificates (income, caste, domicile, 
birth and death), pensions, revenue services and licences at the district level. Nearly 2,000 e-
District/e-Government services across all 36 States/UTs have been integrated with 
DigiLocker and the e-District platform, enabling anytime, anywhere access to citizens. 
 
District e-Governance Societies (DeGS): DeGS are registered societies under the respective 
State Governments and District Administrations.  They function as the nodal institutional 
mechanism at the district level and sub district levels for implementation and monitoring of 
e-District, CSC and other e-Governance/Digital India initiatives, including rollout of district 
service delivery infrastructure, capacity building, and coordination among district -level 
departments and stakeholders. 
 
Assessment of digital initiatives: 

● The Government has, from time to time, undertaken assessment and impact studies of 
e-Governance initiatives under the Digital India Programme through periodic 
monitoring, stakeholder consultations and independent third-party evaluations. 
● In 2025, a survey -based study titled “Digital India Program: Citizen Feedback & 
Actionable Insights” was conducted to assess digital adoption and its evolving impact. 
The study found that 90% of respondents were aware of and had used digital services, 
particularly Aadhaar, UPI/BHIM, Digilocker, Ration Card services and other digital 
services. Further, 71% accessed Digital India services at least once a month, of whom 
77% reported increased usage over time. Additionally, 88% of respondents expressed 
pride in  India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, such as Aadhaar and UPI, and its 
growing global recognition. 
● The third-party evaluation of Electronic Governance scheme was conducted through 
India Institute of Public administration (IIPA), Delhi in November, 2025. The study 
has highlighted that the Digital India Programme has significantly transformed citizen 
service delivery by leveraging technology to improve access to information and 
integrate government services. It has enhanced transparency, reduced service delivery 
time, promoted paperless and faceless governance, expanded digital inclusion, and 
empowered citizens through improved social and economic outcomes. 
 
Further, the following assessment was also undertaken to evaluate the impact of Common 
Services Centres (CSCs): 
● An independent impact assessment of the Common Services Centres (CSC) Scheme 
(CSC 1.0) was carried out by the Centre for Innovations in Public Systems (CIPS), 
Hyderabad. 
It emerged from the assessment study of CSC 1.0 that the CSC initiative holds 
substantial potential for viability, and long -term sustainability. The CSC scheme is 
indeed a powerful vehicle not only for the efficient and effective delivery of citizen 
services but also for promoting entrepreneurship among the rural population and 
spurring socio-economic developmental activity. 
● A mid-term impact assessment of CSC 2.0 was carried out by the Indian School of 
Business (ISB), Hyderabad. The report analysed that CSCs reduced citizens' travel 
distance by 27.25 km, travel time by 40.43 minutes, waiting time by 69.45 minutes, 
travel cost by ₹52.12, and wage loss by ₹179.44 per transaction. 
● End-Term Impact Assessment was conducted by the Academy of Management 
Studies (AMS). The assessment reported that 98% of beneficiaries were able to obtain 
the required services through CSCs, 93% perceived a positive impact on their lives 
and 95% expressed satisfaction with the services delivered through CSCs. 
 
The Government has undertaken various measures to further strengthen CSCs as last -mile 
digital service delivery centres, which include: 
● Expansion of broadband connectivity through BharatNet to Gram Panchayats and 
rural institutions. As of June 2026, a total of 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) has 
been made service-ready under the BharatNet Project across the country 
● Expansion of the portfolio of citizen-centric digital services through CSCs 
● CSC e -Governance Service India Limited has developed and implemented an AI -
based Segmentation Module in the SPECTA platform for data-driven monitoring and 
analysis of CSC operations. The module leverages Artificial Intelligence (AI), 
Machine Learning (ML) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to rank Village Level 
Entrepreneurs (VLEs) based on service delivery and transaction patterns and to 
categorize CSC services into appropriate business segments 

● Chief Secretaries/Chief Administrators of States/UTs have also been requested in 
respect of strengthening the participation of State/UT Governments and District e -
Governance Societies (DeGS) in CSC project implementation, VLE selection along 
with integration of State/UT e-District services with the CSC portal to improve VLE 
sustainability and citizen-centric service delivery. 
● Enhancing the Digital Seva Portal, integration of additional Central and State 
Government services with digital seva portal alongwith Capacity building and skill 
development of Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs) 
● Improving service delivery mechanisms and working in close coordination with 
Central Ministries, State Governments.

particularly in Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh and Udaipur district; 
 
(d) the details of financial assistance released by the Government for implementation of NEP 
2020, State/UT-wise; and 
 
(e) whether the Central Government proposes to engage with State Governments, particularly 
Karnataka to ensure uniform implementation of NEP, 2020 benchmarks and if so, the details 
thereof alongwith the details of initiatives for improving Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)?

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART S (a) TO (e) OF  THE LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 15 ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 ASKED BY 
SHRI PRAVEEN PATEL AND SHRI LUMBARAM CHOUDHARY, HON’BLE 
MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT REGARDING “ IMPLEMENTATION OF 
NATIONAL EDUCATION POLICY (NEP), 2020” 
 
(a): After announcement of National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020), a number of 
transformative changes have taken place in school education for its implementation. Several 
initiatives have been ta ken and the centrally sponsored schemes namely, Samagra Shiksha, 
PM Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI), Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM 
POSHAN) and Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society (ULLAS)  have been 
aligned with the objectives and vision of NEP 2020. 
 NEP 2020 gives the highest priority to achieving universal Foundational Literacy and 
Numeracy (FLN) for all children by Grade 2  and accordingly,  the Department launched 
National Initiative for  Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy (NIPUN 
Bharat Mission) under the aegis of the NEP and aligned with centrally sponsored scheme of 
Samagra Shiksha for early learning across States and Union Territories. 
  Implemented across the country, a range of interventions have been undertaken  under 
the Mission . These include nationwide implementation of Vidya Pravesh, a three -month 
school-readiness module for all Grade 1 students; large-scale teacher and school head training 
through NISHTHA (National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic 
Advancement)-FLN focusing on activity -based and child -centric pedagogy; provision of 
play-based and digital learning resources such as DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for 
Knowledge Sharing)- FLN content, Jaadui Pitara- a collection of Learning Teaching Material 
(LTM)  & e-Jaadui Pitara for children in the 3 –8 age group, Primers developed in 121 Local 
Languages for foundational literacy and numeracy in mother tongue  and teaching learning 
material for students.  
 Further, guidelines on co -location of Anganwadi Centres with primary schools, 
released on 3rd September 2025, ensure convergence between school education and 
Anganwadis, supporting smoother transition from pre-school to Grade 1. 
 NEP 2020 st resses upon providing multidisciplinary and a holistic education across 
the sciences, social sciences, arts, humanities, and sports for a multidisciplinary world in 
order to ensure the unity and integrity of all knowledge. 
 NEP 2020 provides for 50 hours of Continuous Professional Development (CPD) for 
teachers with focus on pedagogy, digital literacy and subject specific expertise. NCTE has 
developed a guiding document- National Professional Standards for Teachers (NPST) -which 
defines the work of teachers and makes explicit elements of high -quality, effective teaching 
in 21st century schools that will improve educational outcomes for students. Also, National 
Mission for Mentoring (NMM)  was launched for  creation of a large pool o f outstanding 
professionals willing to provide mentoring to school teachers. 
(b):  Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI)  schools are being set up as NEP 
2020 exemplar schools and are expected to become the template for other schools. As of 
now, a total of 13,092 PM SHRI schools have been selected from 33 States/UTs, based on 
prescribed minimum benchmark through UDISE+ data . The scheme aims to saturate the  

 
 
selected schools with 21 NEP components such as computer lab/ICT lab/smart classrooms, 
library with good furniture, internet facility, vocational skill education, guidance and career 
counselling, fully equipped integrated science lab/physics lab/chemistry lab/biology lab, 
playground with well -equipped sports facilities, school innovation council , youth and eco 
club for mission life, Building as Learning Aid (BaLa) features and jaadui pitara for primary 
school children, 10 bagless days for students, child tracking software for tracking the children 
attendance, fully functioning handwashing facilit y and toilets, green school features etc.  The 
State/UT wise details of 13,092 PM SHRI schools are at Annexure -I. 
 As informed by t he Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 728 Eklavya Model Residential 
schools have been approved to be set up across the country. Most of these schools are in far 
flung areas, hilly areas and North East Region also. The details of EMRSs is at Annexure-II.  
 Under Skill Education component of Samagra Shiksha Scheme, financial assistance is 
provided to the States and UTs for giving skill exposure to students of Grades VI to VIII and 
introduction of National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)  aligned skill courses from 
Grades IX to XII. The scheme is implemented across all States and UTs, including tribal and 
aspirational regions, based on the proposals received from the respective State/UT 
Governments and approved under the Project Approval Board (PAB).  Till 2025-26, 31,477 
schools have been approved under the scheme and 39,49,875 students have been  enrolled in 
different skill courses. 
The Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship has implemented a project to 
strengthen vocational education infrastructure and promote skill -based learning among 
students by establishing 1,200 Vocational Skill Labs. These labs are set up across 600 schools 
comprising 400 Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) and 200 Eklavya Model Residential 
Schools (EMRSs). Each of the selected schools is equipped with two dedicated skill labs. 
(c): Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing (DIKSHA) is the one nation, one digital 
education infrastructure. All states/UTs have been onboarded in DIKSHA. This digital 
infrastructure is artificial intelligence based and is highly scalable. This infrastructure is also 
being utilize d for creating Energized Textbooks (ETBs) and presently 7 754 ETBs are 
published and a total of 3.67 lakh e-contents are available on DIKSHA. 
 Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM ) hosts 
content curated by premier institutions and is available free of cost with the approach of 
“Anyone, Anywhere, Anytime” Learning.  There have been more than 20,000 deliveries of 
courses on the platform, with cumulative enrolments exceeding 6 crores since its inception. 
The State/UT-wise distribution of SWAYAM Enrolments is at Annexure-III. 
 Under the PM eVIDYA initiative, the existing 12 DTH Channels of SWAYAM 
PRABHA for School Education have been expanded to 200 PM eVIDYA DTH TV channels 
to provide curriculum -based educational content, particularly fo r learners who do not have 
access to internet connectivity. A total of 1,12,822 video contents, equivalent to 32,763 hours 
of telecast  has been produced by States/UTs and Autonomous Bodies  in 45 languages, 
thereby facilitating equitable and inclusive access to quality education. 

 
 
 Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK ) is an  integrated and shared ‘seeing’ for data -based 
decision making. So far, VSK has been established in 35 States and UTs  and centrally at the 
NCERT, CBSE and NIOS. 
 ICT and Digital Initiatives component of Samagra Shiksha covers Government 
Schools having classes VI to XII. Under this component financial assistance is provided for 
establishing ICT Labs and Smart Classrooms in schools. The non - recurring/ recurring grant 
under ‘ICT and Digital Initiatives’ is available to the States and UTs  as per norms of the 
scheme. The State/UT wise  details of ICT labs and Smart Classrooms functional since 
inception is at Annexure-IV. 
 As informed by the State of Rajasthan, the  Government schools  in the  districts of 
Chittorgarh, Udaipur and Pratapgarh  utilize DIKSHA resources aligned with the Rajasthan 
State curriculum. Teachers participate in online professional development programmes 
through the DIKSHA LMS Portal, including NIS HTHA and other departmental training 
programmes. Students access QR -coded textbook resources, digital learning materials, 
student courses, assessments, and self -learning modules available on DIKSHA . Also, 
curriculum-based educational content is disseminated through the five PM eVIDYA DTH TV 
Channels dedicated to Rajasthan . ICT Laboratories and Smart Classrooms have been 
established in several Government secondary and senior secondary schools. 
 Since inception 119, 239 and 94 ICT labs have been approved for the districts of 
Chittorgarh, Udaipur and Pratapgarh respectively and 453, 772 and 282 Smart classrooms 
have been approved in the districts of Chittorgarh, Udaipur and Pratapgarh respectively. 
(d): The Department of School Education &  Literacy, Ministry of Education has aligned 
existing schemes such as Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI, Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman 
(PM POSHAN), Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society ( ULLAS) etc. with the 
recommendation of NEP 2020 and budgeta ry allocations to the States/UTs are made under 
these schemes to incorporate the recommendations of NEP 2020.  
 The State/UT wise details of fund released under the scheme of Samagra Shiksha, PM 
SHRI, PM POSHAN and ULLAS during FY 2025-26 is at Annexure-V. 
(e): To create awareness and discuss innovative ideas for NEP implementation, a series of 
workshops / consultation-cum-review meetings have been held with States/UTs, Educational 
Institutions, other stakeholders from time to time. Implementation of NEP 20 20 was 
discussed in National Education Ministers' Conference held in June 2022; National 
Conference of Chief Secretaries held in June 2022, December 2023 and December 2025; 7th 
and 9 th Governing Council Meeting of NITI Aayog held in August 2022  and July 20 24 
respectively; Akhil Bharatiya Shiksha Samagam 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 . There has been 
wide publicity with a positive and encouraging response from stakeholders on NEP 2020. 
 Further, I mplementation of National Education Policy ( NEP) 2020 is a continuous 
process and Centre and State work collaboratively to ensure comprehensive and progressive 
enhancement of overall quality and growth within the education sector. 
The Government implements multipronged strategy to enhance the Gross Enrolment 
Ratio (GER).  Under Samagra Shiksha, financial assistance is provided to States and UTs , 
including the State of Karnataka,  for undertaking various activities for Universalization of 

 
 
School Education including opening/strengthening of new schools upto senior secondary 
level, construction of school buildings & additional classrooms, setting up, up -gradation and 
running of Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas, setting up of Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose 
Avasiya Vidyalayas, construction of hostels for PVTGs under Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi 
Nyaya Maha Abhiyan  (PM JANMAN), construction of hostels under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya 
Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (D A-JGUA) for unsaturated ST population, free uniforms to eligible 
children and free text books at elementary level, transport allowance and undertaking 
enrolment & retention drives, support for out of schools children to complete their education 
through NIOS/SIOS.  
 
Under the student -oriented component for the children with special needs, financial 
assistance is provided for identification and assessment of children with special needs, aids 
and appliances, braille kits and books, appropriate teaching learnin g material and stipend to 
girl students with disability etc. 
 
Also, under Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (P M POSHAN) Scheme, one hot 
cooked meal is provided to all children studying in Government and Government -aided 
schools at elementary level, including Balvatika.

STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF LOK SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS 
(a) TO (d) OF THE LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 150 FOR 29TH JULY, 2026 
REGARDING “NETWORK RELATED PROBLEMS IN BAHRAICH” ASKED BY DR. 
ANAND KUMAR.  
 
(a)  Girijapuri Colony SO has been relocated, at a distance of around 8 kms, as Matehi Chafaria 
SO in Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, from 17.05.2024, covering the same geographical area. It was 
relocated due to network connectivity issues arising out of the area being surrounded by forests on 
all sides.  
 
(b)  Girijapuri locality, under Block & Tehsil-Mihinpurwa, District-Bahraich, is presently 
covered with mobile services of BSNL. Out of 1390 villages in Bahraich, 1389 villages are having 
mobile coverage and 1383 villages are having 4G connectivity.  
 
In Bahraich District, there are 25 Departmental Post Offices and 268 Branch Post Offices to 
provide uninterrupted postal, banking, insurance and citizen centric services to the residents of the 
area. Girijapuri Colony area, under Bahraich District, is being served by Saryu Nahar Colony Branch 
Post Office established on 17.05.2024 through relocation. 
 
(c)  The Department has deployed mobile device along with SIM based network connectivity in 
Saryu Nahar Colony BO established within the same locality to provide uninterrupted postal services 
to the residents of Girijapuri Colony area. 
 
(d)  For providing high bandwidth capacity internet/broadband connectivity and mobile services 
to remote and rural villages and islands in the country, including Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, that 
currently lack coverage, a number of steps and projects have been taken up with funding from Digital 
Bharat Nidhi (DBN), Department of Telecommunications (DoT). 
 Under BharatNet programme, broadband connectivity is provisioned in a phased manner to

Dedicated freight corridor: 
 
Ministry of Railways has taken construction of two Dedicated Freight 
Corridors (DFC) viz. Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) from 
Ludhiana to Sonnagar (1337 Km) and the Western Dedicated Freight 
Corridor (WDFC) from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Terminal (JNPT) to Dadri 
(1506 Km). 
 
The work on EDFC & WDFC has been completed and commissioned.On an 
average more than 443 trains are operated per day on DFCs. The fully 
commissioned sections of the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight 
Corridors (EDFC & WDFC) have demonstrated robust operational 
performance. Freight volumes have steadily increased, with higher average 
speeds, faster turnarounds, and enhanced reliability. The corridors are 
witnessing consistent growth in container, coal, and bulk cargo movement, 
contributing significantly to capacity augmentation in freight 
transportation. 

 
Page 12 of 12 
 
DFC has contributed to creating additional paths on the conventional 
network by diverting freight traffic to EDFC and WDFC. As a result, 
Railways have been able to run additional goods and coaching services 
over its network.  The DFCs have enabled faster transit times, higher 
throughput, and double-stack container operations (especially on the 
Western DFC). These improvements have contributed to lowering overall 
logistics costs, improving supply chain efficiency, and enhancing 
competitiveness of Indian industries. 
 
A new Dedicated Freight Corridor connecting Dankuni in East to Surat in 
West, has been announced in the Union Budget 2026. The work of 
preparation/ updation of Detailed Project Report (DPR) for this corridor has 
been taken up.

Statement referred to in reply of parts (a) to (f) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 152 
to be answered on 29.07.2026 regarding Rooftop Solar Installations under PM-SGMBY 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has been implementing the 
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) since February 2024, aiming to install 
rooftop solar (RTS) systems in one crore residential households across the country by FY 
2026–27 with a total financial outlay of Rs. 75,021 crores. 
 
The PMSG: MBY is a demand-driven scheme wherein all residential consumers in the country, 
including those in the state of Chhattisgarh, having a grid-connected electricity connection with 
the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits of the scheme, for installa tion of RTS systems by 
applying on the National Portal (www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in) of the scheme. 
 
Under the scheme, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 40,07,355 RTS systems have 
been installed, benefitting 48,21,986 households across the country as on 24.07.2026. The RTS 
capacity-wise total number of households solarised under the PM-SGMBY, is given below:

(e) & (f):  The pace of implementation of the scheme is increasing. During the initial phase, it 
took a few months to cover RTS installations for one lakh households, and now, for the same 
coverage, it takes around 7 days. To further ensure timely achievement of the o verall RTS 
installations target, expedite technical feasibility approvals and net -metering installations 
across the country, including in the state of Chhattisgarh, the Ministry has taken the following 
measures: 
• Online process from application to subsidy disbursement directly into the residential 
consumer's bank account through the National Portal.  
• Availability of collateral -free loan from nationalized banks at a concessional 
interest rate of repo-rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for the present, with a 
tenure of 10 years.  
• Simplified the regulatory approval process by waiving the technical feasibility 
requirement and introducing auto load enhancement up to 10 kW.  
• The net metering agreement has been incorporated into the application on the 
National Portal, eliminating the need for a separate physical agreement.  

• Simplified process for registration of vendors to ensure sufficient and qualified 
vendors are available.  
• Capacity-building and training programs are being conducted to create skilled 
manpower.  
• Creating awareness about the scheme through outreach and awareness programs 
such as print advertising in leading newspapers, TV commercial campaigns, Radio 
campaigns across FM stations, including regional channels, etc., across the country. 
• Regular monitoring of the scheme's progress at different levels, including with 
states/DISCOMs. 
• Conducting regional review meetings from time to time. 
• Established grievance redressal mechanism for timely resolution of grievances. A 
Call Centre with telephone number 15555 is operational in 12 languages. 
 
Further, MNRE and REC Ltd., as the National Programme Implementing Agency (NPIA), for 
PMSG: MBY, work in close coordination with all the DISCOMs, for effective implementation 
of the scheme.

Further, development / redevelopment / upgradation / modernisation of 
stations on Indian Railways including provision of passenger amenities 
such as waiting hall, foot over bridge, lift, escalator, passenger information 
system, waiting room, parking, circu lating area, approach road etc., is a 

 
Page 20 of 23 
continuous and ongoing process and works in this regard are undertaken 
as per requirement, subject to inter -se priority and availability of funds. 
Development / redevelopment / upgradation / modernisation of a station is 
carried out based on category of station/condition/traffic handled etc.  
 
Amrit Bharat Station Scheme involves preparation of master plans and their 
implementation in phases to improve the stations of Indian Railways. The 
master planning, keeping in view the necessity of each station, includes: 
● Improvement of access to station and circulating areas 
● Integration of station with both sides of city 
● Improvement of station building 
● Improvement of waiting halls, toilets, sitting arrangement, water 
booths  
● Provision of wider foot over bridge/subway to commensurate with 
passenger traffic 
● Provision of lifts/escalators/ramps 
● Improvement of platform surface/ provision of platform shelter 
● Provision of kiosks for local products through schemes like ‘One 
Station One Product’ 
● Parking development 
● Amenities for Divyangjans 
● Better passenger information systems 
● Provision of air concourse, executive lounges, Multimodal integration, 
landscaping, etc. 
 
The scheme also envisages sustainable and environment friendly solutions 
etc. as per necessity, phasing and feasibility and creation of city centre at 
the station in the long term.  Development of stations into city centres 
envisages enhanced economic activities at and around the stations apart 

 
Page 21 of 23 
from improved travel experience. Furthe r, development/upgradation of 
railway stations has a positive impact on tourism in the surrounding areas. 
 
Development / Upgradation of railway stations is a complex in nature 
involving safety of passengers & trains and requires various statutory 
clearances such as tree cutting, heritage, fire clearance, airport clearance 
etc. These stations are in operation since long, so brownfield work 
challenges are being faced, such as shifting of utilities (involving 
water/sewage lines, optical fibre cables, gas pipel ines, power/signal 
cables, etc.), infringements, operation of trains without hindering 
passenger movement, speed restrictions due to works carried out in close 
proximity of the tracks and near to high voltage power lines, etc. and these 
factors affect the progress of work and completion time.  
 
Indian Railways is committed to make its railway stations accessible for 
Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjans) and passengers with reduced 
mobility as part of “Sugamya Bharat Mission” or ‘Accessible India 
Campaign’ of Government of India. In compliance of the Rights of Persons 
with Disabilities Act, 2016, “Guidelines on accessibility of Indian Railway 
stations and facilities at stations for differently abled persons 
(Divyangjans) and passengers with reduced mobility ” have been circulated 
and notified in the Gazette of India. The guidelines include provisions of 
facilities for Divyangjans and passengers with reduced mobility such as 
entrance ramps, accessible parking, low height ticket counters/help 
booths, toilets, d rinking water booths, subways/foot over bridges with 
ramps/lifts, standard signages including Braille signages and tactile 
pathways for visual impairment etc. 
 
Escalators and lifts at railway stations are provided as per extant policy 
depending upon techno -economic feasibility and inter -se priority of the 

 
Page 22 of 23 
stations. So far, 1,794 escalators at 443 railway stations and 2,159 lifts at 
791 railway stations have been provided over Indian Railways.  
 
Development / upgradation / modernisation of stations including  under 
Amrit Bharat Station Scheme is generally funded under Plan Head -53 
‘Customer Amenities’. The details of allocation and expenditure under Plan 
Head-53 are maintained Zonal Railway -wise and not station -wise or state -
wise. 
 
Rajasthan is covered under t he jurisdiction of five railway zones, namely,

Jharkhand is covered under the jurisdiction of three railway zones, namely,

Madhya Pradesh is covered under the jurisdiction of seven railway zones,

Odisha is covered under the jurisdiction of three railway zones, nam ely,

STATEMENT TO BE LAID ON THE TABLE OF LOK SABHA IN RESPECT OF PARTS 
(a) TO (e) OF THE LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 154 FOR 29TH JULY, 2026 
REGARDING “BHARATNET PROGRAMME AND NATIONAL BROADBAND MISSION 
2.0” ASKED BY SHRI BHOJRAJ NAG & SHRI MANOJ TIWARI. 
 
(a), (d) & (e) Mobile tower installation schemes, submarine optical fibre cable projects and the 
Amended BharatNet Programme have been funded from Digital Bharat Nidhi for universal and 
meaningful broadband connectivity with a view to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat and ensure that 
the benefits of Digital India reach the rural and remote areas across the country, including in the State 
of Odisha and the Keonjhar Lok Sabha constituency.  
  
 Under the Amended BharatNet Programme, provision has been made for optical fibre 
connectivity to approximately 2.65 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) and approximately 3.8 lakh non-
GP villages on demand basis, across the country. The programme also has provision for incentive 
for 1.50 crore rural fibre connections distributed across the country. 
The programme is implemented in two models across the country:  
 
(i) BSNL-led model, which covers 1,67,727 GPs in 21 States and 5 Union territories (UTs); 
and  
(ii) State-led model, which covers 97,336 GPs in 7 States.  
 
 BSNL, as the Project Management Agency, has signed agreements with Project 
Implementing Agencies for implementation of the programme for 18 packages covering 21 States 
and 5 UTs. As of June 2026, a total 43,908 kilometre of optical fibre cable has been laid and 13,494 
GPs have been upgraded under the programme. Details are at Annexure I.  
  
 The National Broadband Mission 2.0 was launched by the Government on 17.1.2025 and has 
been effective since 1.4.2025. The Mission aims to fast-track rapid expansion of digital 
communications infrastructure, bridge the digital and socio-economic divide and ensure high-speed 
broadband and meaningful connectivity for all, across the country.   
During the last one year, the progress under the main components of the Mission is as follows: 
 
(i) The national average fixed broadband download speed has reached 60.85 Mbps as on 
31.3.2026. 
(ii) The number of rural internet subscribers per 100 population has increased from 45.03 to 
48.31 during 2025-26. 
(iii) Broadband connectivity to anchor institutions (schools, Primary Health Centres, 
Anganwadis and Panchayat offices) has reached 21,82,312 connections as on 31.3.2026. 
(iv) The national average for the time taken to dispose right of way applications has reduced 
from 80.63 days in the financial year (FY) 2024-25 to 35.62 days in FY2025-26. 
(v) The use of sustainable energy in mobile towers has increased from 8% to 11.44% during 
FY2025-26. 
(vi) At present, all 36 States and UTs are live on the centralised portal for right of way 
applications, marking nationwide adoption of a uniform digital platform for the processing 
of and grant of permissions in response to such applications. 
 
(b) & (c) The Government has approved the BharatNet Project including the Amended 
BharatNet Programme and 12 mobile tower installation schemes, including the 4G Saturation Project 
and schemes for border areas, Aspirational Districts, Left Wing Extremism areas and island 
territories, with a view to strengthen high-speed broadband infrastructure and improve digital 
connectivity for delivery of telecom services in rural, remote, forested and uncovered areas across 
the country.

7. All locomotives are equipped with Vigilance Control Devices (VCD) to 
improve alertness of Loco Pilots. 
8. Retro-reflective sigma boards are provided on the mast which is 
located two OHE masts prior to the signals in electrified territories to 
alert the crew about the signal ahead when visibility is low due to 
foggy weather. 
9.  A GPS based Fog Safety Device (FSD) is provided to loco pilots in fog 
affected areas which enables loco pilots to know the distance of the 
approaching landmarks like signals, level crossing gates, etc. 
10. Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile 
Strength (UTS) rails, Prestressed Concrete Sleeper (PSC) Normal/Wide 
base sleepers with elastic fastening, fan shaped layout turnout on PSC 
sleepers, Steel Channel/H-beam Sleepers on girder bridges is used 
while carrying out primary track renewals. 
11. Mechanisation of track laying activity through use of track machines 
like PQRS, TRT , T-28 etc. to reduce human errors. 
12. Maximizing supply of 130m/260m long rail panels for increasing 
progress of rail renewal and avoiding welding of joints, thereby 
improving safety. 
13. Ultrasonic Flaw Detection (USFD) testing of rails to detect flaws and 
timely removal of defective rails. 
14. Laying of longer rails, minimizing the use of Alumino Thermic Welding 
and adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e., Flash Butt 
Welding.

15. Monitoring of track geometry by OMS (Oscillation Monitoring System) 
and TRC (Track Recording Cars). 
16. Patrolling of railway tracks to look out for weld/rail fractures. 
17. The use of Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossing in turnout 
renewal   works.

(a) to (e):  India’s electronics sector has witnessed a remarkable transformation in recent 
years, driven by a series of Government initiatives and industry reforms. The country is 
steadily emerging as a global hub for electronics system design and manufac turing. 
Electronics Development Fund (EDF) was one of these initiatives of Government of India, to 
promote market driven innovation in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM). 
 
The EDF was set up as a Fund of Funds, designed to invest in professionally managed 
Daughter Funds which are SEBI registered venture funds. These Daughter Funds provided 
risk capital to startups and companies developing new technologies in the area of ESDM and 
Information Technology (IT).  By doing so, the EDF played a crucial role in building a self -
sustaining electronics ecosystem that encourages innovation, product design, and intellectual 
property creation within the country. 
 
The selection of startups for investments by the Daughter Funds of EDF were made on the 
basis of various parameters which included their innovation capability, indigenous 
technology development, and IP creation potential, technical capability of founding t eam as 
well as a scalable and commercially viable business model. 
 
Canbank Venture Capital Funds Ltd. (CVCFL) is the Fund Manager and Ministry of 
Electronics and Information Technology is the anchor investor of EDF. As on 30.06.2026, 
EDF has invested Rs. 257.77 crore in eight Daughter Funds, which in turn have made

STATEMENT 
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (e) of the Lok Sabha Starred Question No. 159 
to be answered on 29.07.2026 regarding “Vacant Posts in IREDA”  
 
(a): Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) , being a Central Public Sector 
Enterprise (CPSE), follows the employee categorization prescribed under the Department of 
Public Enterprises (DPE) guidelines. Accordingly, employees are broadly classified as Executives 
(E-0 to E-9 level), Non-Unionised Supervisors (S-1 and S-2 level) and Non-Executives (NE-1 to 
NE-7 (Selection Grade (SG)) level). Further, in IREDA, E -1 to E -9 level are classified under 
Group-A, E-0 level is classified under Group-B, NE-3 to NE-7 (Selection Grade) and S -1to S-2 
level are classified under Group-C, NE-1 & NE-2 level are classified under Group-D. The group-
wise details of sanctioned, filled and vacant posts under Groups A, B, C, and D in IREDA  are 
given at Annexure-I. 
 
(b): In compliance with Deptt. of Personnel and Training ( DoPT) Office Memorandum (OM) 
No.36012/2/96-Estt.(Res) dated 02.07.1997, IREDA is maintaining post-based reservation rosters. 
Also, the reservation rosters are maintained for direct recruitment on all India basis - by open 
competition (SCs – 15%, STs – 7.5%) and otherwise than by open competition (SCs – 16.66%, 
STs – 7.5%). The group-wise details of the currently filled posts, vacant and backlog posts as per 
the reservation norms prescribed for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) are given 
at Annexure-II. 
 
(c): The group-wise details of the sanctioned posts, employees working in the agency, reserved 
posts and filled posts are given at Annexure-III.

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether any Central financial assistance has been extended to Telangana for human-animal 
conflicts mitigation during the last three years and the current year, if so, the details thereof, year-

(b) whether the Government has assessed rising human–animal conflict incidents in Telangana, if

monitoring mechanism; 
(c) whether any steps have been taken under Centrally Sponsored Schemes to support Telangana

(d) whether the Government provides financial assistance for compensation to victims of wildlife

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (e) OF THE LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *16 REGARDING ‘HUMAN-ANIMAL CONFLICT IN TELANGANA’ BY SHRI 
SURESH KUMAR SHETKAR FOR REPLY ON 20.07.2026 
 
 
(a): The management of wildlife including mitigation of human-animal conflicts is primarily the 
responsibility of the concerned State Government/Union Territory Administration. The State 
Government/UT Administration are the first responders to any conflict situation and they maintain the 
details of the conflict along with the species involved. Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 
Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats an amount of Rs. 323.32 lakhs, Rs. 291.68 lakhs, Rs. 
302.34 lakhs and Rs. 208.67 lakhs have been released to the State of Telangana during the financial 
years 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26 & 2026-27 respectively for inter alia management of Human wildlife 
conflict.  
 
(b) to (e): Under the said scheme, activities supported include procurement of early warning systems, 
construction and erection of physical barriers such as solar powered electric fencing, bio-fencing, 
trenches, boundary walls etc. to prevent depredation by wild animals which inter alia includes cattle 
lifting, crop damage, loss of life and property. Rapid Response Teams with community stewards are also 
deployed to mitigate Human-Wildlife Conflict.  
 
The Government of India has assessed the status of human wildlife conflict across the country including 
Telangana especially in context of flagship species such as tigers and elephants wherein during the last 
decade no human deaths due to elephants and only 3 human deaths due to tiger attacks were reported by 
the State of Telangana. Further, granular data in respect of compensation and affected districts is collated 
at level of the State.  
 
Important steps taken by the Government to manage human-wildlife conflicts include the following: 
 
i. Section 11 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 adequately empowers the State Chief Wild 
Life Wardens to manage wildlife in conflict situations. 
 
ii. The Ministry has issued advisories and guidelines to manage human-wildlife negative 
interactions through interdepartmental coordinated actions besides adherence to SOPs in this 
regard. Use of technological aids are used to strengthen these interventions.  
 
iii. The Ministry has established a Centre of Excellence for Human–Wildlife Conflict Management 
at the Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History (SACON), WII–South India Centre, 
Coimbatore, to strengthen the scientific and institutional framework for managing human–
wildlife conflict.  
 
 
Further, the Ministry has enhanced the amount of ex-gratia relief in case of death or permanent 
incapacitation due to wild animal attacks in December 2023 from Rs. 5 lakhs to 10 lakhs under these 
Schemes as per the directions in this regard which is supplemented through relevant schemes of the State

REGARDING “SHRINKING OR VANISHING LAKES” 
(a) to (d)  Water being a state subject, protection , conservation and 
management of wetlands, including lakes, is underta ken by the respective 
State Governments/UT Administrations in accordance with the applicable 
statutory provisions. The Central Government supple ments the measures and 
efforts being taken up by the State Governments/UT Administrations. Ministry 
of Jal Shakti has conducted 1st Census of Water Bodies in 33 States/UTs under 
the Centrally Sponsored Scheme “Irrigation Census” with 100% Central 
Assistance (reference year 2017-18). The objective of the Census is to develop 
a national database for all water bodies by collect ing information on all 
important aspects of the subject including their si ze, condition, status of 
encroachment, use, storage capacity, status of filling up of storage etc.  
While the Central and State Governments take all po ssible steps for the 
conservation and management of wetlands (includes l akes), developmental 
activities and anthropogenic pressures do impact wetlands.  
The assessments in the CAG report are based on an i nventory of water 
bodies prepared by the Department of Environment & Remote Sensing, Jammu 
& Kashmir using LISS-III satellite imagery having a n approximate spatial 
resolution of 23 meters. Such datasets provide prel iminary technical 
information for administrators and researchers and are indicative in nature. 
They do not constitute conclusive evidence of perma nent disappearance, 
shrinkage, encroachment or unlawful conversion of w etlands. Remote sensing 
data indicates changes in water spread or land cove r of the wetland but 
cannot independently establish substantial changes.  Such conclusions require 
correlation with land records, cadastral maps, noti fied wetland boundaries, 
field inspections and records maintained by the com petent custodial and 
enforcement authorities. Subsequently, J&K Governme nt has undertaken a 
comprehensive revision and expansion of the invento ry using very-high-

3 
 
resolution satellite imagery, grid-based analysis, field verification and 
jurisdictional refinement. As a result, the invento ry has been updated to 1,793 
wetlands and water bodies. The revised inventory of  water bodies is shown at 
Annexure-I. 
Further, the Government has taken various measures for conservation and 
management of wetlands, including lakes. These include policy, regulatory and 
programme interventions by the Central Government a s well as conservation 
and management measures undertaken by the concerned  State 
Governments/UTs. The major initiatives are as follows: 
i. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Cha nge (MoEF&CC) has 
notified the Wetlands (Conservation & Management) R ules, 2017 under 
the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 which, inter -alia, prohibit 
conversion for non-wetland uses including encroachm ent of any kind, 
solid waste dumping, discharge of untreated wastes and effluents from 
industries, cities, towns, villages and other human  settlements and any 
construction of a permanent nature. Also, the State /UT Wetlands 
Authorities have been constituted as the nodal authorities responsible for 
conservation and management of wetlands.  
ii. MoEF&CC is currently implementing a Centrally Spons ored Scheme 
namely, the ‘National Plan for Conservation of Aqua tic Eco-systems 
(NPCA)’ for conservation and management of wetlands  in the country on 
cost sharing basis between Central Government and r espective State 
Governments. The scheme covers various activities s uch as interception, 
diversion and treatment of wastewater, shoreline pr otection, lake front 
development, in-situ cleaning i.e., desilting & dew eeding, storm water 
management, bioremediation, catchment area treatmen t, lake 
beautification, survey & demarcation, bio-fencing, fisheries development, 
weed control, biodiversity conservation, education and awareness 
creation, community participation, etc. Under the N PCA scheme, 
MoEF&CC has provided financial assistance of about Rs. 1170 crores as 

4 
 
Central share to the States/UTs for about 172 wetla nds across the 
country. 
iii. The other steps taken by MoEF&CC for conservation a nd management of 
wetlands across the country include, implementation  of Ramsar 
Convention on wetlands, Mission Sahbhagita and Save  Wetlands 
Campaign for peoples and stakeholders’ participatio n in the wetlands 
conservation and management, Amrit Dharohar initiat ive to promote 
unique conservation values of Ramsar sites. 
iv. “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” (JSJB) initiative was l aunched in Surat, 
Gujarat on 6 September 2024. In June 2025, JSJB 2.0  was launched. The 
implementation cycle for JSJB 2.0 commenced on 1 Ju ne 2025 and 
concluded on 31 May 2026. The initiative leverages community funds, 
individual donations, Corporate Social Responsibili ty Funds and others 
for construction of low-cost structures like borewe lls, recharge shafts, 
recharge pits, using locally available material, to  harvest rainwater, to 
boost ground water level and provide local tailor-m ade solution to water 
issues. The initiative also emphasizes convergent f inancing from various 
schemes of the Central, State and local bodies like  Viksit Bharat - 
Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Atal 
Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation ( AMRUT), Per Drop 
More Crop, Repair, Renovation and Restoration Compo nents under the 
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY), Compe nsatory 
Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authorit y (CAMPA) and 
Finance Commission grants. 
v. State wise details of the remedial measures as repo rted by the State 
Governments of J&K, Goa, Karnataka and Telangana are at Annexure-II.

(b) whether oil marketing companies have been directed to

stations and on customer receipts, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether adequate consultation with stakeholders has been done 
regarding E20 fuel programme and if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has noticed that despite the fuels being 
diluted by ethanol, the  end price to consumers is not reduced and if 
so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether any financial incentives ar e given to vehicle owners for 
transforming from conventional fuels to biofuels and if so, the details 
thereof?

(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO ( e) OF THE 
LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. * 164 FOR ANSWER ON 30th 
JULY, 2026 ASKED BY SHRI M K RAGHAVAN  REGARDING IMPACT OF 
E20 FUEL. 
 
(a) & (c) Government in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has 
introduced the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme through a 
phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving 
NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, Oil Marketing Companies 
(OMCs), Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Society of 
Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), Indian Institute of Petroleum 
(IIP) and other technical institutions. 
Ethanol is not a new fuel. It has been used globally for over a century, 
with co untries such as Brazil operating higher ethanol blends for 
decades. In India, the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme 
commenced with a pilot in 2001, E5 was introduced in 2006, and 
although blending remained around 1.53% in 2013 -14, it has since 
been increased progressively in a calibrated manner after creating the 
necessary production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory 
framework.  
As seen from the table, the progression has been gradual: 
Ethanol Supply Year Average Blending (%) 
2013-14 ~1.53 
2020-21 ~8.1 
2021-22 ~10 
2022-23 ~12 
2023-24 ~14.6 
2024-25 ~19.2 
2025-26 (Nov-June) 20 

  
The E20 programme has been developed through an extensive 
consultative and phased implementation process. Automobile 
manufacturers, component manufacturers, SIAM, ARAI, vehicle testing 
agencies, Oil Marketing Companies, ethanol producers, sugar and 
grain industries and other stakeholders were associated at every 
stage of policy formulation and implementation. 
  
The transition to E20 was undertaken only after s uccessful validation 
of fuel systems, engine durability, drivability, material compatibility, 
emissions performance and consumer acceptance. 
  
Laboratory studies and field trials conducted by ARAI, SIAM, Indian Oil 
Corporation Limited (IOCL), IIP and autom obile manufacturers are as 
per respective certification requirements and customised test 
protocols developed along with Original Equipment Manufacturers 
(OEMs). The exhaust emissions meet the respective norms (i.e. BS VI 
vehicles meet the BSVI emission nor ms when tested with E20). The 
test for engine durability has not shown any failure due to E20. Tests 
covering parameters such as engine drivability, startability, corrosion 
resistance and material compatibility have confirmed that E20 is safe 
for use under prescribed standards.  
E20 offers a higher -octane rating, superior anti -knock characteristics, 
cleaner combustion and smoother engine performance. E20 improves 
acceleration and ride quality while reducing carbon emissions. These 
studies also established t hat legacy vehicles do not exhibit variation 
in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20.  
These laboratory studies, field validation and real -world operating 
experience have not established adverse impact on vehicle 
performance due to E20 fuel.  
This is evident from the fact that E15+ blended petrol has been in 
widespread use for over three -and-a-half years and E19 -E20 fuel for 
over two-and-a-half years.  

More than 20 crore two -wheelers and over 3 crore petrol cars have 
been operating on these blen ds without any verified evidence of 
widespread engine failure or vehicle breakdown attributable to ethanol 
blending. 
Manufacturer service data have also confirmed that there is no 
abnormal corrosion, wear or reduction in vehicle life due to E20 fuel, 
and a utomobile manufacturers continue to honour warranty 
obligations for vehicles using specification-compliant E20 fuel. 
A leading automobile manufacturer has reported servicing 2.84 crore 
vehicles during FY 2025 –26, including about 1.5 crore legacy vehicles, 
without finding any E20 -linked engine damage, abnormal corrosion or 
reduction in component life. A leading two -wheeler manufacturer has 
similarly reported no higher incidence of damage in E20 -operated 
vehicles. 
With regard to mileage, studies by Government agencies and 
automobile manufacturers indicate that reduction in fuel efficiency in 
certain E10-designed vehicles is limited to about 2 -6%. However, the 
same is influenced by several factors, including driving conditions, 
driving habits and vehicle maintenance.   
The Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme has resulted in foreign 
exchange savings of about ₹1.98 lakh crore, substitution of nearly 317 
lakh metric tonnes of crude oil, reduction of around 952 lakh metric 
tonnes of CO ₂ emissions and additional income of over ₹1.66 lakh 
crore for farmers. 
(b) Public Sector OMCs have informed that currently normal petrol sold 
at their retail outlets across the country is E20.  Since E0 or E10 petrol 
is not marketed at retail o utlets, separate display of lower ethanol 
blends or printing of ethanol percentage on customer receipts has not 
been considered necessary.  
However, wherever E85 fuel is sold, the dispensing units are 
prominently labelled, as it is intended exclusively for  use in Flex Fuel 
Vehicles (FFVs). 
(d) India is the world's third -largest importer of crude oil, meeting 
nearly 85 per cent of its crude oil requirement through imports.   The 

retail selling price of E20 petrol is market -determined, and Public 
Sector OMCs d etermine petrol prices after considering international 
crude oil prices, exchange rates, freight, taxes, ethanol procurement 
costs and other operational expenses. For e.g. during February -March, 
2026, the retail selling price of petrol remained below the m arket 
determined level, resulting in an under -recovery of approximately 
Rs.21,300 crore for public sector OMCs on account of petrol. 
During the recent West Asian crisis, despite sharp increases in global 
crude prices, India was able to shield consumers thr ough calibrated 
Government interventions, diversified sourcing and the increasing 
contribution of domestically produced biofuels. Since February 2026, 
even though global crude prices rose by around 70 –80%, domestic fuel 
prices increased only by about 7–8%.  
During the peak of West Asia crisis, the market price of petrol could 
have been around Rs.125 per litre, however Indian consumers 
continued to pay only Rs.94.77 per litre (ex -Delhi) also because OMCs 
could procure ethanol at ~Rs.70/litre. By replacing a part of imported 
petrol with domestically produced ethanol, India has reduced its 
exposure to international crude oil price volatility and exchange -rate 
fluctuations. 
This demonstrates that ethanol blending is a strategic investment in 
energy security, pri ce stability, farmer welfare and foreign exchange 
savings, rather than a revenue-generating exercise for OMCs.  
(e) E85 fuel intended for use exclusively in Flex Fuel Vehicles (FFVs) is 
priced nearly ₹20 per litre lower than conventional blended petrol to 
ensure that the economic benefits of domestically produced ethanol 
are passed on to consumers.   However, this fuel can be used only for 
specially manufactured flex fuel vehicles.

Statement referred to in reply to parts (a) to (f) of Lok Sabha Starred Question No. *166 
answered on 30.07.2026 regarding “Supply Of Drinking Water Under JJM” asked by Dr. C M 
Ramesh & Smt. Jyotsna Charandas Mahant 
(a) & (b) Drinking water is a State subject and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, 
implementation, operation and maintenance of drinking water supply schemes, including those under 
the Jal Jeevan Mission, lies with th e respective State/UT Governments. The Government of India 
supports the States by providing technical and financial assistance. 
Since August 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States, is implementing Jal Jeevan 
Mission (JJM)-Har Ghar Jal to enable every rural household in the country to have assured potable 
water through tap connection at a service level of 55 litre per capita per day (LPCD), of prescribed 
quality (BIS:10500), on regular and long-term basis. The Union Cabinet has approved the extension 
of the JJM 2.0 by December, 2028 with an enhanced outlay and a restructured implementation 
framework focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water supply sector. 
As informed by State Govt. of Andhra Pradesh, out of 1539 habitations in Anak apalli district, 549 
habitations are covered with 55 LPCD (100% tap connection) and the remaining 990 habitations are 
scheduled to be covered by December 2028.  
(c) & (d) The planning, design, approval, implementation and day-to-day operation and maintenance 
(O&M) of piped water supply schemes, including the granular tracking of service delivery at the 
individual habitation level, are the responsibilities of the respective State/UT Governments  level 
only, not maintained by national level.  
As reported by the State Government of Chhattisgarh, 1,816 habitations in 33 districts covered under 
JJM but receiving less than fifty -five LPCD of drinking water supply since 2023.  Also, the State 
Government of Chhattisgarh has reported that Since 2023, 471 habitations across five districts have 
been receiving a supply of drinking water almost daily. The district-wise details submitted by the 
State is at Annexure-I. 
(e)  'Water' being a State subject, grievances / complaints, etc. inter alia  including inadequate or 
irregular drinking water supply under JJM are handled and disposed of at the State/UT Level.  
As reported by the State Government of Chhattisgarh, a total of 2,062 complaints regarding 
inadequate or irregular drinking water supply have been received since 2021–22. Of these, 1,941 
complaints have been resolved, while 121 complaints remain pending. The district-wise details 
submitted by the State is at Annexure-II.  
(f) To address persistent shortages in habitations despite coverage, Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 has shifted 
its core focus from infrastructure creation to sustainable service delivery and source security. The 
Government has mandated the preparation of District  Source Sustainability Action Plans (DSSAP) 
and adopted Aquifer-Based Planning for scientific groundwater recharge. A digital Decision Support 
System (DSS) has been deployed to monitor groundwater stress and predict declining yields. 
Furthermore, JJM 2.0 g uidelines strictly mandate the incorporation of alternate water sources in 
schemes for climate resilience, enforce Domestic Water Allocation Priority to safeguard drinking 
water during scarcity, and have established District Technical Units (DTUs) to trans ition from 
reactive repairs to preventive maintenance, ensuring uninterrupted water supply. Also, the States/UTs 
are taking up convergence activities utilizing funds where available under VB -GRAMG, Finance 
Commission Grants and District Mineral Funds.

Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives and key components of the National Urban Digital 
Mission (NUDM); 
(b) the progress made in implementation of the said Mission including 
the details of  States, Union Territories (UTs) and Urban Local 
Bodies (ULBs) covered thereunder across the country;

planning across the country?

THE MINISTER OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI MANOHAR LAL) 
 
(a) to (e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 
 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) to (e) OF THE LOK  
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 167 FOR ANSWER ON 3 0.07.2026 
REGARDING “NATIONAL URBAN DIGITAL MISSION” 
 
(a) to (e): At present, the National Urban Digital Mission (NUDM) is in 
the pilot phase only. The pilot implementation of the mission was 
launched in February, 2021 under which citizen centric urban digital 
infrastructure named as the Urban Platform for deliverY of Online 
Governance (UPYOG) is being developed. It comprises a set of e-
governance solutions usable by all ULBs for delivery of digital 
municipal services. It promotes the use of modern technologies in 
urban governance through the development of the UPYOG platform, 
which is an open- source, micro services -based and modular digital 
platform. This architecture enables interoperability, easy 
customization, and seamless integration with existing State and 
municipal systems.  The year -wise details of the financial allocation 
made for the implementation of the NUDM mission over the past three

LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 168 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 30.07.2026 
 
Development of Areas under Integrated Tribal Development Agency 
 
*168. Shri Tangella Uday Srinivas: 
 Shri Appalanaidu Kalisetti: 
 
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether the Union Government provides financial assistance for the development of Integrated 
Tribal Development Agency (ITDA) areas under various schemes, if so, the details thereof;  
(b) the funds allocated, released and utilised under such schemes during the last five years, State-wise, 
including Andhra Pradesh;  
(c) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment of the implementation and developmental 
outcomes of Central interventions in ITDA areas, if so, the key findings thereof;  
(d) the measures taken to strengthen infrastructure, education, healthcare, livelihoods and skill 
development in ITDA areas; and  
(e) whether any proposals from States/UTs relating to the creation, reorganisation or expansion of ITDA 
areas are pending with the Union Government, if so, the details and the present status, thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI JUAL ORAM) 
 
(a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (e) OF THE LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 168 FOR 30.07.2026 ASKED BY SHRI TANGELLA UDAY 
SRINIVAS AND SHRI APPALANAIDU KALISETTI, HON’BLE MEMBERS OF 
PARLIAMENT REGARDING DEVELOPMENT OF AREAS UNDER INTEGRATED TRIBAL 
DEVELOPMENT AGENCY 
 
(a) The Union Government supports development in ITDA/ITDP areas through various schemes and 
programmes of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and other sectoral Ministries. Assistance is provided, inter 
alia, under Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution, Pradhan Mantri Adi Adarsh Gram Yojana/State 
Tribal Sub-Plan support, PM-JANMAN, Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA), 
Eklavya Model Residential Schools, PM-JANMAN, scholarship schemes and tribal livelihood 
programmes. Grants under Article 275(1) are provided to bridge critical gaps in sectors such as education, 
health, agriculture and infrastructure. ITDAs/ITDPs function as important field-level institutions for 
convergence and implementation of these interventions.  
 
(b) Funds under the aforesaid schemes are generally allocated and released State-wise and scheme-wise, 
and not separately for each ITDA/ITDP area. Releases are made on the basis of approved proposals, 
availability of funds, utilisation certificates and compliance with scheme guidelines. The State-wise details 
of funds released during the last five years, including for Andhra Pradesh is at Annexure-I.  
 
(c) The implementation of Central interventions is reviewed regularly through meetings with States/UTs, 
field visits, scheme dashboards, physical and financial progress reports and outcome-based monitoring. 
Further, a National Conclave on Strengthening of ITDAs and ITDPs was organised on 3 June, 2026 to 
assess institutional capacity, convergence, planning and last-mile service delivery. The deliberations 
highlighted the need for stronger staffing, integrated planning, reliable data systems, community 
participation, improved convergence with line departments and greater functional and financial 
empowerment of ITDAs/ITDPs.  
 
(d) The Government is implementing a convergence-based approach in ITDA areas covering: 
(i) Roads, housing, drinking water, electricity, mobile connectivity and other basic infrastructure under 
DA-JGUA, PM-JANMAN and schemes of the concerned line Ministries; 
(ii) Establishment and strengthening of Eklavya Model Residential Schools, hostels, scholarships and other 
educational facilities; 
(iii) Healthcare interventions, including mobile medical units, health screening, maternal and child 
healthcare and the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission; 
(iv) Promotion of agriculture, horticulture, minor forest produce, Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, tribal 
enterprises and market linkages; and 
(v) Skill development, capacity building and livelihood training through convergence with the concerned 
Ministries and State Governments. 
 
(e) Creation, reorganization or expansion of ITDAs/ITDPs is considered on the basis of proposals 
received from the respective State Government/UT Administration and their conformity with the 
prescribed criteria.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

ANSWERED ON- 30TH JULY, 2026 
INFRASTRUCTURE FOR PEDESTRIANS 
  
169.  SHRI MANISH TEWARI : 
 SMT. SAJDA AHMED:  
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the recent judgement 
of the Supreme Court  recognising the right to walk on safe and 
demarcated footpaths as a fundamental right and  recommending a 
comprehensive legislative and policy framework for pedestrian 
rights, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) whether the Government proposes to enact a Central Law or 
amend the existing laws,  including the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 to 
mandate safe, accessible a nd encroachment free  footpaths and fix 
accountability of road owning authorities, if so, the details and the 
timeline thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Government has prescribed any standards or 
guidelines in this regard, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) the details of pedestrian-friendly measures implemented and the 
pedestrian infrastructure available on National Highways and other 
roads under the jurisdiction of the Central Government  including the 
total length of footpaths, the number of pedestrian crossings, f oot 
overbridges, underpasses and other pedestrian facilities, State/UT -
wise; 
 
(e) the details of the financial assistance provided under the 
existing Central schemes for the  development of pedestrian 
infrastructure during the last five years, State/UT -wise, along with 

the steps taken or proposed to improve pedestrian safety, promote 
universal accessibility and integrated transport planning; and 
 
(f) the details of pedestrian fatalities reported during the last five 
years along with the  measures taken or pro posed to reduce 
pedestrian fatalities across the country? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
 
(a) to (f) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
  
  

STATEMENT 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS  (a) TO ( f) OF THE 
LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 169 FOR ANSWER ON 30TH 
JULY, 20 26, ASKED BY SHRI MANISH TEWARI  AND SMT. SAJDA 
AHMED REGARDING INFRASTRUCTURE FOR PEDESTRIANS.  
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
(a) to (f)  Government in Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 
regulates the motor vehicles in accordance with the provision s of 
the Motor Vehicles Act and is responsible for development, 
operation and maintenance of National Highways (NHs). Sub-section 
(1A) of section 138 of the Motor Vehicles Act empowers the State 
Governments for making rules for the purposes of regulating 
activities and access of pedestrians to public places a nd National 
Highways. Further, sub -section (2) of s ection 138 provides further 
rule making powers to State Governments for prohibiting use of 
footpaths or pavements by motor vehicles and prevention of da nger, 
injury or annoyance to the public. 
  
As far as pedestrian infrastructure on National Highways is 
concerned, comprehensive guidelines have been published by 
Indian Roads Congress (IRC) viz. IRC:103 -2022 “Guidelines for 
Pedestrian Facilities”. Accordin gly, pedestrian infrastructure such 
as pedestrian underpasses, foot -over bridges, pedestrian crossings, 
footpaths, etc. are integral part of all National Highway projects 
wherever required based upon detailed planning and assessment, 
and are provided as pe r site requirements, either as part of 
improvement works or as stand -alone projects based on audit, to 
ensure seamless movement of the pedestrians. Further, regular 
safety audits are also conducted on all National Highways (NHs) at 
design, construction, an d pre -opening stage of National Highway 
projects as well as on existing NHs for ensuring seamless 
pedestrian infrastructure. IRC guidelines entail “universal 
accessibility” as one of the key principles with regard to pedestrian 
infrastructure. 
  
In accorda nce with the Rule 166 of Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 
1989, the design, construction and maintenance of roads other than 
National Highways shall be in accordance with the standards and 
specifications of the Indian Road Congress as may be applicable, or 

any other instructions or guidelines issued by the State Government 
from time to time. 
  
Government in Ministry of Road Transport & Highways provides 
budgetary support for National Highway projects which includes 
several components including pedestrian infras tructure, wherever 
required, based upon detailed planning and assessment. 
  
The details of fatalities on all roads and pedestrian fatalities 
reported on NHs during the last five years are annexed.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 17 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
DISBURSEMENT OF INCENTIVES UNDER PM-VBRY 
 
17. PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Prime Minister has announced the disbursement of 
incentives under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana 
(PM-VBRY) and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)the details of the incentives proposed for first-time employees and 
employers and the sectors covered under the Scheme; 
(c)the details of the estimated number of beneficiaries from 
Maharashtra and the assistance likely to be disbursed during the 
year 2026-27; 
(d)whether spe cial measures have been taken to promote formal 
employment and increase enrolment of eligible establishments 
and first-time employees in Mumbai and if so, the details thereof; 
(e)the details of the estimated number of establishments and workers 
in Mumbai expected to be covered under the Scheme during the 
year 2026-27; and 
(f) the steps taken by the Government to ensure timely registration, 
awareness and seamless transfer of benefits to eligible 
employees and employers in Maharashtra? 
 
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA) 
 
(a) to (f): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
*                                                  ***** 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (f) OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 17 BY PROF. VARSHA EKNATH 
GAIKWAD AND SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL DUE FOR REPLY ON 
20.07.2026 REGARDING "DISBURSEMENT OF INCENTIVES UNDER 
PM-VBRY" 
 
(a) to (f): The Government, on 1 July 2025, approved the 
Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme, titled the Pradhan 
Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PMVBRY), to promote 
employment generation, enhance employability, and strengthen 
social security across all sectors including MSMEs and rural 
enterprises, with a particular focus on the manufacturing sector.  
 
  The scheme aims to incentivise creation of more than 3.5 
Crore jobs all across the country, over a period of 2 years including 
the state of Maharashtra. The scheme comprises of two parts i.e. 
Part A and Part B and focuses on providing support to both 
employees and employers by way of incentives. The scheme 
provides for incentives for 1.92 crore eligible First time employees 
under Part A. Incentive for creation of approximately 2.59 crore 
additional jobs to employers is provided for under Part B of the 
scheme. The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is the 
implementing agency for the scheme. 
 
  Prime Minister disbursed incentives worth around ₹2,400 
crore under the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM -
VBRY) at a special programme held on 19 June 20 26 at New Delhi. 
As part of the nationwide outreach effort, PM-VBRY events were also 
organised simultaneously at around 200 locations across the 
country.  
 
  The PMVBRY is a demand-driven scheme. For the State of 
Maharashtra, including Mumbai, under part A, incentive amount of 
Rs 149.41 crore has disbursed to 2.49 lakh first timer employees; and 
under Part B, incentive amount of Rs 435.92 cr has been disbursed 
to 12,701 beneficiary establishments.  
 
  The scheme and its provisions have been widely 
disseminated through extensive outreach efforts across the country. 
EPFO has undertaken awareness and stakeholder outreach 
programmes, including monthly Nidhi Aapke Ni kat (NAN) 
programmes, SMS/email and digital communication campaigns etc. 
to facilitate timely registration and seamless transfer of benefits.  

  A dedicated portal (pmvbry.epfindia.gov.in) has been 
developed to facilitate all scheme -related processes and f or real -
time monitoring of beneficiaries and sector -wise progress. Detailed 
Scheme Guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and 
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) have been made available on 
this portal for ease of understanding.
