STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (D) OF THE LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 187 FOR REPLY ON 31.07.2026 
REGARDING “CONTRIBUTION OF INDIA FOR GLOBAL PEACE”. 
India has consistently sup ported the United Nations in strengthening 
international peace and security. This support has been expressed in a 
variety of ways, including its unique contribution to UN peacekeeping 
operations. This contribution is also reflected in India’s membership of  
the UN Security Council on 8 occasions, with the next candidature 
formally announced for 2028 -29. Each tenure has witnessed placing 
issues of Indian interest on the international agenda, the last in 2021 -22 
being maritime security and counter -terrorism. T he six priorities for the 
2028-29 candidature are: (i) A Voice of Global South (ii) Advancing 
Reformed Multilateralism (iii) A Future Ready Peacekeeping (iv) 
Addressing threats posed due to misuse of AI (v) Securing Maritme 
Commons (vi) Countering Terror Financing.   
India is a key contributor to global peace and security, with almost 
3,00,000 peacekeepers serving in more than 50 UN missions. Currently, 
4,200 Indian peacekeepers are deployed in 9 out of 11 active missions, 
working in challenging conditions to promote international peace.  India’s 
engagement in peacekeeping activities is held in high esteem by the UN 

3 
and member states which is illustrated in various citations and awards 
received by our peacekeepers.  
In recent times, issues pertaining to glob al peace have been debated in 
the United Nations as well as other forums. India has firmly advanced its 
view that dialogue and diplomacy are the best means to achieve lasting 
and durable peace. This has been stated in respect of the Ukraine conflict, 
the developments in West Asia as well as hostilities in the Gulf.  
With regard to the challenge of terrorism, India has strongly advocated a 
policy of zero -tolerance and asserted the right of nations to defend 
themselves against terrorism. Since 1996, India has  also called for the 
adoption of a Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism. India 
supports the counter -terrorism mechanisms established by UN Security 
Council Resolutions, including Resolutions 1267 and 1988 and its 
successors related to sancti ons against Al -Qaeda, Islamic State of Iraq 
and Levant (ISIL), and associated entities such as Lashkar-e-Tayyiba (LeT) 
and Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM). The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), 
as the National Central Bureau for INTERPOL, provides assistance t o 
Indian law enforcement agencies in investigation of cases of terrorism 
and organized crime.  
On cyber -security, India participates in all UN -mandated processes on 
Information and Communication Technology (ICT) security including the 

4 
newly established per manent Global Mechanism on developments in the 
field of ICTs for international security and advancing responsible State 
behaviour in the use of ICTs. India hosted the AI Impact Summit in 
February 2026, where it put forward a human-centric vision of AI – MANAV, 
which stands for Moral and ethical systems; Accountable governance; 
National Sovereignty; Accessible and inclusive; Valid and legitimate 
systems. 
India’s global role has benefited from its effective and purposeful 
multilateral diplomacy. Recent examples of this include election of Indian 
candidates to International Tribunal for the Law of Seas (ITLOS) and Vice-
President of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF).  India’s candidatures 
have received wide support across member states, e.g. election to the  
United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) for the seventh term (2026-
2028), re-election to the Executive Board of the UNESCO (2025-2029), UN 
Economic and Social Council (2026-2028), Vice Chair 2025 and Chair 2026 
of the Kimberley Process, re -election to Council of the International Civil 
Aviation Organisation (ICAO), Council of the International Maritime 
Organization (IMO), election to the Postal Operations Council (POC) and 
Council of Administration of Universal Postal Union (UPU) 2026-2029.   

5 
We have also been a powerful voice for reform of international institutions 
and participate actively in the Inter-Governmental Negotiations for UNSC 
reform.

(a) to (c): The Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice (DISHA) Scheme 
has been continued as DISHA 2.0 as a Central Sector Scheme for the period of 2026-31 for 
pan India implementation in 36 States/UTs . DISHA 2.0 aim s at leveraging technology to 
develop and enhance the outreach of citizen friendly solution platforms for legal services.  It 
includes four components viz. Tele-Law: Reaching the Unreached (free pre-litigation advice 
to all); Nyaya Bandhu (Pro Bono legal Services) Programme; Legal Literacy and Legal 
Awareness Programme and VIDHI (Vision for Integrated Delivery of Harmonized Legal 
Initiatives)-Sanjeevani. 
The Tele -Law Programme is being implemented through CSC -SPV (CSC e -
Governance Services India Ltd.). It connects people with panel lawyers through mobile -app 
and Toll-Free No. 14454 for rendering free pre -litigation legal advice via use of video/tele 
conferencing facilities available at Common Service Centres (CSCs)/Village Level 
Entrepreneurs (VLEs) at the panchayat level, across the country. As on 30.06.2026, more than 
1.13 crore free pre-litigation legal advice has been rendered to beneficiaries under the Tele-
Law Programme, including through Tele-Law Mobile Application. State/UT-wise details of 
beneficiaries covered under the Tele-Law Programme are at Annexure I. 
The Tele-Law Mobile Application is available for download on both the Google Play 
Store and the Apple App Store. As on 30.06.2026, the total number of Tele-Law Mobile App 
downloads is more than 2.75 lakh, 34,415 calls have been registered through this app and 
33,334 pre-litigation legal advice were provided during last three years. 
Under Nyaya Bandhu (Pro -Bono Legal Services) Programme, advocates voluntarily 
provide legal assistance to marginalized and disadvantaged sections of society covered under 
Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities (LSA) Act, 1987. As on 30.06.2026, 10,835 
advocates have been registered under the Nyaya Bandhu Programme and 5 ,559 cases have 
been registered by beneficiaries across the country. State/ UT wise details of cases registered 
under the Nyaya Bandhu Programme are at Annexure II. 
The Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme (LLLAP)  under DISHA 
Scheme, envisages engaging with institutions and building partnerships across stakeholder 
Ministries/Departments/Organizations, to build capacity of the grassroot workers, legally 
empower them and spread legal awareness through workshops, webinars, Information, 

3 
 
Education and Communication ( IEC) materials and collaboration with Prasar Bharati  for 
production and telecast /broadcast of DISHA awareness p rogrammes on Doordarshan and 
Akashvani. 28 thematic National Webinars have also been organized covering key socio-legal 
issues. As on 3 0.06.2026, the programme has  cumulative outreach of more than 2.32 crore 
persons across the country. State/UT-wise data of persons outreached is not maintained.

*189.  Smt. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: 
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognizance of fertilizer shortage, 
especially DAP in various parts of the country, if so, the details thereof indicating their 
demand and supply during the last three years, State and year-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government has taken measures to augment the supply of 
fertilizers, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the details of DAP, MOP and NPK fertilizer imports vis-a-vis domestic fertilizer 
production since 2019, year-wise; and 
 
(d) whether the Government has taken initiatives to increase domestic production 
of fertilizers, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA 
 
 
(a) to (d):  A statement is laid on the table of the House.

-2- 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *189 FOR 
31.07.2026 REGARDING “SHORTAGE OF FERTILIZERS” TABLED BY SMT. 
PRIYANKA GANDHI VADRA. 
 
(a) & (b) Following steps are taken by the Government every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate availability of fertilizers in the country: 
 
(i) Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of 
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State 
Governments, assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of 
fertilizers. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of 
Fertilizers (DoF) allocates adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing 
monthly supply plan and continuously monitors the availability. 
 
(ii) The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 
(iii) The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized 
well in advance to ensure timely availability.  
 
(iv) The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with 
manufacturers and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely 
placement of indents. 
 
(v) Regular coordination is done with the Ministry of Railways for giving sufficient 
rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
(vi) The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/block level is done by 
the concerned State government. 
 
In view of above, the availability of the fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS, in 
the country, has remained adequate during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season i.e. from 
01.04.2026 to 27.07.2026. The information regarding requirement, availability, sales

(d) With regard to Urea, the Government had announced New Investment Policy 
(NIP) – 2012 on 2nd January, 2013 and its amendment on 7thOctober, 2014 to 
facilitate fresh investment in the urea sector and to make India self-sufficient in the 
urea sector. Total 6 new urea units have been set up under NIP-2012 which includes 
4 urea units set up through Joint Venture Companies (JVC) of nominated PSUs and 
2 urea units set up by the private companies. The units set up through JVC are 
Ramagundam urea unit of Ramagundam Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd (RFCL) in 
Telangana and 3 urea units namely Gorakhpur, Sindri and Barauni of Hindustan  
Urvarak & Rasayan Limited (HURL) in Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar, 
respectively. The units set up by private companies are Panagarh urea unit of Matix 
Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (Matix) in West Bengal; and Gadepan-III urea unit of  

-4- 
Chambal Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd. (CFCL) in Rajasthan. Each of these units has 
installed capacity of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonne per annum (LMTPA). These units are 
highly energy efficient as they are based on latest technology. Therefore, these units 
have together added urea production capacity of 76.2 LMTPA, thereby total 
indigenous urea production capacity (Reassessed Capacity, RAC) has increased from 
207.54 LMTPA during 2014-15 to 269.42 LMTPA during 2026-27. Further, an 
exclusive policy for the revival of Talcher unit of FCIL through JVC of nominated PSUs 
namely Talcher Fertilizers Limited (TFL) by setting up a new Greenfield Urea plant of 
12.7 LMTPA at coal gasification route has also been approved. Recently, the Union 
Cabinet has approved the proposal for setting up of a new Brownfield Ammonia-Urea 
Complex of 12.7 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT) annual capacity of Urea production within 
the existing premises of Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizer Corporation Limited (BVFCL), 
Namrup, Assam through JVC of nominated PSUs namely Assam Valley Fertilizer and 
Chemical Company Ltd. (AVFCCL). These two projects are under execution phase. 
Moreover, the Government has also notified the New Urea Policy (NUP) – 2015 on 
25th May, 2015 for the existing 25 gas-based urea units with one of the objectives of 
maximizing indigenous urea production beyond RAC.  The NUP-2015 has led to 
additional production of urea by 20-25 LMT as compared to the production during 
2014-15 annually.  
Above steps together have facilitated increase of Urea production from level of 225 
LMT per annum during 2014-15 to a record Urea Production at 314.07 LMT during 
2023-24. During 2025-26, 293.30 LMT of Urea was produced in the country. 
In addition to this, on 15.07.2026, CCEA approved National Investment Policy 
for Urea-2026 for Aatmanirbhar Bharat (NIPU-2026) for making fresh 
investments in Urea Sector. 
Further, the Government has implemented Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme 
w.e.f. 01.04.2010 for Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) Fertilizers. Under the Scheme, 
P&K fertilizers are covered under Open General License (OGL) and companies are 
free to import/manufacture these fertilizers as per their business dynamics. 
To reduce dependence on imported Phosphatic fertilizers and make country self-
reliant the following measures have been taken by the Government: 
(i) D/o Fertilizers has issued guidelines 18.01.2024 to ensure reasonableness of MRP 
and encourage domestic production. 
(ii) Based on the requests, the new manufacturing units or increase in manufacturing 
capacity of existing units have been recognized / taken on record under the NBS 
Scheme. 
(iii) The number of P&K fertilizers covered under NBS Scheme has increased from 22 
grades in 2021 to 28 grades. 
(iv) Freight Subsidy on SSP, which is an indigenously manufactured fertilizer, has 
been approved since Kharif, 2022 to promote SSP usage for providing Phosphatic or 
'P' nutrient to the soil.

500th meeting held on 7th July 2026 has accorded in principle approval on the proposal 
of raising funds amounting to Rs. 1500 crore through a Further Public Offer (FPO) to

government.

infusion in the existing Joint Venture - Talcher Fertilizers Limited (TFL) and to have 
Strategic Joint Venture Investments by collaborating with other stakeholders to support 
India's fertilizer security and reduce dependence on imports.  
     
 (d):      The renewable energy and water management initiatives of RCF are aimed at 
improving operational efficiency, sustainability and resource optimization, while the 
agrochemical initiatives are intended to broaden the product basket and support 
integrated crop nutrition. These initiatives are not expected to adversely affect fertilizer 
production or supply to farmers.  
 
(e):     Decisions regarding establishment or expansion of fertilizer manufacturing 
facilities are taken after due consideration of factors such as regional fertilizer demand, 
availability of raw materials, techno-economic feasibility, financial viability, logistics and 
other locational advantages. Such requirements are assessed periodically to ensure 
efficient fertilizer production and distribution across the country. 
 
The following steps are taken by the Government in every season for ensuring 
timely and adequate supply of fertilizers in the country, including in the State of Tamil 
Nadu: 
 
I. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture 
and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, 
assesses the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers. On the basis of 
requirement projected by DA&FW, Department of Fertilizers (DoF) allocates 
adequate quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and 
continuously monitors the availability. 
 
II. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the 
country by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer 
Management System (iFMS). 
 
III. The gap between demand (requirement) and production for Urea & other 
fertilizers is met through imports. The import for the season is also finalized well in 
advance to ensure timely availability. 

3 
 
 
 
 
 
 
IV. The State Governments are regularly advised to coordinate with manufacturers 
and importers for streamlining the supplies through timely placement of indents. 
 
V. Regular coordination with the Ministry of Railways is undertaken for giving 
sufficient rakes, priority to fertilizers and for timely evacuation of rakes for States. 
 
VI. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district level is done by the 
concerned State government. 
 
     Accordingly, the availability of fertilizers has remained adequate in the country, 
including in the State of Tamil Nadu, during the ongoing Kharif 2026 season (from 
01.04.2026 to 26.07.2026). The information regarding requirement, availability, 
sales and closing stocks of fertilizers in the country, including in Tamil Nadu, during 
the said period is placed at Annexure.

be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of the progress of the 16 ongoing Research and Development (R&D) projects 
under the AYURGYAN Scheme in the country, State/UT-wise, including Odisha, particularly 
in the Keonjhar Parliamentary constituency; 
(b) the details of the operational status of the Ayurveda Biology Integrated Health Research 
(ABIHR) component; 
(c) the details and the projected timeline for setting up the three new All lndia Institutes of 
Ayurveda (AllAs) announced in the Union Budget 2026; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen research, education and healthcare 
infrastructure for the promotion and integration of Ayurveda through these initiatives?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH  
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 (a) to (d)  A Statement is laid on the table of the House. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

The Statement referred in reply to Lok Sabha Starred question no. 193 for 31.07.2026 
(a) & (b) The Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme namely 
Ayurgyan since 2021-22 with the aim to support Research & Innovation in Ayush by providing 
Extra Mural Research activities and Education by providing academic activities, training, 
Capacity Building etc.  The Scheme has 03 components viz. (i) Capacity Building & 
Continuing Medical Education (CME) in Ayush (ii) Research & Innovation (R&I) in Ayush 
from FY 2021-22 and (iii) Ayurveda Biology Integrated Health Research (ABIHR) was also 
added under the scheme as 3rd component in FY 2023-24. 
Being the  Central Sector Scheme, financial assistance is provided to the eligible 
institutions/organization across the country (including the state of Odisha) and the scheme is 
not specific to any State/UTs and regions .Under the Research & Innovation (R&I) in Ayus h 
and Ayurveda Biology Integrated Health Research (ABIHR) components of the Ayurgyan 
Scheme, 34 and 11 research projects were supported respectively since inception of the scheme 
(i.e. 2021-22) for a duration of three years and funds were released on insta lment basis. The 
details of the same is annexed at Annexure.  
The outcomes of the research projects are in the forms of product development, patents, 
technology developed, SOPs, presentations on international platform, publication in reputed 
journals etc. The anticipated outcomes are realized upon completion of the projects. A total 82 
research papers have been published in peer -reviewed journals under R&I component 
(including Erstwhile EMR) from FY 2021 -22 to as on 30.06.2026 . Further, under the R&I 
component of Ayurgyan Scheme, an amount of Rs.41.36 lakhs were relea sed to National 
Institute of Technology, Rourkela, located in the state of Odisha, for conducting the research 
project.  
(c) In pursuance of the announcement made in the recent Union Budget regarding the 
establishment of three new AIIAs, two committees namely, the Selection Committee and the 
Project Core Committee (PCC) have been constituted by the Ministry of Ayush for the purpose 
of site selection under the Challenge Method, issued by the Cabinet Secretariat. 
(d) To strengthen integration of Ayurveda with basic sciences and the conventional system of 
medicine through  high-end interdisciplinary  research by promoting  collaborative 
research between Ayush institutions  and institutions engaged in modern  biological scien ces, 
ABIHR component of Ayurgyan Scheme has been implemented from 2023-24. Further, under 
Centre of Excellence component of Ayurswasthya Yojana, there is a provision for financial 
assistance for upgradation of infrastructure and integrative research activities.  

 Ministry of Ayush is also implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of National Ayush 
Mission (NAM) through State/UT Governments and supporting their efforts for overall 
development and promotion of Ayush systems of medicines including Ayurveda in the Country 
through State/UT Governments. The main objective of the scheme, inter-alia are as follows:  
➢ Co-location of Ayush facilities at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health 
Centres (CHCs) and District Hospitals (DHs). 
➢ Upgradation of existing standalone Government Ayush Hospitals. 
➢ Setting up of up to 10/30/50 bedded integrated Ayush Hospitals. 
➢ Establishment of new Ayush colleges in the States where availability of Ayush teaching 
institutions is inadequate in Government Sector. 
➢ Infrastructural development of Ayush Under -Graduate Institutions and Ayush Post -
Graduate Institutions/ add on PG/ Pharmacy /Para-Medical Courses. 
 Further, with regard to integration of Ayurveda, Government of India has adopted a 
strategy of Co -location of Ayush facilities at Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community 
Health Centres (CHCs) and District Hospitals (DHs), thus enabling the choice to the patients 
for different systems of medicines under a single window. 
In addition, Research Councils under Ministry of Ayush nam ely Central Council for 
Research in Ayurvedic Science (CCRAS), Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy 
(CCRH), Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Central Council for 
Research in Siddha (CCRS) and Central Council for Research in Yog a & Naturopathy 
(CCRYN) also undertake research activities such as Clinical Research, Drug Proving, Drug 
Verification, Drug validation, Drug Standardization, Public Health Research, Fundamental 
Research and Epidemic research through their Research Institutes/Treatment Centre/Peripheral

strengthening public healthcare system is with the States/Union Territories. However, under the National
Health Mission (NHM), the Government of India supports all States/ Union Territories including
Maharashtra and Union Territories of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu to strengthen the
rural healthcare system. States/ Union Territories submit their proposals through the annual Programme
Implementation Plan (PIP), and based on the available resource envelope (RE), the Government of India
grants approvals in the Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per the approved norms and guidelines. The

https://nhm.gov.in/index1.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1377&lid=744

including strengthening of rural healthcare services in the country, including Maharashtra and the Union
Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu from the FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 is at
Annexure-I.
In addition to NHM, support to States and Union Territories are also approved for strengthening
of Health Care System including Rural Health Care under PM-ABHIM for an amount of Rs. 32,961.10

 Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total subsidy outlay under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme 
for the current financial year; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to revise the present price of urea 
which has remained unchanged since March 2018, if so, the details

(c) special subsidy, if any, being extended for DAP in view of rising global

THE MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS

-2- 
 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO 195* FOR 
31.07.2026 REGARDING “NUTRIENT BASED SUBSIDY SCHEME” TABLED BY 
SHRI NAVEEN JINDAL 
----------- 
(a): For Kharif 2026, under Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme, the Government 
has approved Rs. 41,533.81 crore as subsidy to ensure availability of Phosphatic & 
Potassic (P&K) fertilizers.  
(b): No Sir, as of now, there is no such proposal of the Government to revise the present 
price of Urea.  
(c): In case of Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilizers, Government has implemented 
Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Policy w.e.f. 01.04.2010.  Under NBS policy, MRP of 
P&K fertilizers is decontrolled and companies are free to fix MRP as per their business 
dynamics at a reasonable level. The Government monitors international prices of key 
fertilizers and raw materials and fluctuations, if any, are subsumed while fixing NBS 
rates for P&K fertilizers annually / bi-annually to ensure affordable supply of P&K 
fertilizers to the farmers. Relevant factors like requirement of nutrients in the country, 
balanced use of fertilizers, subsidy burden and MRP of fertilizers are taken into account 
while recommending the subsidy rates for different nutrients.  
Further, to make Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP) which is a key fertilizer, 
available at affordable price of Rs. 1350 per 50 kg bag, special provisions like Rs. 3500 
per MT to cover 'Other Costs' which includes costs incurred from factory gate to farm 
gate, advantage / disadvantage due to increase / decrease in international prices, 
provision for GST component included in the MRP and provision for reasonable return

STARRED QUESTION NO. *196
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 31TH JULY,2026
FACILITIES FOR PATIENTS IN AIIMS
*196 DR. ANAND KUMAR:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has assessed the waiting area and shelter facilities available for patients and
their Kins/attendants arriving from far-flung areas in various All India Institutes of Medical Sciences
(AIIMS) and Post Graduate Institutes (PGIs) in the country, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government is aware that many patients and their relatives coming from farflung areas
are forced to stay outside the hospital premises for days while waiting for treatment or appointments and
encounter extreme heat, chilling cold and rain which imposes mental, physical and financial burdens on
them, if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide larger waiting rooms, rest areas, drinking water, toilets
and other necessary basic amenities for the convenience of the relatives/attendants of patients coming
from far-flung areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the proposed action plan, timeframe and financial provisions
made in this regard?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENTREFERRED TO IN REPLYTO LOK SABHA
STARRED QUESTION NO. 196* FOR 31TH JULY,2026
(a) to (d) The All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) and Post Graduate Institutes (PGIs) have
been providing basic amenities including waiting rooms, shelter facilities, clean drinking water, toilets
and other amenities to the patients and their attendants. In addition, institutes have made provision for
affordable, clean, safe and accessible accommodation facilities to the patients’ attendants in their night
shelters.
These institutes receive high patient load including referrals from various hospitals across the country.
The new AIIMS are witnessing significant increase in Out-Patient Department (OPD) patients and
In-Patient Department (IPD) admissions on account of continuous expansion in delivery of various
healthcare services. Augmentation of night shelters, waiting areas etc. on account of increase in footfall
is an ongoing process based on the actual patient load and requirements.

LOK SABHA
STARRED QUESTION NO. *199
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 31TH JULY,2026
INCIDENCE OF SICKLE CELL DISEASE
*199 DR. KIRSAN NAMDEO:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that the incidence of sickle cell disease is significantly
high among the tribal population of the Gadchiroli, Chandrapur & Gondia district of the
Gadchiroli-Chimur Parliamentary Constituency in Maharashtra, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the number of persons screened, identified as carriers and diagnosed with sickle cell
disease in Gadchiroli, Chandrapur & Gondia district of Maharashtra under the National Sickle
Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission during the last three years, year-wise;
(c) whether the Government proposes to establish additional sickle cell screening centres,
genetic counselling facilities, blood storage units and dedicated treatment centres in the said
Parliamentary Constituency to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment for affected tribal
populations, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the details of financial assistance, manpower deployment, awareness programmes and
availability of medicines such as Hydroxyurea along with other measures taken/proposed to be
taken by the Government to achieve the objective of eliminating sickle cell disease as a public
health problem by 2047 in Gadchiroli district of Maharashtra?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.

STATEMENTREFERRED TO IN REPLYTO LOK SABHA
STARRED QUESTION NO. 199* FOR 31TH JULY,2026
(a) to (d) ‘Public Health’ & ‘Hospitals’ are State subjects. This Ministry provides technical and
financial support to the States/UTs including Maharashtra, for conducting screenings,
procurement of drugs for sickle cell anaemia and strengthening existing blood
banks/establishing new blood bank, based on the proposals received in the form of Programme
Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission (NHM).
Under National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission (NSCAEM), screenings in the
targeted age group of 0-40 years are conducted at all health facilities from District Hospitals
(DH) upto Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) level in affected 17 tribal states including
Maharashtra for diagnosis of Sickle Cell Disease (SCD).
As reported by the States on SCD portal, as on 26.07.2026, more than 7.25 crore screenings
have been conducted in tribal dominated areas of the country including 1.11 crore in the State
of Maharashtra. As informed by State, number of persons screened, identified as carriers and
diagnosed with SCD in Gadchiroli, Chandrapur and Gondia district, under this Mission is at
Annexure.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has devised the cost norms for establishment of Centres
of Excellence (CoE) on SCD funded by Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) in various states. 17
CoEs in 15 states including in AIIMS Nagpur, Maharashtra have been approved by MoTA.
Patients living with SCD are provided with counseling regarding lifestyle management,
pre-marriage and pre-natal decisions.
Hydroxyurea has been included in NHM Essential Drugs List at Sub-Health Centres, Primary
Health Centres (PHC)/ Urban PHC, Community Health Centres and DHs to address the issue
of access to medicine. To monitor the drug procurement and ensure the availability of essential
medicines in public health facilities, Drugs and Vaccine Distribution Management System
(DVDMS) has been launched by the Govt. of India.
Through MoTA, awareness and counseling material have been developed and shared with the
States for propagation of awareness of disease, screening and management.
Under Department of Health Research, ICMR has established the ICMR-National Institute for
Research in Tribal Health (NIRTH), Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh and a Centre for Research
Management and Control of Hemoglobinopathies in Chandrapur, Maharashtra which supports
national programs including sickle cell disease.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA  
STARRED QUESTION NO. 2 
ANSWERED ON-20/07/2026 
 
National Digital University Initiative 
 
*2. Shri Baijayant Panda: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the National Digital University initiative has improved access to higher education 
for students from remote, rural and aspirational districts, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of learners enrolled through digital platforms under the initiative since its 
inception; and 
(c) the measures taken by the Government to ensure academic quality, credit transferability 
and industry relevance of the courses offered under the said initiative? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI DHARMENDRA PRADHAN) 
 
 
(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the table of the House. 
 
 
 
***** 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (C) IN RESPECT OF LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 2 ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 REGARDING 
“NATIONAL DIGITAL UNIVERSITY INITIATIVE” ASKED BY SHRI BAIJAYANT 
PANDA, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT 
 
(a) to (c): The Government of India has framed the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 with 
a vision to strengthen learner-centric and technology-enabled education. In alignment with this 
vision, the Government has envisaged the establishment of a Digital University platform to 
provide flexible and multidisciplinary learning. 
 
National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of 
Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), has launched “NIELIT Digital University 
(NDU) Platform” in October 2025. NDU is a digital learning platform to deliver online and 
blended skill-based courses in emerging technology sectors such as Artificial Intelligence, 
Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing and other frontier domains. The courses on this digital 
platform are aligned to National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) with credits to be 
transferred in the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) after successful completion. As on date, 
the NDU Platform host more than 100 courses, with over 2.70 Lakhs registration. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Education has undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the digital 
learning in higher education ecosystem. The University Grants Commission (UGC) Open & 
Distance Learning Programmes and Online Programmes Regulations, 2020 provide a 
framework for offering quality higher education through Open & Distance Learning and 
Online modes. In the Academic Year 2025-26, over 800 Online programmes were approved 
in more than 120 Universities/HEIs, with an enrolment of 4,26,196 learners.  
 
Further, premier institutions, including IITs, are offering online programmes in emerging areas 
such as Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Machine Learning and Cyber Security. The online 
Bachelor of Science in Data Science programme by IIT Madras has seen more than 55000 
enrolments since 2021.    
 
Additionally, with a view to democratise quality education through digital technology, the 
Ministry of Education has initiated the SWAYAM online platform to provide free access to 
courses from premier institutions. There have been more than 20,000 deliveries of courses on 
the platform, with cumulative enrolments exceeding 6 crores since its inception. Further, under 
the UGC (Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM) Regulations, 
2021, Higher Educational Institutions may offer up to 40% credits in a semester through 
SWAYAM. As of July 2026, 450 universities have adopted the SWAYAM framework for 
credit transfer.  
 
Further, to enhance industry-academia collaboration and improve employability of learners, 
the Ministry of Education has launched SWAYAM Plus platform. As of July 2026, the 
platform offers more than 500 industry-aligned courses across 15 sectors in collaboration with 
89 industry partners.

(a) the details of steps taken by the Government during the last three years to encourage girl 
students in villages and rural areas enrol for higher education in the country, year and State -
wise including Uttarakhand; 
 
(b) whether any Non -Governmental Organisation (NGO) has been entrusted the task of 
giving adequate publicity through social media in various States to encourage girl students to 
enrol for higher education; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI DHARMENDRA PRADHAN) 
 
(a) to (c):  A statement is laid on the table of the House.  
 
 
***** 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (c) OF LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO.20 FOR ANSWER ON 20.07.2026 ASKED BY SHRI 
AJAY BHATT, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT REGARDING 
ENROLMENT OF GIRL STUDENTS FROM RURAL AREAS IN HIGHER 
EDUCATION 
 
(a) to (c): Education is subject of concurrent list and both Central and State government 
work collaboratively to ensure comprehensive,  and progressive enhancement of overall 
quality and growth within the education sector.  Various schemes/ projects/ programmes run 
by the Ministry have been aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. NEP 
2020 aims to ensure that no child loses o pportunity to learn and excel because of the 
circumstances of birth or background. It has taken into account the concerns of the Socio -
Economically Disadvantaged Groups (SEDGs) which inter -alia includes geographical 
identities such as students from village s, small towns, and aspirational districts and other 
categories. This policy aims at bridging the social category gaps in access, participation, and 
learning outcomes. 
 
The Ministry has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)  
as Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) in June 2023 with an outlay of 
Rs. 12926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phases to cater to needs 
of educationally unserved/ underserved areas. The scheme has been further extended till 31 st 
March, 2028 for completion of PM -USHA projects and for additional 6 months (i.e till 30 th 
September, 2026) for completion of ongoing RUSA projects. It is a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme aimed at funding specific State government universities and colleges, including in 
the rural areas, so as to improve their quality by ensuring their conformity to  prescribed 
norms and standards. Under PM -USHA, priority is given to Focus Districts which are 
identified by the concerned States/ UTs based on various criteria including low Gross 
Enrolment Ratio, Gender Parity, population proportion and enrolment proportion for females, 
transgenders, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes, 
Aspirational/ Border Area/ Left Wing Extremism prone district, etc. In particular, the Gender 
Inclusion and Equity Initiatives (GIEI) component of PM -USHA inter-alia also envisages to 
improve girls’ enrolment in higher education, particularly in focus districts, by promoting 
their greater participation in STEM, vocational and other professional courses. 
 
The Central Government has taken various measures to promote  higher education among the 
students across the nation including women, such as fee reductions, establishment of more 
institutes, scholarships, priority access to national level scholarships to aid students with poor 
financial backgrounds to pursue their education.  
 
University Grants Commission (UGC) is implementing scholarship scheme "National 
Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPG)" to provide scholarship to students pursuing 
Post Graduate Programs. UGC is also providing fellowships to pursue Ph.D. in all disciplines 
including STEM education, under UGC NET -Junior Research Fellowship and Savitribai 
Jyoti Rao Phule Single Girl Child Fellowship. 

 
Apart from this, UGC is implementing the scheme of “Development of Women’s Studies in 
Indian Universities and Colleges”. This scheme provides funds for setting up Women Studies 
Centers (WSCs) in universities and colleges, focusing on teaching, research, cu rriculum 
development, training and outreach activities. The objectives of the scheme are to provide 
financial support in advancing Women’s Studies through teaching, research and practical 
work. 
 
Similarly, All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) also offers various 
scholarships like AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Women (Degree & Diploma), 
AICTE PG scholarship Scheme, AICTE Doctoral Fellowship (ADF), AICTE Saksham 
Scholarship Scheme (Degree & Diploma) and AICTE Swanath Scholarship Scheme (Deg ree 
& Diploma). AICTE has also launched the AICTE Post -Doctoral Fellowship (PDF) scheme 
in June 2024 from the academic year 2024 -25 for girls and boys of AICTE approved 
Institutions. 
 
Further, with a view to improve female enrolment in the Undergraduate Pr ogrammes in 
Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and National Institutes of Technology (NITs), 
supernumerary seats were created which increased the female enrolment from less than 10% 
to more than 20%. Women constitute around 43% of enrolment in STEM edu cation, one of 
the highest in the world. 
 
Budget announcement 2026-27 envisages establishment of one girls’ hostel in every district 
to support women’s participation in STEM as in higher education STEM Institutions 
prolonged hours of study and laboratory work pose some challenges for girl students. 
 
As per All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE): 2023 -24, the  female enrolment in 
higher education has increased in the country over the last three years, rising from 2.06 crore 
in 2021-22 to 2.23 crore in 2023-24. The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) for females increased 
from 28.5 in 2021 -22 to 31.2 in 2023 -24. Throughout this period, the female GER 
consistently remained higher than the male GER, resulting in a Gender Parity Index (GPI) 
greater than 1. This indicates that female participation in higher education has surpassed male 
participation during these years. 
 
For the State of Uttarakhand, female enrolment increased from 2.82 lakh in 2021 -22 to 3.24 
lakh in 2023-24. The GER for females in Uttarakhand increased from 43.7 in 2021-22 to 51.7 
in 2023-24 which is significantly higher than the All -India female GER (31.2) in 2023 -24. 
The GPI remained above 1 throughout the last three years reflecting higher participation of 
females than males in higher education in the State.

(a) to (e) Public Health & hospitals fall under the State list and therefore, the primary responsibility of
strengthening public healthcare system is with the States/Union Territories. However, under the National
Health Mission (NHM), the Government of India supports all States/Union Territories. States/Union
Territories submit their proposals through the annual Programme Implementation Plan (PIP), and based
on the available resource envelope (RE), the Government of India grants approvals in the Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per the approved norms and guidelines.
As updated by the States/Union Territories on Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) portal, as on

The Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) are required to deliver 12 packages of primary health
care services across urban, rural, tribal dominated and aspirational district areas, encompassing
Reproductive and Child Care Services, Communicable Diseases, Non Communicable Diseases,

Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has explored the potential of Corporate Social

(b) if so, the framework developed by the Government to encourage deployment

(c) the contribution of CSR -supported innovation and social enterprises towards 
addressing developmental challenges, generating employment and improving 
delivery of public services;  
 
(d) the progress achieved in facilitating partnerships among corporate entities, 
research institutions, incubators and social enterprises for promoting innovation-
led development; and  
 
(e) the initiatives taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to expand the 
role of CSR in financing innovation, strengthening social entrepreneurship and 
supporting growth of high-impact organizations capable of achieving sustainable 
and scalable outcomes? 
 
 
ANSWER

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (e) OF LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. 201 (1st POSITION) FOR 3 rd AUGUST 2026  ASKED BY SHRI VE 
VAITHILINGAM, HON’BLE MEMBER  OF PARLIAMENT REGARDING CSR 
RESOURCES TOWARDS RESEARCH AND INNOVATION. 
      
(a) to (c): Yes Sir. The legal framework for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) 
has been provided under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’), Schedule 
VII of the Act and Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014.  Schedule VII of the Act 
indicates the list of eligible activities which can be undertaken by the companies 
under CSR.  These activities are broad-based and may be interpreted liberally so 
as to capture the essence of the subjects enumerated therein. 
The activities mentioned under Schedule VII are broadly aligned with national 
priorities to promote inclusive and sustainable development and include 
measures to support multiple social sectors viz. education, environmental 
sustainability, gender equality, healthcare, livelihood enhancement projects, skill 
development, eradication of hunger, safe drinking water, sanitation, socio -
economic equalities including slum area development, rural development projects 
and for reducing inequalities faced by socially &  economically backward groups 
etc. Further, under Schedule VII, companies may undertake CSR activities by 
contributing to four funds namely Clean Ganga fund, Prime Minister’s National 
Relief Fund (PMNRF), Prime Minister’s Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency 
Situations Fund (PMCARES) and Swachh Bharat Kosh, thus delivering scalable 
social impact across the country. The activities thus mentioned in Schedule VII  
Further, item (ix) of the Schedule VII also provides for contribution to incubators 
or research and development projects in the field of science, techn ology, 
engineering and medicine.     
On the basis of annual filings made by companies in the MCA21 registry, 
Development sector-wise CSR expenditure in India for the last five financial years 
i.e. FY 2021-22 to FY 2024-25 is attached at Annexure. 
(d):   Under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 4(1) of the 
Companies (CSR Policy) Rules, 2014, it is prescribed that the Board of the 
company is empowered to undertake its CSR activities either by itself or through- 
i. a company established under section 8 of the Act, or a registered public 
trust or a registered society, exempted under sub -clauses (iv), (v), (vi) or (via) of 
clause (23C) of section 10 or registered under section 12A and approved under 80 
G of the Inco me Tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961), established by the company, either 
singly or along with any other company; or 

ii. a company established under section 8 of the Act or a registered trust or a 
registered society, established by the Central Government or State Government; 
or  
iii. any entity established under an Act of Parliament or a State legislature; or  
iv. a company established under section 8 of the Act, or a registered public 
trust or a registered society, exempted under sub -clauses (iv), (v), (vi) or (via) of 
clause (23C) of section 10 or registered under section 12A and approved under 80 
G of the Income Tax Act, 1961, and having an established track record of at least 
three years in undertaking similar activities.  
The above legal framework facilitates partnerships between the companies and 
suitable implementing agencies.  
(e): The Ministry has recently vide notification dated 27.05.2026 widened the 
ambit of Schedule VII by introduction of new item no. (xiii) namely “Subscription 
to zero coupon zero principal instruments on Social Stock Exchange." This 
amendment will help Not for  Profit Organisations to raise funding for public 
welfare projects in a transparent and regulated manner.

*202. SHRI T R BAALU: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has taken any initiative to promote Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship training programmes  in fashion designing for the handloom weavers 
particularly, rural women to improve their livelihood opportunities; 
  
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(c) the details of number of handloom workers benefitted under the said programmes 
during the last three years and the current year along with the expenditure incurred by 
the Government on such schemes during the said period, State/UT-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP

STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PART (A) TO (C) OF LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *202 ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 REGARDING ‘PROMOTION OF 
SKILL DEVELOPMENT FOR HANDLOOM WEAVERS’ ASKED BY SHRI T R BAALU 
  
(a) to (c):  Government of India actively implements several initiatives targeting skill 
development, and entrepreneurship training for handloom weavers, including fashion 
designing, with a special emphasis on empowering rural women. The Handloom Sector 
is one of the largest unorganized economic activities of India and it constitutes an integral 
part of the rural and semi - rural livelihood engaging over 35 lakh persons. The sector 
engages over 25 lakh female weavers and allied workers which make it an important 
source of economic empowerment of women.  
  
▪ Under the Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres  under various schemes, viz. 
Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), 
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training 
Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the 
society across the country including handloom weavers. The SIM aims at enabling 
youth of India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills, 
including handloom weaving. State/UT -wise details of handloom workers trained 
under schemes of MSDE during the last three years and the current year (up to 
30th June 2026) is given at Annexure-I. 
▪ SAMARTH (Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector) is a demand -driven, 
placement-oriented skilling program of Ministry of Textiles that targets the 
sustainable creation of livelihoods and provides entry-level training, upskilling, and 
reskilling across the entire textile value chain including handloom and handicrafts. 
State/UT-wise details of handloom workers trained under Samarth during the last 
three years and current year up to 29th July 2026 is given at Annexure-II. 
▪ National Handloom Development Programme (NHDP) is the flagship Central 
Sector scheme implemented by the Ministry of Textiles to provide holistic, need -
based support to handloom weavers. Under National Handloom Development 
Programme (NHDP) need based financ ial support is provided for various 
interventions like provision of upgraded looms & accessories, construction of 
worksheds, lighting units, product & design development as well as Concessional 
Credit under Weaver MUDRA Scheme from the Banks/financial institutions to the 
handloom sector to meet their credit requirement for term loan & working capital in 
a flexible and cost -effective manner ( Annexure III & IV ). The Government 
promotes the formation and strengthening of Handloom Producer Companies 
(HPCs) as a key institutional mechanism for organizing handloom weavers into 
professionally managed, member owned enterprises. 237 Handloom Producer 
Companies are formed under NHDP during 2020-21 to 2025-26. About 1.50 lakh 
weavers/handloom entities are on-boarded on Government e-Marketplace (GeM) 
for marketing of handloom products to the Government Departments. The 
Government has also developed India handmade as a dedicated e -commerce 
platform for authentic handloom products, including GI-tagged products, enabling 
verified weavers and producer groups to sell directly to consumers. Overall, 5413 
weavers have been onboarded onto India handmade platform during 2023 -24 to 
2026-27 (up to 30.06.2026).  
▪ Craft Cluster Initiative:   National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), in 
collaboration with the offices of DC -Handlooms and DC-Handicrafts emphasizes 

on extensive fieldwork and collaboration between students and artisans across 
India. Through research and design projects, students work to uplift traditional 
crafts and blend them with contemporary design elements.  
▪ Six Indian Institute of Handloom Technology (IIHT) (Varanasi, Salem, Bargarh, 
Fulia, Guwahati, Jodhpur) uphold academic excellence in handloom and textile 
education through three-year Diploma and four-year B. Tech programs.  
▪ Funds under PMKVY  are released to implementing agencies for meeting the 
training cost as per prescribed norms.  Under JSS scheme, funds are released to 
Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) directly.  Under NAPS, stipend support 
up to Rs 1500/- per month is released to apprentices through DBT and not to the 
establishments covered.  Day to day administration as well as financial control in 
respect of CTS scheme implemented through ITIs lies with the respective State

Udaipur, Prayagraj, Kolkata, Dimapur and Thanjavur. These ZCCs organize various cultural 
activities and programmes on regular basis all over India for which annual grant-in-aid is 
provided to them. The number of cultural programmes/ festivals/ activities organized, artists

 Besides, the following cultural programmes/ festivals/ activitiesorganizes/ organized 
by Ministry of Culture through these ZCCs are as under: 
 
Rashtriya Sanskriti Mahotsavs (RSMs): 
 
 Ministry of Culture, Government of India through its Zonal Cultural Centres 
(autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture), organizes Rashtriya Sanskriti 
Mahotsavs (RSMs) to celebrate the spirit of tradition, culture, heritage and the rich diversity 
of our incredible country. The broader objective of this Mahotsav is to preserve, promote and 
popularize India's cultural heritage, reconnect the younger generation with our traditions and 
showcase to the nation and the world our soft power through unity in diversity. Since 2015, 
Ministry has organized 14 RSMs and 04 Zonal Level RSMs through its seven ZCCs. An 
amount of Rs. 13587.86 lakh was released to various ZCCs for organization of these RSMs/ 
Zonal RSMs at various venues of the country and a total of 12543 artists have participated in 
these RSMs/ Zonal RSMs. 
 
 
Kashi Tamil Sangamam: 
 
 Kashi Tamil Sangamam event was organized during 2022, 2023 & 2025 (3rd& 4th 
editions) at Varanasi. The Nodal Authority for organizing Kashi Tamil Sangamam event was 

 
 
Ministry of Education. The cultural inputs for the event were jointly facilitated by the ZCCs 
on behalf of the Ministry of Culture. 1115 artists in 2022, 674 artists in 2023& 1059 artists in 
3rd edition & 850 artists in 4th edition during 2025 have participated in the event. 
 
MadhavpurGhed Fair: 
 
 MadhavpurGhed Fair 2022 to 2026 was organized in Gujarat. The fair was an 
epitome of the deep cultural and historical relationship that western State of Gujarat shares 
with the North-Eastern States. The cultural inputs for the event were facilitated by NEZCC. 
120 artists in 2022, 239 artists in 2023, 45 artists in 2024, 800 artists in 2025 & 269 artists in 
2026 from North East Region have participated. MadhavpurGhed, a small but culturally 
significant village is the place where according to folklore, Lord Krishna married Rukmini, 
the daughter of King Bhishmaka. 
 
Saurashtra Tamil Sangamam: 
 
 Saurashtra Tamil Sangamam was organised from 17th to 30th April, 2023 in Gujarat 
jointly by the Ministry of Culture and Government of Gujarat with the main purpose of 
facilitating exchange of history, art and culture between the States of Gujarat and Tamil 
Nadu. This event was organized at 3 locations i.e. Somnath, Dwarka and Kevadia. The 
cultural inputs for the event were facilitated by the ZCCs through participation of 250 artists. 
 
Vividhhta Ka Amrit Mahotsav: 
 
 'Vividhhta Ka Amrit Mahotsav' was organized by the Ministry of Development of 
North Eastern Region (DoNER) in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture in 2024 & 2025 
at Rashtrapati Bhawan, New Delhi. The cultural inputs for the event were facilitated by 
Ministry of Culture in 2024 through NEZCC (424 artists) & in 2025 through SZCC, 
Thanjavur (177 artists)  
 
BHARATIYA KALA MAHOTSAV:  
  
 Bharatiya Kala Mahotsav was organized at Rashtrapati Nilayam, Hyderabad in 2024 
& 2025 on the directives of Rashtrapati Bhawan and Ministry of Culture in which Cultural 
Performances were showcased. Hon’ble President of India inaugurated the event. 250 artists 
in 2024 &370 artists in 2025 participated in the event. 
 
KALAGRAM: 
 
 On the request of Government of Uttar Pradesh, Ministry of Culture had set up a 
cultural village viz. Kalagram in Sector-7 of Maha Kumbh district through North Central 
Zone Cultural Centre (NCZCC) located at Prayagraj, an autonomous organization of the 
Ministry. The main features of Kalagram were: 
 
 Main Entrance: 635 ft wide, 54 ft high, depicting 12 Jyotirlingas and the story of Lord 
Shiva consuming Halahal, a confluence of art and spirituality. 
 A stage 104 feet-wide & 72 feet-depth on the theme of Char-Dham. 
 Artists and Performances: 14,632 artists performed on various stages including 
Kalagram. 
 Anubhut Mandapam: 360° immersive experience narrating Ganga descent from 
heaven to earth. 
 Aviral Shashwat Kumbh: Digital display by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), 
National Archives of India (NAI) and Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts 
(IGNCA). 
 Food Zone: Satvik cuisine from all Zonal Cultural Centres apart from the local 
cuisine of Prayagraj. 

 
 
 Sanskriti Angans: Display and sale of traditional Indian handicrafts and handlooms in 
the courtyards by 98 artisans of the seven Zonal Cultural Centres. 
 
Aadi Thiruvathirai Festival: 
 
 Ministry of Culture organised the Aadi Thiruvathirai Festival at 
GangaikondaCholapuram in Tamil Nadu from 23rd to 29th July, 2025 to celebrate the birth 
anniversary of Rajendra Chola I and commemorate the 1000th year of his maritime 
expedition to Southeast Asia. The Hon’ble Prime Minister graced the function on 27th July, 
2025 in the presence of 30 Adheenams and released a commemorative coin on Rajendra 
Chola I, a Devaram booklet published by Sahitya Akademi and a musical album on the 
Bhagavad Gita composed by Ilaiyaraaja. 
 
         The festival featured performances by folk artists and the rendering of Devaram 
Thirumurai by Othuvars, a vanishing tradition that continues to survive in select Shiva 
temples of Tamil Nadu. 
 
CULTURAL PERFORMANCES AT WORLD EXPO-2025: 
 
 The Ministry of Culture, Government of India showcased India’s rich cultural 
heritage at World Expo 2025 in Osaka with 25 artists delegation. The contingent presented 
diverse folk and classical performances including Lavni, Dandiya, Pung Cholom, Kathak, 
Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi and Sattriya, along with instrumental recitals by young maestros. 
Daily shows from 29 September to 4 October, 2025 attracted large audiences and earned high 
appreciation from Expo authorities. A highlight of India’s participation was Gandhi Jayanti 
Celebration held on 2 October, 2025 at the Festival Station Auditorium within the Expo 
Grounds. India’s participation received widespread acclaim for its artistic excellence and 
contribution to cultural diplomacy. 
 
CULTURAL PRESENTATION DURING REPUBLIC DAY CELEBRATIONS: 
 
 Vande Bharatam Dance Competition Event was organized by the Ministry of Culture 
on behalf of Ministry of Defence, under the aegis of Republic Day Celebrations during 2022, 
2023 and 2024. 485 dancers were selected to perform at the Republic Day Parade 2022 and 
479 dancers during 2023 on the theme of ‘Ek Bharat Shrestha Bharat’ & ‘Naari Shakti’ 
respectively. During 2024 RD Parade, around 1500 female artists/dancers in the age group of 
18-35 years presented the cultural extravaganza on the theme ‘Sankalp se Siddhi’. For the 
first time, 112 Female Heralders who had led the parade playing traditional drums & musical 
instruments were also part of the finale show. A special prize has been awarded to Ministry 
of Culture for “Vande Bharatam” Dance Group by Ministry of Defence each year.   
 
 
 A cultural presentation was also organized during the Republic Day Celebrations, 
2026 at Kartavya Path, New Delhi through NZCC, Patiala to showcase of India’s rich and 
diverse cultural heritage. A total of approximately 1,400 folk artists from all seven Zonal 
Cultural Centres (200 artists from each ZCC), along with 1,100 classical artists and 100 
heralders from the Sangeet Natak Akademi and 100 props holders from the National School 
of Drama, participated in the event. The cultural presentation was curated around the theme 
“èवतंğताकामंğ – वÛदेमातरम; समृɮͬधकामंğ – आ×मǓनभ[रभारत”, reflecting the spirit of 
national unity, freedom and self-reliance. 
 
 Sangeet Natak Akademi (SNA), an autonomous organization under Ministry of 
Culture, organizes festivals at all over the country, gives grants-in-aid for research, 
documentation and publishing in the performing arts; organizes and subsidizes seminars and 
conferences of subject specialists; documents and records the performing arts for its audio-
visual archive. The Akademi organizes “Festival, Workshop & Exhibition” to present 

 
 
classical, traditional, tribal and other forms of Indian performing arts in order to preserve art 
traditions in live practice and develop technique and creative process through performance 
and workshop, by holding and supporting music festivals, Seminars & Workshops & 
Exhibitions etc. 
 
 Since 2013, SNA has been holding a series of festivals titled ‘Desaj’ in different 
regions of the country to promote and encourage artists in the field of folk and tribal music, 
dance and theatre of the country. Besides Desaj festival the following festivals has been 
organizing by the Akademi for preservation of tribal culture: 
 
 Lok Jan Pratha Utsav-celebrating the tribal performing arts of India. 
 Lok Sangam- festival of senior folk and tribal artists of India. 
 Lok Pratibha- a festival of young folk and tribal artists focused on narrative and 
traditional arts form of India. 
 
 SNA have a scheme “Training and Preservation of Traditional, Folk & Tribal 
Performing Arts” in which various selected forms of music, dance, theatre including crafts 
associated with the performing arts and allied arts from all over the country is given support 
with special attention to training in non-formal and personalized atmosphere in the tradition 
of Guru-shishya Parampara. The scheme supports performances, workshops and exhibitions 
of musical instruments and crafts associated with traditional performing art forms.  
 
 SNA also runs a scheme viz. “Survey, Research, Documentation, Dissemination & 
Publication”. The objective of this scheme is to preserve recordings of different arts forms for 
the purpose of research and dissemination. Under the said scheme, the Akademi provides 
grant to individuals and cultural institutions for research work and documentation of folk and 
tribal art forms of the country. 
 
 SNA presented more than 2500 folk and tribal artists from all over India in Jayati Jai 
Mamah Bharatam dance choreography held on the occasion of Republic Day Parade 2025 at 
Kartavya Path, New Delhi.Fifty (50) artists of Gond Tribes were also engaged 
from Gadchiroli-Chimurto participate in the Republic Day Parade 2026.  
  
 The Akademi presented more than 250 folk and tribal artists from all over India in 
IGC 20.COM held on the occasion of Twentieth session of the Intergovernmental Committee 
for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, UNESCO in December 2025 at Lal 
Quila, New Delhi. 
  
 The Akademi presented 250 folk and tribal artists from all over India on the occasion 
of Closing ceremony of Birsa Munda Birth Anniversary held in November, 2025 at 
Didiyapada, Gujarat.  
 
 SNA is the nodal agency for all the Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) related matters 
and maintains the National Inventory of ICH which involves the audio-visual documentation 
and digitization of the ICH elements. In addition, the reports and AV material received as 
part of the Scheme for “Safeguarding the Intangible Cultural Heritage and Diverse Cultural 
Traditions of India” (operational between 2013-2016 only) is digitally available with SNA. 
 
 On the occasion of Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrating 75 years of India’s 
Independence, Sangeet Natak Akademi& Sahitya Akademi in collaboration with Department 
of Culture, Government of Madhya Pradesh organized a grand festival of folk and tribal 
performing arts named ‘Utkarsh’ at Bhopal from 3rd to 5th August, 2023. The festival was 
inaugurated by the Hon’ble President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu. Total 48 groups and 
approx. 1000 folk and tribal artists from different States and UTs of India participated in the 
festival.  
 

 
 
 Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous institution 
under the Ministry of Culture, has undertaken the following major initiatives for the 
preservation, promotion, documentation and dissemination of India's indigenous and tribal 
cultural heritage during the period from 2014 to 2025 through its Indian Knowledge System: 
 
 Documentation, research and archiving of tribal and indigenous traditions, oral 
histories, folklore, performing arts, rituals, festivals, crafts and traditional knowledge 
systems across different States and Union Territories. 
 Ethnographic field documentation through audio-visual recording, photography and 
digital archiving under various academic divisions of IGNCA. 
 Organisation of national and regional exhibitions, seminars, workshops, lecture series, 
festivals and cultural interactions highlighting the art, culture and knowledge 
traditions of tribal communities. 
 Publication of research monographs, exhibition catalogues, documentaries and other 
scholarly works on tribal culture and indigenous knowledge systems. 
 Digitization and preservation of manuscripts, photographs, rare archival records and 
audio-visual material relating to tribal and folk traditions. 
 Collaboration with State Governments, universities, research institutions, museums, 
cultural organisations and tribal communities for documentation and dissemination of 
tribal cultural heritage. 
 Implementation of projects relating to intangible cultural heritage, including 
documentation of traditional performing arts, crafts, oral traditions and community 
knowledge. 
 
 To promote and preserve the tribal languages of India, Sahitya Akademi (an 
autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture) has constituted a separate board viz. 
Centre for Oral and Tribal Literature (COTLIT). The Board consist of various Tribal 
language experts, who suggest various steps and measures to be undertaken from time to time 
for the protection and promotion of tribal languages - both by publishing literature and by 
organizing programmes such as Tribal Writers’ Meet etc.  
 Sahitya Akademi has also a Language Development Board (LDB) which comprises of 
language experts from both the recognized and unrecognized languages of the country. 
Through this Board, the Akademi bestows Bhasha Samman for significant contribution to the 
languages not formally recognized by it as also for contribution to classical and medieval 
literature. For the years 2014 to 2025, the Akademi has given Bhasha Samman for 16 
unrecognized languages including, Kumauni, Adi, Bhili, Halbi, Kurukh, Ladakhi, Sourashtra, 
Magahi, Tulu, Koshali-Sambalpuri, Paite, Hariyanvi, Bhojpuri, Tiwa, Mizo, and Bundeli, and 
another 20 Bhasha Samman in the field of Classical and Medieval Literature.   
 
 Apart from this, Sahitya Akademi also organizes various Language Conventions as 
suggested by the Language Development Board in order to preserve and discover the richness 
of language and literature of various unrecognized languages.   
 
 Besides, more than 300 tribal writers from Tiwa, Koshli-Sambalpuri, Rabha, Bhoti, 
Kurmali, Sadri, Saora, Naga, Nyishi, Baigani, Korku and Kharia languages, have been 
benefited by the Language Conventions organized by the Sahitya Akademi. In addition, 24 
writers received Bhasha Samman in 16 unrecognized languages which included Kumauni, 
Adi, Bhili, Halbi, Kurukh, Ladakhi, Sourashtra, Magahi, Tulu, Koshali-Sambalpuri, Paite, 
Hariyanvi, Bhojpuri, Tiwa, Mizo and Bundeli. Further, 20 Bhasha Samman were given to 20 
writers in the field of Classical and Medieval Literature.   
 
 During the past two years, first-year students of the National School of Drama 
(NSD), an autonomous organization under Ministry of Culture, undertook educational visits 
to the Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS), Bhopal, as part of their 
academic curriculum to develop an understanding of anthropology and India's diverse 
cultural heritage. The visits focused on the study of tribal cultures, traditional dance forms, 

 
 
folk music and indigenous knowledge systems, with special emphasis on the tribal heritage 
and cultural traditions of Madhya Pradesh. 
 
 Adi Rang Mahotsav is a flagship initiative of the National School of Drama dedicated 
to preserving, promoting and showcasing India's tribal performing arts and indigenous 
cultural traditions. Instituted in 2013–14, it is the country's first national festival exclusively 
focused on tribal theatre and allied cultural practices. Since its inception, more than 25 
editions of Adi Rang Mahotsav and its associated festivals have been organized across the 
country, engaging well over 10,000 tribal artists, performers and artisans. The festival has 
been hosted at several locations, including Mumbai, Dwaronda (West Bengal), Raipur, 
Daman, Port Blair, Surat, Nashik, Chaibasa (Jharkhand), Hyderabad, Tinsukia (Assam), 
Kendujhar (Odisha), Goa, Santiniketan (West Bengal), Khairagarh (Chhattisgarh) and New 
Delhi, thereby reaching diverse tribal communities and audiences nationwide. The festival 
features tribal theatre, music, dance, crafts, indigenous knowledge systems, seminars and 
workshops, providing a national platform for tribal artists and artisans while promoting the 
preservation of India's rich tribal cultural heritage and enhancing their livelihood 
opportunities.

 Anthropological Survey of India (AnSI), under Ministry of Culture, plays a 
significant role in the preservation, promotion and documentation of India's indigenous and 
tribal cultures as part of its broader anthropological mandate. AnSI has contributed 
extensively to safeguarding cultural heritage through research, field investigations, 
documentation and museum-based initiatives. The major contributions of AnSI's are the 
systematic documentation of folk arts and craft traditions. AnSI has recorded and preserved 
cultural expressions such as Warli paintings, Gond wall art and tribal musical instruments, 
while various research projects have focused on mapping both tangible and cultural heritage, 
thereby strengthening the preservation of community traditions. 
 
 AnSI has also promoted indigenous cultural practices through visual anthropology by 
producing ethnographic films that document endangered performing arts and oral traditions. 
One such initiative is the documentation of the Beniputul glove-puppet tradition of West 
Bengal, which has contributed to the preservation of traditional knowledge and enhanced 
public awareness of India's diverse cultural heritage. 
 
In the field of traditional knowledge systems, AnSI undertakes research on indigenous 
ecological knowledge system, sustainable resource management and community-based 

 
 
practices. AnSI’s Regional Centres, including the Andaman and Nicobar Regional Centre, 
have prioritised the study of traditional knowledge systems, while collaborative research 
projects have further documented tribal knowledge and customary practices. 
 
 Further, AnSI’s museums support cultural heritage by showcasing tribal life and 
cultural expressions, including elements.  
 
 Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya (IGRMS), Bhopal, an autonomous 
institution under the Ministry of Culture, was established with the objective of preserving, 
documenting, researching, interpreting and disseminating the diverse cultural heritage of the 
people of India, with particular emphasis on tribal and indigenous communities. The Museum 
adopts an integrated approach to showcasing the country's cultural diversity through Open-
Air Exhibitions, Indoor Galleries, ethnographic collections, field documentation, research, 
publications, educational outreach and community engagement. 
 
 IGRMS serves as a national repository of ethnographic heritage and provides a 
platform for the preservation of both tangible and intangible cultural traditions by fostering 
collaboration among museums, academic institutions, cultural organizations and indigenous 
communities. To preserve, promote and disseminate the rich cultural heritage of tribal and 
indigenous communities, IGRMS undertakes a wide range of activities, which include: 
 
 National Tribal Dance Festival: Started in 2015 as a collaborative venture with 
SCSTRTI Bhubaneswar. 
 Tribal Fusion Music: Program launched in 2016 to celebrate indigenous musical 
blending. 
 Oriha Festival: Celebrated the festival of the Wancho tribe of Arunachal Pradesh on 
the IGRMS campus. 
 Tribal Literature Festival (TLF): Introduced at a national level to preserve the 
language and literature of Tribal India. 
 Artist Camps (2017): Successfully organized 13 workshops including tribal healers in 
Mysuru, wood carving in Assam, and textile weaving in Manipur. 
 Reh Festival Documentation: Documented the traditional Reh festival of the Idu 
Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh in 2017. 
 Weekly Market Documentation: Carried out extensive field documentation of tribal 
weekly markets in Assam. 
 Indigenous People's Day: Commemorated the International Day of the Indigenous 
People annually through exhibitions, lectures, and symposia starting in 2018. 
 Gunjar Festival: Hosted an indigenous music and cultural festival featuring the 'Bana' 
string instrument of the Pradhan Gond tribe along with Kalbelia and Chakri dances. 
 Chitralipi Programme: Launched a tribal painting initiative featuring nine 
communities to celebrate the work of the famous late Gond artist Sri Jangarh Singh 
Shyam. 
 Digital COVID Response (2020): Launched online videos showcasing museum 
collections and preserved tribal house types during the pandemic period. 
 Azadi ka Amrit Mahotsav (2021): Hosted tribal artists' workshops featuring painting, 
wood carving, bamboo, cane craft, pottery, and textile traditions. 
 Deshaj Exhibition: Organized an exhibition focused on indigenous technology to 
support tribal artists and promote native knowledge systems. 
 Janjati Gaurav Diwas (2022): Launched and observed the day to commemorate the 
birth anniversary of the legendary freedom fighter Birsa Munda. 
 Tribal Freedom Fighters: Curated and organized a dedicated exhibition highlighting 
the contributions of tribal freedom fighters.

Assessment of Carbon Sink Targets 
 
*205. SHRI MAHENDRA SINGH SOLANKY: 
          SMT. ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN:   
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of progress made towards the national target of creating an additional carbon 
sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO₂ through enhanced forest cover, including specific 
expenditure, total area of land and measurable outcomes from afforestation, ecological 
restoration and landscape-based conservation programmes during the last five years in 
the country, State/UT- wise particularly in Madhya Pradesh, Ratlam, Bharatpur and 
Dewas-Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies; 
 
(b) whether any forest restoration, climate resilience or biodiversity conservation projects 
have been sanctioned or proposed for the Dewas-Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituency; 
 
(c) the ecological outcomes achieved and total expenditure incurred under the Green Credit 
Programme (GCP) in Kandhamal, Boudh, Bhanjanagar and Nayagarh; 
 
(d) whether the Government has developed any technology-enabled monitoring system for 
real-time monitoring of forest restoration and Green Credit Programme activities in 
these areas and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(e) the steps taken to strengthen community participation, particularly through Joint Forest 
Management Committees (JFMCs), Gram Sabhas and local bodies in forest 
conservation and climate resilience initiatives in the country including in Delhi; and 
 
(f) the details of initiatives taken to boost Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) collection 
and market linkage with e-NAM to enhance local livelihoods in these districts along 
with the projects being operated through community participation in the said 
districts/regions and the details of achievements made and future action plans for these 
projects?

(SHRI BHUPENDER YADAV)
