STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (f) OF THE LOK 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 205 DUE FOR REPLY ON 03.08.2026 
REGARDING ASSESSMENT OF CARBON SINK TARGETS BY SHRI MAHENDRA 
SINGH SOLANKY AND SMT.  ANITA NAGARSINGH CHOUHAN. 
(a) to (f) Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, an organization under the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change, carries out the assessment of forest resources 
including forest carbon stock of the country biennially and publishes the findings in the India 
State of Forest Report (ISFR). The assessment is a wall-to-wall mapping exercise based on 
remote sensing supported by intensive ground verification and field data from the National 
Forest Inventory.  As per the GHG inventory for the year 2022, reported in India’s first Biennial 
Transparency Report submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate 
Change (UNFCCC), the forest net sink and carbon sequestration is 0.149 billion tonnes of CO2 
equivalent. Thus, India has achieved 2.44 billion tonnes of carbon sequestration from forest 
and tree cover by 2022 against its target of sequestering 2.5-3 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent 
through increased forest and tree cover by 2030. 
Forest restoration, climate resilience and biodiversity conservation activities are undertaken 
under various Centrally Sponsored and Central Sector Schemes implemented by the 
States/UTs. Further, the Government is implementing various programmes for conservation, 
enhancement of forest and tree cover and ecological restoration, including the National Mission 
for a Green India (Green India Mission) under the National Action Plan on Climate Change 
(NAPCC), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), 
Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI), Nagar Van Yojana 
and other afforestation and ecological restoration programmes through the States/UTs. 
State/UT-wise details of funds approved/released under the afforestation schemes, namely the 
Green India Mission (GIM), National CAMPA, MISHTI and Nagar Van Yojana, are placed at 
Annexures I, II, III and IV, respectively. Parliamentary Constituency-wise data, including for 
Ratlam, Bharatpur and Dewas-Shajapur Lok Sabha Constituencies is not maintained.  
The Green Credit Programme (GCP) is an innovative mechanism to incentivise voluntary 
environmental actions and promote the Lifestyle for Environment (LiFE) movement. The 
Green Credit Rules, 2023, notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, provide for 
activities such as tree plantation, water management, sustainable agriculture, waste 
management, air pollution reduction, mangrove conservation and restoration, Eco Mark label 
development, and sustainable building and infrastructure, resulting in the issuance of Green 
Credits. The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), Dehradun is 
Administrator for implementation of the Programme. 
ICFRE has reported that one eco-restoration project covering an area of 5 hectares has been 
taken up under the Green Credit Programme in Balliguda Forest Division, Kandhamal. An 
expenditure of ₹24,75,736 has been incurred on the project as on date, as reported by the State 
Forest Department. No eco-restoration projects have been taken up under the Green Credit 
Programme in Boudh, Bhanjanagar and Nayagarh. The Green Credit Programme provides for 
tree plantation and eco-restoration of degraded forest lands on registered land parcels. No 
comprehensive assessment of the ecological or environmental outcomes under the Green Credit 
Programme has been undertaken so far. 
A digital monitoring and verification framework has been developed under the Green Credit 
Programme (GCP). The framework provides for periodic monitoring of plantation and eco-
restoration activities through the Green Credit Programme Portal, supported by field-based 
verification. In addition, the ICFRE, Dehradun, developed a Manual on Monitoring and 

Reporting of Restoration Activities under the Green Credit Programme to facilitate uniform, 
transparent and scientific monitoring of project implementation.   
The National Forest Policy, 1988 recognizes the dependence of forest-dwelling and other 
forest-dependent communities on forest resources and emphasizes their participation in the 
protection, regeneration and development of forests, while also promoting employment 
opportunities for people living in and around forests. At the village level, Gram Sabhas play an 
important role in the management of community resources. Further, Joint Forest Management 
Committees (JFMCs) and Village Eco-Development Committees (EDCs) have been 
constituted in various States through participatory approaches to involve local communities in 
forest protection, conservation and management, including matters relating to the livelihoods 
of forest-dwelling communities.   
 
The Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) are permitted to collect Non-Timber 
Forest Produce (NTFP) in accordance with the extant rules and guidelines of the respective 
State/UT Governments. Non-Timber Forest Produce is generally not traded through the 
National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) platform, which is primarily meant for notified 
agricultural commodities.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. *206 
ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026. 
  
ESTABLISHMENT OF INDUSTRY-LINKED SKILL DEVELOPMENT CENTRE IN ANAKAPALLI 
 
*206. DR. C M RAMESH: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)  whether the Government proposes to establish an Industry-Linked Skill Development Centre 
in Anakapalli to meet the manpower requirements of the Visakhapatnam –Anakapalli industrial 
region;  
 
(b) if so, the details of the sectors proposed to be covered under the training programme; 
 
(c)  the total number of youth proposed to be trained annually through the said centre; and 
 
(d)  the placement mechanism proposed with the industries to ensure employment  
opportunities for the trained youth? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d):  A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED IN REPLY TO PART (a) to (d) OF LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *206 ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 REGARDING ‘INDUSTRY -LINKED SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT CENTRE IN ANAKAPALLI’ ASKED BY DR. C M RAMESH 
  
(a) to (d): Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM) , the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re -skill and up-skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres / institutes under various sc hemes, viz. Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Sikhshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society acro ss the country including Visakhapatnam -
Anakapalli industrial region of Andhra Pradesh. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get 
future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.  
 
Skill development training is being undertaken in Anakapalli and Visakhapatnam districts through 
the existing training ecosystem comprising Government Institutions, State Government 
Universities/Colleges, AICTE -affiliated institutions, ITIs, State Skill De velopment Missions 
(SSDMs), Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), Jan Shikshan Sansthans  (JSSs) and other training 
partners. Further, the schemes of MSDE are demand -driven and the Training Centres (TC) are 
accredited/ affiliated on the basis of the proposal submitted by the Project Implementing Agencies, 
after taking the skill gap into account.  
 
Under PMKVY 4.0, Skill development training is imparted in the Anakapalli-Visakhapatnam region. 
At present, 68 Training Centres are empanelled (including 02 PMKK centres) in the Anakapalli -
Visakhapatnam region. Some of the key sectors covered under PMKVY include Life Sciences, 
IT/ITeS, Logistics, Construction, Electronics & Hardware, Automotive, Capital Goods, 
Hydrocarbon, Power, Green Jobs, Plumbing, Apparel, Healthcare, Tourism & Hospital ity, 
Instrumentation Automation Surveillance and Communication (IASC) and Management.  
 
Under NAPS, no separate Industry linked Skill Development Centre is established, as 
establishments use their existing workplace infrastructure and training facilities. At present, 292 
establishments functional in the Anakapalli -Visakhapatnam region have en gaged 15,142 
apprentices. Under NAPS, apprenticeship opportunities are available across diverse sectors both 
through designated trades and optional trades. Under NAPS, apprentices have been engaged in 
sectors such as Retail, Life Sciences, IT-ITeS, Production and Manufacturing, Electrical, including 
New and Renewable Energy, Automobile, Automotive, Tourism and Hospitality, Fabrication, 
Construction, Electronics, Logistics, BFSI, Power, Agriculture, Furniture and Fittings, Rubber, 
Marine and other allied sectors.  
 
Under JSS, the training is offered in 83 National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) aligned job 
roles in 24 different sectors, varying from Level 2 to Level 4. Some of the popular sectors are 
Apparel Made -Ups & Home Furnishing, Beauty & Wellness, Automo tive, Capital goods, 
Handicrafts & Carpets, Food Processing, Agriculture, Domestic Worker, Electronics & Hardware, 
Plumbing etc. At present, one JSS is functional in Visakhapatnam district. 
 
Under CTS, skill training is imparted through a network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in 170 
NSQF-aligned trades. Each trade has a dedicated course curriculum. The duration of training is six 
months, one year, and two years. The training courses  under CTS are designed to impart basic 
skills and knowledge in the respective trades so as to prepare trainees for wage employment as 
well as self-employment. At present, there are 520 ITIs established in Andhra Pradesh, out of which 
85 are Government and 435 are Private ITIs.  
 
The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) 
scheme aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training in the country. The 
Scheme has a total outlay of Rs. 60,000 crore (Central Share – Rs. 30,000 crore, State Share – 
Rs. 20,000 crore and Industry Share – Rs. 10,000 crore). The scheme comprises of two 
components: 

i.   Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a 
Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital 
content, and new courses aligned to industry needs.  
 
ii.  Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, 
Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting -up sector -specific National Centres of 
Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with glo bal partnership, and 
curriculum development.  
  
The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) 
Scheme is being implemented across States/UTs, including Andhra Pradesh, to upgrade the 
quality and relevance of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). The Nationa l Steering Committee 
(NSC) has approved six (6) Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs) submitted by Anchor Industry 
Partners (AIPs), comprising three from Telangana, one from Odisha, one from Gujarat and one 
from Andhra Pradesh.  
  
The approved Visakhapatnam Cluster comprises one (1) Hub ITI and three (3) Spoke ITIs, with 
ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel (AM/NS India) selected as the Anchor Industry Partner (AIP). As per the 
approved Strategic Implementation Plan (SIP), the focus sectors i nclude Steel & Engineering, 
Ferro Alloys & Metals, Advanced Manufacturing, Automation & Industry 4.0, Electric Vehicles 
(EVs), Renewable Energy, Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering, Petrochemicals, Logistics & Supply 
Chain, IT/Data Centers and Healthcare.  
  
The details of the cluster approved in Andhra Pradesh are as under:

34 States/UTs have constituted their State Steering Committee (SSC) led by Chief Secretary of 
the State/UT, an apex body at the State/UT level for guiding and overseeing the implementation of 
scheme. 23 States/UTs have floated their proposal for inviting the interest of industry. The Scheme 
is proposed to be implemented in a phased manner over a period of five (5) years. 
  
To ensure employment opportunities for the trained youth in the country, including the 
Visakhapatnam-Anakapalli industrial region, the following mechanisms have been adopted by 
MSDE:  
 
i. National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space.  
ii. The Awarding Bodies recognized by NCVET are expected to develop the qualifications as 
per the industry demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National 
Classification of Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations.  
iii. 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have been 
set up which identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as well as to 
determine skill competency standards.  
iv. Directorate General of Training (DGT) under the aegis of MSDE is implementing Flexi MoU 
Scheme and Dual System of Training (DST) which are meant to provide training to ITI 
students in industrial environment as per their requirements.  
v. Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job-roles have been specially aligned with Industry 
4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc. for 
upcoming market demand and industry requirements. 
vi. DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in 
emerging areas such as 5G Network Technician, Artificial Intelligence Programming 
assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, Drone Technician etc.  

vii. DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, CISCO, Microsoft, AWS etc. to 
ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These 
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills training in mod ern 
technologies.  
viii. The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 envisages greater integration of vocational 
education with mainstream education and promotes seamless mobility between academic 
and vocational pathways. In line with this vision, the Apprenticeship Embedded Degree 
Programme (AEDP), developed in collaboration with UGC and AICTE, enables students 
enrolled in degree and diploma programmes to undertake apprenticeship training as an 
integral part of their curriculum. The programme enhances employability, promotes 
outcome-based learning, strengthens industry-academia linkages and facilitates acquisition 
of industry-relevant skills. 
ix. Kaushal Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) are 
organised to facilitate the placements and apprenticeship opportunities to the certified 
candidates.

(a) whether the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) has been operationalised for eligible Central Government 
employees, if so, the details thereof, including the number of employees who have  opted for the

(b) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation and performance of the UPS  since its

associations, pensioners' organisations or other stakeholders seeking replacement,  modification or

(d) whether the Government has examined the feasibility of replacing the Unified Pension  Scheme with 
any alternative pension framework, if so, the details thereof including the alternatives considered and

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE

STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. *207 REGARDING 
“UNIFIED PENSION SCHEME” RAISED BY SHRI JANARDAN SINGH SIGRIWAL, HON’BLE 
MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026. 
 
(a) Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), notified on 24.01.2025, has been introduced as an option under National 
Pension System (NPS)  with the objective of providing assured monthly payout after retirement to the 
Central Government employees covered under the NPS.  UPS was also available to past retirees who 
superannuated or retired on or before 31.03.2025 under NPS and had completed 10 years of regular service, 
as well as to the legally wedded spouse of such eligible deceased retirees. The UPS has been envisaged to 
address the demand of the employees covered under NPS regarding assured pension after retirement while 
ensuring fiscally responsible funded and contributory pension scheme. UPS became effective from 
01.04.2025 and the last date for exercising the option to migrate to UPS was 30.11.2025. The total number 
of employees, including new joinees, ex isting employees and past retirees, who opted for UPS, as on 
19.07.2026 is 1,18,195. 
 
(b) As the scheme has been rolled out w.e.f. 01.04.2025, Government has not reviewed the implementation 
and performance of the UPS as on date.  
(c) Based on the representations from employees and associations, t he cut-off date to opt for UPS was 
extended upto 30.11.2025. The Government extended the benefit of 'Retirement gratuity and Death gratuity' 
under the provisions of the Central Civil Service (Payment of Gra tuity under National Pension System) 
Rules, 2021, to the Central Government employees covered by UPS. Further, the Government employees 
who opted for UPS under NPS shall also be eligible for option for availing benefits under the CCS (Pension) 
Rules, 2021, or the CSS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 2023, in the event of death of the Government 
servant during service or his discharge on the ground of invalidation or disablement. The Government also 
extended tax benefits to UPS as available to NPS. 
Additionally, the Government allowed the Central Government employees, who opted for UPS, one-time 
one-way switch facility to revert to NPS. 
 
(d) & (e) UPS has been introduced as an option under NPS for the employees of Central Government who 
are covered under the NPS. As on date, there is no proposal under consideration  to make any changes or 
replace the UPS.

MANDATORY TEACHER ELIGIBILITY TEST 
 
†*208. Shri Bhausaheb Rajaram Wakchaure: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the job crisis has arisen for experienced teachers appointed prior to 2013 due to the 
condition of mandatory Teacher Eligibility Test (TET), if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to grant a permanent exemption to these experienced teachers 
under Section 23(3) of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the mandatory requirement of the said examination is proposed to be waived off on 
'humanitarian grounds' for teachers who are on the verge of retirement, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government acknowledges the significance of decades of teaching experience 
over any formal eligibility test; and 
(e) the current status of the proposed amendment in Section 23 of the RTE Act to protect the 
interests of experienced teachers? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
 
(a) to (e):  A statement is laid on the table of the House. 
***** 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (E) OF LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 208 FOR REPLY ON 03/08/2026 ASKED BY HON’BLE 
MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT SHRI BHAUSAHEB RAJARAM WAKCHAURE 
REGARDING “MANDATORY TEACHER ELIGIBILITY TEST”. 
(a) to (e): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and the recruitment, 
service conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the 
respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The information regarding 
teachers appointed prior to 2013 who may be affected by the mandatory Teacher Eligibility Test 
(TET) requirement is maintained by the respective State Governments and Union Territory 
Administrations. 
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, vide its judgment dated 01.09.2025, inter alia, held that the 
Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is one of the minimum qualifications prescribed under Section 23 
of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, and is mandatory 
for appointment as a teacher in schools covered under the Act. The order of the Hon'ble Supreme 
Court may be accessed at the following link:  
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2018/36466/36466_2018_9_1501_63764_Judgement_01- 
Sep-2025.pdf. 
Subsequently, while disposing of the review petitions in the matter, vide judgment dated 
29.05.2026 the Hon'ble Supreme Court extended the timeline for acquisition of TET qualification 
from 31.08.2027 to 31.08.2028. The judgment dated 29.05.2026 of the Hon'ble Supreme Court 
may be accessed at the following link: 
https://api.sci.gov.in/supremecourt/2025/53434/53434_2025_7_1501_71637_Judgement_29-
May-2026.pdf. 
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the judgment dated 29.05.2026, has further observed that the 
respective appropriate Governments/authorities should endeavour to conduct the Teacher 
Eligibility Test (TET) periodically, preferably twice every year, with an interval of approximately 
six months between successive examinations, so as to afford eligible teachers a reasonable 
opportunity to comply with the prescribed minimum qualification.

MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ

SANITATION WORKERS UNDER PRIS 
 
 
*21.SHRI MUHAMMED HAMDULLAH SAYEED: 
 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number of sanitation workers engaged under the Panchayati 
Raj Institutions (PRIs) in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep have been disengaged 
following the discontinuation of sanitation activities; 
 
(b) if so, the reasons for the discontinuation of the sanitation programme and the 
disengagement of these workers; 
 
 (c) whether the Government proposes to restore the sanitation programme and re-engage the 
affected workers; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the steps taken or proposed to be taken to strengthen 
sanitation services and ensure livelihood opportunities for the affected workers in 
Lakshadweep? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH) 
 
 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
 
  

2 
 
 
 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
No.*21 ANSWERED ON 21.07.2026 REGARDING “SANITATION WORKERS UNDER 
PRIs” 
 
(a) to (b):   “Panchayat”, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State List 
of Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. Panchayats are set up and operate through 
the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. States/ Union Territories (UTs) have made their own 
Panchayati Raj Act, subject to the provisions of the Constitution. Article 243G of the 
Constitution empowers the Legislature of a State to make provisions, by law, for the 
devolution of power and responsibilities upon Panchayat at appropriate level, subject to such 
conditions as may be specified, with respect to the preparation of plans for economic 
development and social justice and implementation of schemes for economic development 
and social justice as may be entrusted to them including those in relation to matters included 
in the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution. The State legislatures are to consider the 29 
subjects set out in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution of power and responsibilities upon 
Panchayats. One of these 29 subjects includes “Health and sanitation, including hospitals, 
primary health centres and dispensaries”.  
 
Accordingly, all matters relating to Panchayats, including engagement of sanitation 
workers, implementation of the sanitation programme etc. comes under the jurisdiction of the 
State/UT, including UT of Lakshadweep. Powers have been delegated to the Lieutenant 
Governors and Administrators in the Union Territories in respect of various matters.  
 
The UT of Lakshadweep has informed that Sanitation activities have not been 
discontinued in their Union Territory and the UT Administration deployed 332 Multi-Tasking 
Staff/Multi-Skilled Employees for sanitation and waste management activities in place of the 
210 casual labourers previously engaged for this purpose, which is an increase of about 58%.  
 
(c) to (d): The UT of Lakshadweep has informed that sanitation services have been 
continuing uninterrupted across all inhabited islands and the sanitation programme has not 
been discontinued. The engagement of casual labourers has been discontinued from 
31.05.2026 on the deployment of adequate regular manpower. Sanitation services have also 
been strengthened through the deployment of regular staff, ensuring uninterrupted sanitation 
and solid waste management services across all inhabited islands. The existing manpower is 
considered adequate for carrying out sanitation and allied public service functions through the 
Village (Dweep) Panchayats. As per information received from the Department of Drinking 
Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, the UT of Lakshadweep has intimated that their 
all 10 villages are reported to have been 100% covered with Solid Waste Management 
(SWM) arrangements and Liquid Waste Management (LWM) arrangements and have been 
declared as Open Defecation Free (ODF) Plus (Model).

The Ministry of MSME launched Udyam Registration Portal on

industrial units including MSMEs undertaki ng new investments or

Industries and Export Corporation (PSIEC) which has developed 52 
Industrial Focal Points across the state.

manufacturing. As per the data in latest ASI report, number of factories 
in manufacturing industries increased from 12726 in 2017-18 to 13166 
in 2023-24 in the State of Punjab. 
The Government has launched Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
Schemes for 14 key sectors (including Textile Products: MMF segment 
and technical textiles) with an approved financial outlay of ₹1.91 lakh

employment generation of over 14.15  lakh (direct and indirect) in the 
country (including Punjab). 
 
 

 
A total of 1.47 crore credit guarantees amounting to ₹14.69 lakh 
crore have been extended to MSEs across the country (including 
Punjab), including manufacturing units, since inception in 2000 till 
30.06.2026 under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small 
Enterprises (CGTMSE).

Scheme notified on 10.04.2026 for development of investment -ready 
industrial parks in the country (including Punjab) to enable investors

capacity. The total financial outlay for the Scheme is ₹ 33,660 crore 
and the duration of the Scheme is for a period of 6 years. Under the 
Scheme, financial assistance is available for the development of 100 
industrial parks.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

ANSWERED ON 03/08/2026 
 
EXPANSION OF ACADEMIC ASSISTANCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
†*212. Shri Ram Shiromani Verma: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
a) whether the Government proposes to expand the scope of scholarships, hostels, digital 
education and other academic assistance in higher education to support students belonging 
to economically weaker families who are unable to pursue higher education due to financial 
hardships and if so, the details thereof; and 
b) whether the Government is contemplating any time -bound action plan in this regard and if  
so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI) 
 
(a) and (b): A statement is laid on the table of the House 
 
*** 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (A) AND (B) OF THE LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 212 FOR REPLY ON 03.08.2026 ASKED BY SHRI RAM 
SHIROMANI VERMA, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAM ENT REGARDING 
EXPANSION OF ACADEMIC ASSISTANCE IN HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
(a) and (b): The National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasizes access, equity, affordability 
and inclusion in higher education. The Government is committed to ensuring equitable access to 
quality higher education for all students, particularly those belonging to eco nomically weaker 
families. 
The Government is implementing various scholarship schemes for providing financial assistance to 
eligible students for pursuing higher education, as per  scheme guidelines. The Post -Matric 
scholarship schemes for SC, ST and OBC are Centrally Sponsored Schemes being implemented by 
States and UTs and administered by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment  and Ministry 
of Tribal Affairs. Under these scholarship schemes, the benefits are extended to all the students 
belonging to SC, ST and OBC, subject to their parental income ceiling and as per scheme guidelines. 
Department of Higher Education (D oHE) implements the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha 
Protsahan (PM-USP) Yojana comprising of scholarship schemes namely (i) PM-USP Central Sector 
Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students; and (ii) PM-USP Special Scholarship 
Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh , to provide financial assistance for pursuing higher 
education to eligible students belonging to economically weaker families, as per scheme guidelines.  
In FY 2025-26, the Central Government has provided about 1.09 crore scholarships for pursuing 
Post-Matric and Higher Education. This includes about 36 lakh scholarships for Other Backward 
Classes (OBC), Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) and Denotified Tribes (DNT) students; about 
48 lakh scholarships for Scheduled Castes (SC) students; and about 24 lakh scholarships for 
Scheduled Tribes (ST) students.  
 
The Government, to make higher education affordable in institutions like Indian Institutes of 
Technology (IITs) and National Institutes of Technology (NITs), is providing relaxation in tuition 
fee to students from economically and socially weaker sections of the society. From AY 2016 -17, 
the complete fee waiver is being provided for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and PwD students 
and economically backward students (whose family income is less than ₹ 1 lakh per annum), and 
also 2/3rd remission of fee for  other economically backward students (whose family income is 
between ₹ 1 lakh to ₹ 5 lakh per annum). The 31 NITs & IIEST - Shibpur are also providing 100% 
tuition fee waiver to students belonging to SC/ST/PH category to pursue postgraduate (M.E./ 
M.Tech.) programmes in their institutions. 
The Government has supported the creation and expansion of infrastructure, including hostel 
facilities, in Higher Educational Institutions through the Higher Education Financing Agency 

(HEFA), which provides financial assistance for infrastructure development in eligible institutions. 
As on March 2026, HEFA, since its inception in 2017 has disbursed loans worth ₹ 24,977.62 crores 
to different Centrally Funded Institutions (CFIs). 
The Central Universities create additional hostel infrastructure from time to time to meet students' 
accommodation requirements. The Central Government supports development of university 
infrastructure, including hostels, through Grant -in-Aid and funding f rom Higher Education 
Financing Agency (HEFA). It may be noted that during FY 2013-14, ₹ 5,603.79 crore was released 
as grant to Central Universities. From FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, ₹ 1,13,943.55 crore was released 
to Central Universities. During the year 2 026-27, an amount of ₹ 17,440 crore has been allocated. 
These funds are utilized by the Universities for meeting their academic, administrative and 
infrastructural requirements in accordance with their priorities. 
Further, the Government of India in the Union Budget 2026–27, has proposed for establishment of 
one Girls' Hostel in every district to improve access to higher education, particularly in STEM 
institutions, and to create affordable hostel capacity as core academic access infrastructure . The 
share of female students in STEM enrolment has also shown a steady improvement over the years, 
rising from 38.4% in 2014-15 to 44% in 2023-24 (AISHE data 2023-24), reflecting growing gender 
inclusivity in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics education in the country. 
The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP - 2020) envisions a transformative approach to digital 
education, aiming to leverage technology to provide high -quality, accessible and equitable 
education for all. The policy promotes the integration of digital tools, resources, and platforms into 
the education system. To achieve NEP 2020 aims and objective, Ministry of Education implements 
“National Mission on Education through Information and Communication Technology 
(NMEICT)”. The scheme aims to leverage the potential of ICT in all processes of education. Under 
the NMEICT scheme, Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM) 
platform has been initiated to provide free access to courses from premier institutions. There have 
been more than 20,000 deliveries of courses on the platform, with cumulative enrolments exceeding 
6 crores since its inception. Further, to enhance industry -academia collaboration and improve 
employability of learners, the Ministry of Education has launched multilingual SWAYAM Plus 
platform. As of July 2026, the platform offers more than 500 industry -aligned courses across 15 
sectors in collaboration with 89 industry partners.  
The Department of Higher Education, in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, has started SATHEE (Self-
Assessment, Test & Help for Entrance Examination) portal in November 2023, to provide access to 
quality education for competitive examination such as JEE, NEET, CUET, ICAR, SSC and IBPS 
etc. The platform provides free educational content and guidance from premier institutions for the 

competitive exams to all learners, including economically and socially weaker sections. More than 
21 lakh learners have registered on the platform so far. 
Further, the Government has launched the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) initiative to 
provide nationwide access to scholarly journals for students of eligible higher educational and 
research institutions, thereby strengthening access to quality academi c resources. The One Nation 
One Subscription (ONOS) Scheme provides access to over 13,000 journals from 32 publishers to 
all eligible institutions. 7499 higher education institutions (HEIs) and research and development 
(R&D) institutions are covered under ONOS. 
In addition, the Government of India has launched the PM-Vidyalaxmi, a new central sector scheme 
in November 2024, with the objective to ensure that no student is denied the opportunity to pursue 
higher education due to financial constraints. Under the sch eme, collateral-free and guarantor-free 
education loan is provided to all the students, who get merit-based admission in top Quality Higher 
Education Institutions (QHEIs) and who desire to avail the education loan and there is no upper 
limit for this. Further, for students with annual family income up to ₹ 8 lakh, the scheme provides 
3% interest subvention on education loans up to ₹ 10 lakhs. Since the launch of this scheme on 
6th November 2024 till 21st July 2026, 1,12,817 collateral-free and guarantor-free PM Vidyalaxmi 
education loans have been sanctioned. The amount sanctioned is ₹ 15,634.78 crore.  
Further, the Department of Higher Education is implementing the PM -USP Central Sector Interest 
Subsidy Scheme. Under the PM USP -CSIS Scheme, full interest subvention is provided to all 
students who are pursuing technical/professional courses from NAAC accredited Institutions or 
professional/ technical programmes accredited by NBA or Institutions of National Importance or 
Central Funded Technical Institutions (CFTIs) and whose annual family income is up to ₹ 4.5 lakhs 
for loans up to Rs. 10 lakhs, during the  moratorium period. There is no upper limit on number of 
student beneficiaries for this Scheme.  
Moreover, under the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme 
for Education Loans (PM-USP CGFSEL) of the Central Government, credit guarantee is provided 
for education loans sanctioned up to ₹ 7.5 lakhs. The guarantee cover is  up to 75% of outstanding 
default. Further, under the model education loan scheme of the Indian Banks’ Association, the 
repayment period for education loan is up to 15 years after moratorium period (course year plus one 
year).  
Thus, PM Vidyalaxmi, PM -USP CSIS and PM USP CGFSEL schemes, along with the various 
scholarships together provide holistic support to all deserving students to pursue higher education. 

As a result of these cumulative initiatives, India’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education 
increased from 23.7 in 2014 –15 to 30 in 2023 –24. Female GER rose from 22.9 to 31.2 during the 
same period. SC GER has increased by 8.9 points and ST GER has increased by 9.3 points from 
2014–15 to 2023–24. The rise in GER has been accompanied by significant growth in student 
enrolment, with total higher education enrolment increasing from 3.42 crore in 2014 –15 to 4.50 
crore in 2023–24, adding more than 1.08 crore students to the higher education system.

 the details of steps being taken by the Government to check

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *213 FOR REPLY ON 03.08.2026 RAISED BY SHRI 
CHHOTELAL REGARDING MIGRATION OF WORKERS FROM UTTAR 
PRADESH. 
 
   The Central Government in coordination with State 
Governments is implementing various schemes for creating 
employment opportunities and encouraging self-employment so that 
people earn their livelihood near thei r places of residence. These 
include Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin), Aajeevika-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), Pt. 
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushlya Yojana (DDU -GKY), Rural

Programme (PMEGP), PM Vishwakarma Scheme, Production -Linked

Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana  (PMVBRY), to name a few. 
 
Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one-stop 
solution for providing career related services including jobs from 
private and government sectors, in formation on online & offline job 
fairs, job search & matching, career counselling, vocational 
guidance, information on skill development courses, skill/training 
programmes etc. through a digital platform [www.ncs.gov.in].  
 
 Further, State Government of UP has taken various initiative 
such as One district One product Yojana, Vishwakarma Shram  
Samman Yojana,  Kaushal Vikas   and Kaushal Unnayan  program, 
Rojgar Mela, increase in minimum wages, social security schemes, 
registration of building workers with BoCW Welfare Board and provide 
education, health, pension,  maternity benefits etc.  
 
In order to safeguard the interests of the migrant workers  
the Central Government had enacted the Inter -state Migrant  
Workmen (Regulation of  Employment and Conditions of Service) 
Act,1979. This Act has now been subsumed in the Occupational 
Safety, Health and the Working Conditions (OSH) Code. The OSH 
Code provides for decent working conditions, minimum wages, toll 
free helpline number, benefits of Public Distribution System, journey 
allowance once in a year, Migrant worker is eligible to avail all the 
benefits which is available to a regular worker of that establishment 
including benefits of ESIC, EPFO and other benefits etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 214 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 3, 2026/ SHRAVANA 12, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL AND GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLES  
*214: DR. SAMBIT PATRA: 
Will the Minister of Finance be pleased to state: 
a) the action plan being implemented to promote ESG (Environmental, Social and 
Governance) Principles; 
b) Whether any regulatory mechanism has been evolved to prevent violations of the Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) standards implemented by the 
Government in respect of ESG, if so, the details thereof; 
c) Whether the Government has introduced a strict regulatory framework to curb misleading 
marketing strategies such as ‘purpose washing’, wherein certain companies falsely project 
a commitment to ESG standards, if so, the details thereof; and 
d) the steps taken by the Government towards the regulation and standardisation of ESG rating 
agencies in alignment with international standards, along with the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
FINANCE MINISTER 
(SMT. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN) 
 
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 214 RAISED BY DR. SAMBIT PATRA, HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 REGARDING ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL 
AND GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLES. 
(a ) and (b): Vide Circular dated May 10, 2021, SEBI has prescribed disclosure on ESG 
parameters based on the nine principles of National Guidelines on Responsible Business 
Conduct (NGRBCs), as formulated by MCA, under the Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report (BRSR). BRSR reporting is mandatory as part of the Annual Report for 
the top 1000 listed companies based on the Market Capitalization w.e.f. FY 2022-23. SEBI has 
designated the Stock Exchanges to act as first-level regulators for monitoring disclosures made 
by the listed companies. In case of receipt of any complaint regarding disclosures, the same is 
examined, and appropriate action can be initiated by SEBI, wherever necessary.  
 
(c ) SEBI has issued a Circular regarding ESG debt securities which defines purpose-washing 
as “ making false, misleading, unsubstantiated, or otherwise incomplete claims about the 
purpose for which bonds are issued”. SEBI has prescribed safeguards against purpose-washing 
for issuers of ESG debt securities under the NCS (Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations and 
the relevant SEBI Circulars. Issuers are required to utilise proceeds only for the specified 
eligible purp oses, continuously monitor and disclose whether the funded activities are 
achieving the environmental, social and/or sustainability objectives envisaged in the offer 
document, quantify negative externalities, and disclose any deviations to investors, inclu ding 
undertaking early redemption where required by a majority of debenture holders. 
Further, issuers are required to prevent purpose-washing by not using misleading labels, hiding 
trade-offs, cherry-picking data, or making false claims of third-party certification, and maintain 
the highest standards associated with the issue while adhering to the assigned rating. The issuer 
of ESG debt Securities shall  also appoint an independent third-party reviewer/ certifier to 
undertake the activities and responsibilities as specified. 
 
(d) With a view to foster the ESG financing ecosystem in India, SEBI introduced a regulatory 
framework for ESG Rating Providers (ERPs) through the amendment of the SEBI (Credit 
Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999, and the subsequent issuance of a Master Circular. Under 
this framework, regis tration with SEBI is mandatory for any entity to act as an ESG rating 
provider. To ensure transparency, regulations mandate detailed disclosures of the rationale 
behind each assigned rating, enabling stakeholders to assess the underlying factors. Currently , 
there are 19 ERPs registered with SEBI.

Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:

Tourism Circuit covering Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao districts of 
Assam; 
(b) whether any proposal in this regard has been received from the State 
Government of Assam or the Autonomous Councils of the said districts; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to provide Central financial 
assistance for the development of ropeways, eco -resorts, homestays, 
adventure tourism and interpretation centres in the said districts; and 
(d) the details of the Central schemes under which such projects may be 
sanctioned along with the eligibility criteria for getting assistance 
thereunder? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM             (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)

QUESTION NO.*215 ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 REGARDING DEVELOPMENT 
OF TRIBAL TOURISM CIRCUIT IN ASSAM RAISED BY SHRI AMARSING TISSO 
 
(a) to (d): Identification, development and promotion of tourist 
destinations, including tribal tourism circuit is primarily undertaken by the 
concerned State Government  (SG) /Union T erritory Administration (UTA). 
However, the Ministry of Tourism through its schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan 
(SD)’, ‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination 
Development (CBDD)’, a sub-scheme of SD2.0, and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation 
and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the 
efforts of tourism infrastructure development by extending financial 
assistance to the SGs/UTAs.  
 
The projects under the above Schemes are sanctioned subject to 
adherence to the scheme guidelines, submission of Detailed Project Reports 
(DPRs) by SG/UTA, availability of funds, Government directions, inter -se 
priority etc. Details of the projects sanctioned under these schemes of 
Ministry of Tourism in the state of Assam is annexed . In 2024 -25, 
Government of India has also sanctioned the projects ‘Assam State Zoo Cum 
Botanical Garden in Guwahati’ for ₹97.12 Crore and ‘Beautification o f Rang 
Ghar in Sivasagar’ for ₹94.76 Crore in the State of Assam under the initiative 
‘Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development 
of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale’. 
 
In addition, during the financial year 2025-26, the Ministry has initiated 
'Development of Homestays in Tribal Areas' under Dharti Aaba Janjatiya 
Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA – JGUA) scheme as a part of Swadesh Darshan 

2.0 to promote community-based tourism and sustainable livelihoods in tribal 
areas and has sanctioned 5 projects in five states for an amount of ₹17.52 
Crore. 
 
The Swadesh Darshan Scheme was initially designed for the integrated 
development of thematic tourism circuits. The same had been revamped as 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 adopting a destination -centric approach with a focus 
on developing sustainable and responsible tourism destinations to enhance 
visitor experience and effective destination management. 
 
While, submission of proposals by the State Government/Autonomous 
Councils through the State Government  (SG), is a continuous process, no 
proposal specific to Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao districts of Assam is 
presently under consideration of the Ministry of Tourism. 
 
Ministry of Tourism does not operate a separate, dedicated central 
sector scheme exclusively for ropeways, eco -resorts, adventure tourism or 
interpretation centres. However, such components have been part of project 
sanctioned by the Ministry for SGs/UTAs. Further, the Ministry has also 
formulated separate National Strategies fo r Eco -tourism and Adventure 
Tourism, which provide the broader policy framework for such interventions.

(a) & (b): A “Foreign Company” has been defined under sub-section (42) of 
Section 2 of the Companies Act, 2013. A “foreign company” means any 
company or body corporate incorporated outside India which (a) has a 
place of business in India whether by itself or through an agent, physically 
or through electronic mode; and (b) conducts any business activity in India 
in any other manner.  
Foreign companies register under Section 380 of the Companies Act, 2013 
as a Branch Office, Liaison Office and Project office. Many foreign body 
corporates also have Indian subsidiaries which are incorporated in India 
under section 7 of the Companies Act, 2013. The details of Foreign 
Companies as well as Indian subsidiaries of foreign body corporates

years are at Annexure.  
  
The closing of operations is a matter of commercial business decision. It 
depends on a host of factors such as viability of operations, sectoral 
strategy, global priorities, market size, capital and resource allocation 
within the company as well as the decision of a particular business entity 
whether to operate in different geographical areas or not.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 03RD AUGUST, 2026 
 
NCS PORTAL 
 
 
 *217.    SMT. KAMALJEET SEHRAWAT: 
              SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI: 
 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the Memorandum of Understandings (MOUs) signed 
by the Government with private and Government partners to 
improve the service offering of the National Career Service (NCS); 
 
(b) the list of upgraded features and actual employment generated 
under the NCS portal; 
 
(c) the details of the role played by Model Career Centres (MCCs) in 
promoting the usage of NCS portal; 
 
(d) whether all the State Employment Exchanges/State Career 
Services have been digitised and integrated with the NCS portal; 
and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT  
(DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA) 
 
 
(a) to (e):  A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
* 
 
 
 
 

 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. *217 DUE FOR REPLY ON 03.08.2026 BY SMT. 
KAMALJEET SEHRAWAT AND SHRI PRATAP CHANDRA SARANGI  
REGARDING “NCS PORTAL” 
 
(a) to (e):  The Ministry has signed several Memoranda of Understanding 
(MoUs) with public and private employers/portals/platforms to strengthen 
public–private partnerships to expand employment opportunities for 
jobseekers. Till date, more than 40 MoUs have been signed with partners 
such as APNA, Swiggy, Rapido, Zomato, Amazon, TCS iON, Quikr and 
FoundIt (Monster), among others. These partnerships facilitate the 
integration of employment opportunities and services with the NCS 
Portal, including vacancy aggregation, orga nisation of job fairs, skill 
development programmes, career counselling and other employment -
related support services. 
 
NCS portal is also integrated with various Government  portals such 
as Udyam, eShram, Skill India Digital Hub , EPFO, ESIC, MHRD,  
DigiLocker, etc. and has  linkages with  Government recruitment bodies 
like Union Public Service Commission,  Staff Selection Commission, 
Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board,  Railway Recruitment Boards 
etc.  
 
The NCS Portal has been upgraded to a cloud -based, open -
architecture platform, and its enhancement is a continuous and dynamic 
process. Improvements and updates are undertaken in line with evolving 
requirements, leveraging the latest available technologies. These  
upgrades include integration with various public and private job and skill 
portals, enhanced AI -powered features  (including intelligent job 
matching, AI skill gap analysis, personalized job recommendations, AI 
interview coach, multilingual support through Bhasini, etc), cloud-based 
applications for jobseekers and employers, robust verification 
mechanisms, and the launch of a mobile application to improve 
accessibility and user experience. 
 
The NCS Portal brings together Jobseekers and employers on one 
platform to facilitate job opportunities and career related services to the 
Jobseekers of the country. However, notifying final hiring figures is not 
a mandatory requirement on NCS portal.  
  
 

The NCS project also, inter alia,  envisaged setting up of Model 
Career Centres (MCCs) through transformation of Employment 
Exchanges in the country to deliver career related services such as 
organizing online/ offline job fairs, mobilize the employers, provide online/ 
offline career counselling at local level etc. in collaboration with State 
and other institutions to the jobseekers and employers through outreach 
activities. Till date, the Government has approved 407 Model Career 
Centres (MCCs), which also includes 370 Employment Exchanges,  that 
have been upgraded as MCCs. 
 
Further, as on date, 31 States/UTs have been integrated with the 
NCS portal including 8 States/UTs which are directly using NCS Portal.

*219. SHRI YOGENDER CHANDOLIA: 
SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has undertaken major initiatives 
during the last twelve years to improve the flow of credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
across the country; 
(b) if so, the State-wise details thereof, specifically in the Pali Lok Sabha Constituency in Rajasthan; 
(c) whether the Government has operationalised Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 
5.0 and if so, the details of additional credit flow targeted thereunder, including guarantee coverage 
for MSMEs and support to the aviation sector; 
(d) the details of the number of MSME units provided with loans, guarantees and other financial 
assistance through SIDBI and the ECLGS in Ratlam, Jhabua and Alirajpur districts of Madhya Pradesh 
during the last two years, district-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government is implementing any special scheme to provide accessible credit to MSME

ANSWER 
THE FINANCE MINISTER  
(SMT. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN)

***** 
 
  

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (e) OF LOK SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. *219 ANSWERED ON 03rd AUGUST, 2026, REGARDING 
‘CREDIT FLOW TO MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES’ BY SHRI 
YOGENDER CHANDOLIA AND SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY, HON’BLE MEMBERS OF 
PARLIAMENT 
(a) Major initiatives undertaken by Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to improve 
credit flow are illustrated as follows: - 
i. Indirect Lending:  
Financial assistance through refinance and onlending is extended to Banks, NBFCs, SFBs and MFIs 
which is used by these institutions for financing of MSMEs. This creates a multiplier effect and 
increases the flow of credit to MSMEs. As on 31.03.2026, the total indirect lending portfolio of SIDBI 
is ₹5.24 Lakh crore. 
ii. Direct Lending:  
 Branch Banking: Financial loan assistance is extended to MSMEs directly through SIDBI 
branch network of 167 branches. Additionally, microlending is undertaken through specific 
schemes by leveraging the network of partner institutions where loans are facilitated to business 
entities, especially small and women entrepreneurs. 
 Lending through Partnerships  
- Micro lending– Additionally, microlending is undertaken through specific schemes by 
leveraging the network of partner institutions where loans are facilitated to business 
entities, especially small and women entrepreneurs.      
- Co-lending: The Bank launched a product on co-lending arrangement with NBFCs and 
RRBs to provide affordable credit to smaller MSMEs, especially new borrowers, as part of 
its effort to reach underserved/unserved MSMEs. 
 Digital Lending  
- GST Sahay: SIDBI launched a GST Sahay app for ‘on tap’ invoice-based (cash flow based) 
small value credit to micro enterprises using trade data and digital frameworks.  
- TReDS: SIDBI is participating in all the 5 TReDS platform to provide timely finance to 
MSMEs. 
iii. SIDBI Cluster Development Fund (SCDF):  
To promote cluster development, SCDF has been setup to provide low-cost funding to State 
Governments for Infrastructure Development in MSME Clusters. 
iv. Sectoral Development work/ Coordination Among Stakeholders  

To modernise rural non-farm enterprises and improve their productivity and competitiveness, SIDBI 
is implementing the Modernization of Rural Enterprises (MoRE) Programme, which provides both 
financial assistance and capacity-building support through a cluster-based approach. 
(b) As informed by SIDBI, the state-wise data in respect of refinance to Banks is not maintained by 
SIDBI. Hence, state-wise data for the entire refinance portfolio of SIDBI to various lending institutions 
is not available. However, state-wise details of direct credit provided by SIDBI to MSMEs over the 
last five years are placed at Annexure I. Lok Sabha Constituency- wise data is not maintained. Data 
pertaining to direct credit of Pali district of Rajasthan is placed at Annexure II. 
(c) The Government has introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 in May, 
2026. Under the scheme, MSMEs are eligible for additional credit up to 20% of the peak fund-based 
working capital outstanding during the fourth quarter of FY 2025–26. The scheme provides 100% 
guarantee coverage to Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) towards the amount in default for such 
additional credit facility extended to the eligible MSME borrowers. For the scheduled passenger 
airlines, the guarantee coverage is 90%. However, the scheduled passenger airlines are eligible for 
additional credit up to 100% of the total peak credit outstanding (both fund-based and non-fund-based) 
during the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26. Under the scheme, additional credit flow of ₹ 2,55,000 crore 
is envisaged for MSMEs, non-MSMEs and scheduled passenger airlines. 
(d) The details of direct credit provided by SIDBI to MSMEs and details of guarantees issued to 
MSMEs under ECLGS 5.0 in Ratlam, Jhabua and Alirajpur districts of Madhya Pradesh are placed at 
Annexure III. 
(e) As informed by Ministry of Tribal Affairs, National Scheduled Tribe Finance and Development 
Corporation (NSTFDC), an apex organization under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, provides 
concessional financial assistance to eligible Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries for undertaking income 
generating activities and self-employment. The major schemes implemented include Term Loan 
Scheme, Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana (AMSY), Micro Credit Scheme for Self Help Groups 
(MCF) and Adivasi Shiksha Rrinn Yojana (ASRY). These schemes provide financial support for 
income generation, entrepreneurship development and education of Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries. 
Further, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs launched the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-
ST) in 2024 to promote entrepreneurship among Scheduled Tribe communities through concessional

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026 
 
DEVELOPMENT AND PROMOTION OF TOURIST DESTINATIONS IN MEHSANA 
 
*220.  SHRI HARIBHAI PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the potential of developing 
Modhera Sun Temple, Thol Lake Bird Sanctuary, Taranga Hills, Dharoi 
Dam, Sharmistha Talav and Kirti Toran, Vadnagar as an integrated 
heritage, pilgrimage and eco-tourism circuit in Mehsana district; 
(b) if so, the details of the tourism infrastructure created or proposed at 
these destinations, including last -mile connectivity, visitor amenities, 
interpretation centres, signage, parking and digital tourist facilities; 
(c) whether any proposal has been received from the State Government of 
Gujarat for the integrated development, conservation and promotion of 
the said tourist destinations under any Central tourism scheme; 
(d) the details of the financial assistance sanctioned, released and utilised 
for tourism infrastructure and heritage conservation in Mehsana district 
during the last three years; and 
(e) the details of the steps taken by the Government to promote the said 
destinations through domestic and international tourism campaigns? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM   (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e):  A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
 
****** 

STATEMENT IN REPLY TO PARTS ( A) TO ( E) OF LOK SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO.*220 ANSWERED ON 03.08.2026  REGARDING DEVELOPMENT 
AND PROMOTION OF TOURIST DESTINATIONS IN MEHSAN A RAISED BY SHRI 
HARIBHAI PATEL 
 
(a) to (e): Development and promotion of tourism including assessment of 
potential of destinations including Modhera  Sun Temple, Thol Lake Bird 
Sanctuary, Taranga Hills, Dharoi Dam, Sharmistha Talav and Kirti Toran, 
Vadnagar, is primarily done by the concerned State Government (SG)/UT 
Administration (UTA). However, Ministry of Tourism under its various schemes 
such as S wadesh Darshan (SD), Swadesh Darshan 2.0 (SD2.0), Challenge 
Based Destination Development (CBDD) – an initiative under Swadesh Darshan 
and Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Heritage Augmentation Drive 
(PRASHAD) etc. provides financial assistance for de velopment of tourism 
infrastructure and experiences in the country, to the SGs/UTAs, on receipt of 
the project proposals from them, in synergy with the scheme guidelines, 
Government directions, availability of funds, inter-se priority etc. 
 
The Swadesh Darshan Scheme was initially designed for the integrated 
development of thematic tourism circuits. The same had been revamped as 
Swadesh Darshan 2.0 adopting a destination-centric approach with a focus on 
developing sustainable and responsible tourism destinations to enhance 
visitor experience and effective destination management. 
 
Further, the Government of India under its ‘Special Assistance to States 
for Capital Investment (SASCI) – Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to 
Global Scale’ has also sanctioned projects in the country in Financial Year 

2024-25, with the primary objective to comprehensively develop iconic tourist 
centres in the country, branding and marketing them at global scale. 
 
The details of the projects sanctioned under SD, CBDD, SASCI and 
PRASHAD schemes in the State of Gujarat is annexed. 
 
Further, the State Government of Gujarat has informed that they have 
assessed the potential of developing said locations as an integrated heritage, 
pilgrimage and eco -tourism circuit in Mehsana district and destinations i.e. 
Modhera Sun Temple, Thol Lake Bird Sanctuary, Taranga Hills, Dharoi Dam, 
Sharmistha Talav, Kirti Toran and Vadnagar. These destinations have 
adequate last-mile connectivity with well -developed approach pathways for 
easy access, sufficient directional and informat ional signage, adequate 
parking facilities, and essential visitor amenities. 
 
A wide range of tourism infrastructure and visitor amenities have been 
approved under the Ministry of Tourism's central sector schemes in different 
destinations in the state of Gujarat. These amenities includes tourist 
facilitation and interpretation centr es, visitor reception facilities, heritage 
conservation and area development, pathways and promenades, approach 
roads and last -mile connectivity, parking facilities, wayfinding and 
informational signage, illumination and façade lighting of heritage structures, 
landscaping and beautification, amphitheatres and cultural spaces, cafeterias,

(a): The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is mainly implemented on ‘Area 
Approach’ basis wherein claims are worked out on the area of the land parcel based on 
the shortfall in actual yield of the crop insured, submitted by the State Government 
concerned, on the basis of Crop Cutting Experiment (CCE) as well as technology based 
yield estimated under YES-TECH, vis-à-vis threshold yield, as per the formula in the 
Operational Guidelines of the scheme. In case of no shortfall in yield, no claims become 
payable. 
 
As per the information received from the State Government, no discrepancy has 
been found in CCE data. Conduct of CCEs through CCE Agri App has been made 
mandatory since Kharif 2025 and accordingly, in 2025-26, 96% of CCEs were done 
through CCE agri app in Uttar Pradesh to ensure transparency and efficiency. Further, to 
ensure correctness and reliability of the CCEs, field inspections are done by Agriculture 
and Revenue Department officials.  
 
In order to reduce dependency on manual Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs), YES-
TECH (Yield Estimation System Based on Technology) is being implemented w.e.f. Kharif 
2023  for Objective Crop Damage & Loss Assessment and transparency and for gradual 
migration to Remote-Sensing based yield estimation to help in fair and accurate Crop Yield 
Estimation.  Mandatory 30% weightage to yield estimation has been assigned to YES-
TECH derived yield. Uttar Pradesh has implemented YESTECH with 50% weightage in 
2025-26.

STATEMENT REFERRED TO PART (a) TO (e) OF LOK SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO.  25 FOR 21ST JULY, 2026  REGARDING PENDING CLIAMS OF PMFBY 
 
(a) : The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) and Restructured Weather Based 
Crop Insurance Scheme (RWBCIS) is mainly implemented on ‘Area Approach’ basis 
wherein season end claims are worked based on the shortfall in actual yield vis-à-vis 
threshold yield as submitted by the State Government concerned on National Crop 
Insurance Portal (NCIP) and as per the formula in the Operational Guidelines of the 
scheme.  Enrolled farmer has no need to file the claims.  Claims of enrolled and eligible 
farmers are automatically worked out based on the shortfall in yield as reported by the 
State Government concerned.   
 
However, losses due to localized risks of hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloud 
burst & natural fire and post-harvest losses due to cyclone, cyclonic/unseasonal rains & 
hailstorms are calculated on individual insured farm basis. The extent of loss and claims 
in such case are assessed by a joint committee comprising representatives of State 
Government and concerned insurance company within stipulated timeframe under the 
Operational Guidelines of the scheme.  In this case, farmers have to intimate the loss 
within 72 hours of the loss by calling on the toll-free number i.e. 14447. In addition to the 
same, intimation can also be given on crop insurance app, to the State Government, 
insurance company, concerned bank/financial institutions, etc.  
 
Details of claims reported, paid and pending from 2021-22 to 2025-26 under 
PMFBY and RWBCIS in the States of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra (as on 
30.06.2026) are given below: 
(Rs. in crore) 
State  Claims Reported Claims Paid Claims Pending 
Madhya Pradesh 7,716.17  6,374.14 1,342.03 
Maharashtra 27,513.15  27,289.82 223.24 
 
(b):  Yes Sir, timelines are fixed for each and every activity including settlement of claims 
under the scheme and has been duly provided in the Operational Guidelines of the 
scheme. 
 
State Governments are required to upload the notified area and crop wise yield 
based on Crop Cutting Experiments (CCE) as well as technology based yield estimated 
under YES-TECH on the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP), subsequent to which the 
Insurance Companies accept the same leading to calculation of claims on the NCIP. The 
Insurance company has to settle the claims within 21 days from calculation of claims on 
NCIP wherever premium subsidy has been received by them from Government of India 
and concerned State Governments. 
 
In order to rigorously monitor claim disbursal process, a dedicated module namely 
‘Digiclaim Module’ has been operationalized for payment of claims from Kharif 2022 
onwards.  It involves integration of National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) with Public 
Finance Management System (PFMS) and accounting system of Insurance Companies to 
provide timely & transparent processing of all claims. 

 
(c) : Since the scheme is implemented by the State Government, therefore, in order to 
resolve the grievances/complaints including those related to claims of insured farmers, 
provision of Stratified Grievance Redressal Mechanism viz. District Level Grievance 
Redressal Committee (DGRC), State Level Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) has 
been made in the Revised Operational Guidelines of the Scheme.    These committees 
have been given the detailed mandate as outlined in the Operational Guidelines for hearing 
the complaints/ grievances   and to dispose them as per the stipulated procedure. 
    
To further facilitate the grievance redressal mechanism, Krishi Rakshak Portal and 
Helpline (KRPH) has been developed.  A single Pan-India toll free number 14447 has been 
deployed and linked to the insurance companies’ database, where farmers can raise their 
grievances/issues.  Timelines to resolve these grievances/issues have also been fixed.   
 
(d) : The PMFBY envisages adoption of improved technology in implementation of the 
scheme.  Accordingly, YES-TECH (Yield Estimation System Based on Technology) is 
being implemented w.e.f. Kharif 2023 for Objective Crop Damage & Loss Assessment and 
transparency and for gradual migration to Remote-Sensing based yield estimation to help 
in  fair and accurate Crop Yield Estimation. This initiative has been launched for paddy & 
wheat crops from Kharif 2023 and Soybean crop from Kharif 2024 season wherein 
mandatory 30% weightage to yield estimation has been assigned to YES-TECH derived 
yield.    However, State Government of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra has given 100% 
and 50% weightage respectively to YES-TECH based yield in 2025-26.    
 
(e): As per timelines given in the Operational Guidelines of the scheme, insurance 
companies have to settle the claims within 21 Days from calculation of claims on National 
Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP) and receipt of premium subsidy by Insurance Companies. 
In case payment is not made as per timelines mentioned above penalty of 12% is auto 
calculated and levied through NCIP w.e.f. Kharif 2024 season. In the last year, the claims 
have been paid within prescribed timelines except in cases such as yield disputes between 
State Governments and Insurance Companies, error in applicants’ bank account details, 
pendency of premium subsidy from State Government.

Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:

(a)  whether the Ministry proposes any specific incentives for Foundry-Engineering 
and Textile  manufacturing units to occupy underutilized lands in Kolhapur's

addressing stalled industrial development and lack of local manufacturing jobs; 
 
(b)  the current status of land in these industrial areas along with the total allo tted

medium-scale engineering and foundry industries in the Kolhapur industrial

STARRED QUESTION NO. 26 FOR ANSWER ON 21.07.2026. 
 
(a) to (d): Industries is a State subject. Both the Central Government and the State 
Governments implement various policies and programmes to create an 
enabling eco -system for the development of the industrial sector in the 
country. 
As reported by the Government of Maharashtra, there are 08 industrial 
areas in Kolhapur district namely Shiroli, Gokul Shirgaon, Gokul Shirgaon 
(Isolated), Kagal Hatkanangale Five Star, Gadhinglaj, Ajara, Halkarni  and 
I.T. Park, Kolhapur. Against the total allotted area of 1,159.06 hectare, 2866 
units are operational, providing reported employment to 64,741 persons. 
The Government of Maharashtra has further informed that the following 
industrial areas have been de-notified: 
Bhudargad Industrial Area (Akurde, 
Shengaon, Hedwade, Devakiwadi) 
52.82 Hectare (De-notified on 
21.08.2025) 
Shahuwade Industrial Area (Warul, 
Lonane) 
 
61.64 Hectare (De-notified on 
16.06.2026) 
 
The Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation  (MIDC) has 
informed that there is no specific proposal for incentivizing Foundry -
Engineering or Textile manufacturing units to occupy underutilized plots in 
Kolhapur MIDC industrial areas. To promote timely utilization of allotted 
industrial plots, MIDC has issued Circular No. C-05579 dated 21.06.2019, 
under which every plot allotted after the date of the circular is required to 
utilize at least 40 percent of the permissible Floor Space Index and obtain 
the Building Completion Certificate within the stipulated period. 
For the textiles industries, the Ministry of Textiles has informed that under 
the Scheme for Integrated Textile Parks (SITP), four textile parks have 
been developed in Kolhapur district. These parks have 387 operational 
units providing employment to 15,639 persons. 
With regard to the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, no proposal 
for extension of the Scheme specifically to medium-scale engineering and 
foundry industries in the Kolhapur industrial belt is under appraisal. The 
PLI Schemes have been implemented for 14 notified sectors. 
 
The Government of Maharashtra has informed that the Package Scheme 
of Incentives (PSI) is implemented with the objective of promoting balanced 
industrial development across the State. Under the applic able Package 
Scheme of Incentives, eligible industrial units engaged in the 
manufacturing sector, including the engineering and  foundry industries 
(MSME, Large Scale Industries, Mega and Ultra Mega) are eligible for 
fiscal incentives such as Industrial Pro motion Subsidy, Interest Subsidy, 
Stamp Duty Exemption, Electricity Duty Exemption, Power Tariﬀ Subsidy, 
and other admissible benefits, subject to the provisions of the applicable  
Package Scheme of Incentives. 

Under the Package Scheme of Incentives -2019, the Government of 
Maharashtra has sanctioned incentives amounting to 7697.35 crore to  53 
medium-scale industrial units in Kolhapur district. These units operate 
across diverse sectors, including automobile components, foundry, 
textiles, and other manufactu ring industries, thereby supporting industrial 
growth, employment generation, and balanced regional development. 
The Government of Maharashtra has declared Maharashtra Industries, 
Investment and Services Policy, 2025 on 31.12.2025 which aims to 
generate close to 50 lakh direct jobs during the policy period.

Infrastructure for Export Scheme (TIES), National Logistics Policy 2022, developing 
Industrial Corridors under National Industrial Corridor Development Programme 

3 
 
(NICDP), implementing port moderniz ation under Sagarmala programme, Ease of 
Doing Business reforms, establishing the National Single Window System (NSWS), 
PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, supporting start-ups via Start-up India scheme,

ecosystem, all States, including Tamil Nadu are encouraged to formulate their 
State Logistics Policy aligning with the National Logistics Policy (NLP) 2022.

adopted the strategy of developing Industrial Corridors under National Industrial 
Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) in partnership with State 
Governments. The objective of this programme is to develop Greenfield 
Industrial Infrastructure. 
iv. A total of 94 projects w orth Rs. 12,523 Cr have been implemented in Major 
Ports of Tamil Nadu since FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, to strengthen the export 
infrastructure at Ports. 
v. The Government has undertaken reforms  to improve the Ease of Doing 
Business (EoDB)  across the country, i ncluding in the State of Tamil Nadu. 
Further, the Government has undertaken the Reducing Compliance Burden 
(RCB) initiative. As a result, 2,521 compliances have been reduced in the state 
of Tamil Nadu. 
vi. Envisioned as a one -stop shop for investor related app rovals and services in 
the country, National Single Window System (NSWS) has been set up to 
provide “end to end” facilitation and support to investors. 
vii. PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP) has been launched to facilitate 
data-based decisions related t o integrated planning of multimodal 
infrastructure, thereby reducing logistics cost. 
viii. Under Start -up India initiative, the Government is implementing flagship 
Schemes, Fund of Funds for Start -ups (FFS), Start -up India Seed Fund 
Scheme (SISFS), and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Start -ups (CGSS) to 
provide funding opportunities and support start -ups at various stages of their 
business cycle. 
(e) To support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in areas of credit 
facilitation, technology up -gradation and export promotion, various schemes are 
implemented across the country. The schemes implemented, inter-alia, include Prime 
Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), Micro and Small 
Enterprises-Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP), Credit Guarantee Scheme 
for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), Self -Reliant India (SRI) Fund, 
Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme (ESDP), and MSME Champions 
Scheme. Further, to create a conducive environment for the promotion and 
development of MSME, Udyam Registration Portal has been developed to provide an 
online, paperless and transparent MSME registration process.  The details of Central 
assistance, incentives and export promotion schemes extended to exporters and 
(MSMEs) in the country, including Tamil Nadu are as below:  

4 
 
i. The Export Promotion Mission (EPM) was launched in 2025 to strengthen 
India’s export competitiveness with an allocation of ₹2,300 Cr in 2026-27 for 
EPM, including for exporters and institutions from Tamil Nadu. 
ii. Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) Scheme allows import of capital 
goods at zero customs duty for production of goods and services meant for 
export. The scheme supports technology up-gradation and manufacturing 
competitiveness of Indian exporters. 
iii. The District Export Hub (DEH) Initiative provides the district-level framework 
for decentralised export promotion. In each district, the effort is to identify and 
prioritise 3–5 products/services with viable export potential for targeted 
interventions. 
iv. Refund of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme aims 
to refund currently un-refunded duties/taxes/levies borne on the export 
product, including prior stage cumulative indirect taxes on goods and services 
used in production of the exported products. 
v. The Advance Authorisation (AA) scheme allows duty-free import of inputs that 
are physically incorporated into or used in the production of the export 
product. All MSMEs including in Tamil Nadu may avail duty exemption 
benefits. 
vi. Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (ECGC) provides credit 
insurance covers to exporters against non-payment risks by the overseas 
buyers due to Commercial and Political reasons. The Company has 46 
branch offices pan-India including eight in Tamil Nadu at Chennai, Chennai 
South, Coimbatore, Karur, Madurai, Salem, Tirupur, and Tuticorin, which 
serve as local points of contact for exporters and banks. 
vii. The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has established 65 
Export Facilitation Centers (EFCs) in its field offices across the country 
including 04 in Tamil Nadu with the aim of providing requisite mentoring and 
handholding support to MSMEs in exporting their products and services. 
viii. International Cooperation (IC) Scheme of Ministry of MSME aims to build 
capacity of MSMEs by facilitating their participation in international 
exhibitions/fairs/conferences/seminar/buyer-seller meets abroad as well as 
reimbursement of various costs.
