GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.  23 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Mental Pressure of Examination on Primary School Students 
 
†23. Shri Murari Lal Meena:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether educational experts and parents are expressing the need to reduce the increasing 
mental pressure of examinations on primary school students and to encourage their holistic 
development, if so, the view of the Government in this regard;  
 
(b) whether the Government is considering making Continuous and Comprehensive 
Evaluation (CCE) or any other child -friendly evaluation system more effective instead of 
traditional annual examinations for students of Classes 1 to 5, if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to deliberate with the States regarding the 
implementation of a two-day weekly holiday on Saturdays and Sundays, keeping in view the 
physical and mental health, family engagement, and hol istic development of primary school 
students (Classes 1 to 5) and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY)  
 
(a) to (b): Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of 
schools fall under the administrative control of the respective State Government/Union 
Territory (UT) administration.  On its part, the Ministry of Education is guided by , the 
National Education Policy (NEP), 2020  in all its efforts and initiatives. The NEP 2020  
formulated through extensive and participatory consultation with various stakeholders, 
including educational experts and parents,  emphasises joyful learning, play, discovery and 
activity- based pedagogy at foundational and preparatory stages (i.e. upto Class 5)  and 
transforming assessments for holistic development of learners. 
 
To this end, several initiatives such as the Jaadui Pitara and e -Jaadui Pitara 
(https://ejaaduipitara.ncert.gov.in), a collection of interactive learning teaching materials 
including toys, games, puzzles and story cards ; a three months play based ‘School 
Preparation Module and Guidelines’ for Grade I named ‘Vidya Pravesh’; and play and 
activity based text book for classes  – 1 and 2  have been launched by th e Department of 
School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education under the NIPUN Bharat Mission.  
 
Further, the NEP 2020  stresses upon  a shift in assessment system from one that is 
summative and primarily tests rote memorization skills to one that is more regular and 

formative, competency-based, and promotes learning and development of the students, and 
tests higher -order skills, such as  analysis, critical thinking, and conceptual clarity. It 
envisages assessment as a tool for continuously revising teaching -learning processes to 
optimize learning and development for all students. 
 
In pursuance of the NEP, 2020, the National Assessment Cen tre, PARAKH, NCERT under 
the aegis of the Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education has 
developed the Holistic Progress Card (HPC) for all stages of school education. The same 
are available in the public domain at the link  https://parakh.ncert.gov.in/hpc. The HPC 
designed for the foundational and preparatory stages, covering upto Class 5, is a holistic 
360-degree, multi -dimensional report that integrates teacher, peer and self -assessment to 
reflect the uniqueness of each learner in the cognitive, affective and psycho-motor domains.  
 
(c): With Education being in the Concurrent List of the Constitution , operational and 
administrative matters such as school holidays in majority of schools fall within the purview 
of the respective State Governments and UT Administrations.

District-wise details of number of ITIs (in Year 2014 & Year 2026) and enrolment in ITIs (in 
Session 2014 -15 & 2025 -26) in Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Odisha are available at 
Annexure - 2, 3 and 4 respectively. 
 
(c) to (g) The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded 
ITIs (PM-SETU) scheme aims to enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training 
in the country. The Scheme has a total outlay of Rs. 60,000 crore  (Central Share – Rs. 30,000 
crore, State Share – Rs. 20,000 crore and Industry Share – Rs. 10,000 crore). 
 
The scheme comprises of two components: 
 
i.    Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in 
a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital 
content, and new courses aligned to industry needs. 
 
ii.  Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, 
Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including setting -up sector -specific National Centres of 
Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced training of trainers with glo bal partnership, and 
curriculum development. The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability through Upgraded ITIs 
(PM-SETU) Scheme is being implemented across States/UTs, including Chhattisgarh and 
Maharashtra, to upgrade the quality and relevance of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs).  
 
As per the Cabinet approval, the selection of ITIs under Pradhan Mantri Skilling and 
Employability through Upgraded ITIs (PM SETU) scheme is led by the respective State/UT 
Governments in consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill ne eds and 
local industrial potential. Accordingly, States/UTs are required to submit proposals for 
upgradation in collaboration with industry partners. 
 
Chhattisgarh has identified Six (6) clusters, comprising 6 Hub ITIs and 24 Spoke ITIs, under the 
PM-SETU Scheme and have floated the Request for Proposal (RfP) for selection of the Anchor 
Industry Partner (AIP). At present, no proposal or Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) from the State 
is pending for consideration or approval before the National Steering Committee (NSC).  
 
Odisha has identified Two (2) clusters, comprising 2 Hub ITIs and 8 Spoke ITIs, under the PM -
SETU Scheme and have floated the Request for Proposal (RfP) for selection of the Anchor 
Industry Partner (AIP). The NSC has approved SIP for Keonjhar-Barbil Cluster.  
 

Further, under the PM-SETU scheme industry-led Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) would lead 
the upgradation and be empowered to propose necessary interventions relating to curriculum 
redesign in mining, manufacturing and other sectors , training delivery models, infrastructure 
upgradation and industry exposure, in alignment with local industry needs and the Scheme 
guidelines. Directorate General of Training (DGT) has introduced 3 2 new age courses under 
CTS. Once the industry partner is onboard, these courses are available to be operationalized in 
the selected ITIs. List of these new age courses are given in Annexure 5. 
 
As of now, the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has released ₹50 
lakh to the Government of Odisha for engagement of the Project Management Consultant (PMC) 
and ₹30 lakh for Industry Outreach activities during FY 2025–26.

Strengthening Cooperative Movement 
231. Shri Sukanta Kumar Panigrahi 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the implementation of the National Cooperation Policy, 2025 and White Revolution 2.0 
has strengthened the cooperative movement by promoting digital governance, expanding PACS, 
enhancing dairy cooperatives and increasing farmers' income across the country; 
(b) the details of PACS computerised and onboarded on the National Cooperative Database, new 
multipurpose PACS and Dairy Cooperative Societies established, State-wise including in Odisha; 
(c) the details of cooperative institutions, dairy infrastructure, milk procurement facilities and 
financial assistance provided, district -wise comprising Kandhamal, Boudh, Nayagarh and 
Ganjam districts; 
(d) whether the National Cooperative Database has been integrated with the implementation and 
monitoring of these initiatives for transparent and efficient governance; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to provide additional financial and technical support for 
strengthening cooperative and dairy infrastructure in Aspirational Districts and tribal regions, 
particularly Kandhamal, and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
(a) Yes, Sir. The National Cooperation Policy, 2025, which includes White Revolution 2.0, is aimed at 
strengthening the cooperative movement across the country through systematic and holistic 
development of the cooperative sector by encouraging the digitalization cooperative sector, expansion 
of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), primary dairy and fisheries cooperatives to cover all 
uncovered panchayats, promotion of multipurpose PACS , etc. Further, the Policy seeks to enhance 
members' and farmers' incomes through diversification of cooperative activities, value addition, 
improved market access, promotion of exports, capacity building and strengthening of the cooperative 
business ecosystem to achieve the vision of 'Sahkar-Se-Samriddhi'. 
Further, the implementation of White Revolution 2.0 has strengthened the dairy cooperatives 
and increased milk procurement in the cooperative sector. Since the launch of White Revolution 2.0, 
24,097 new DCS have been formed , and 31,394 existing DCS have been strengthened , and the milk 
procurement by cooperatives has increased from 660 LKG/day in 2023 -24 to 697LKG/day in 2025 -
26. 

Page 2 of 6 
 
(b) & (c): The Government launched the Central Sector Project for Computerization of PACS, in 2022. 
The Government of India initially approved 63,000 PACS under Project of Computerization of 
functional PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has now been increased up to 
2925.39 Crore covering 79,630 PACS which entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP 
(Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national software, linking them with NABARD through 
State Cooperative Banks (StCBs ) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). The state -wise 
details are at Annexure-1. 
 Moreover, as a result of the initiatives taken by the Government, 38,138 new PACS, dairy, and 
fishery cooperative societies have been registered nationwide since 15.02.2023. The initiative to 
establish new multipurpose PACS, dairy, and fishery cooperatives is supported by NABARD, NDDB, 
and NFDB through the convergence of various existing Government of India (GoI) schemes, including 
the Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF), the National Programme for Dairy Development 
(NPDD), and the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The State-wise details of PACS, dairy, and 
fishery cooperative societies formed along with members associated with them , are placed as 
Annexure-2. In Odisha, there are 8,667 cooperative societies, of which 8,063 are functional. Under 
the national plan, 2,609 new cooperative societies have been registered in the State, comprising 1,539 
Multipurpose PACS/LAMPS (Large Area Multi-Purpose Societies), 1,009 Dairy Cooperative Societies 
and 61 Fishery Cooperative Societies. Further 466 existing dairy societies have been strengthened.

SHE-MART INITIATIVES 
 
232.  Dr. Rajeev Bharadwaj: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there is any scheme to establish markets in villages 
under the She-Mart initiative, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether there is any plan to set up She-Mart retail outlets in 
Kangra and Chamba districts of Himachal Pradesh, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(c)  whether there is any plan to bring the products manufactured by 
rural women in the markets of metropolitan/major cities, if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI) 
(a) to (c): The Government has announced the setting up of Self Help 
Entrepreneur (SHE) Marts as a new initiative to strengthen market 
access for rural women-led enterprises under the Self Help Group 
(SHG) ecosystem. These marts are envisaged as structured retail 
platforms where products made by SHG members can be showcased 
and sold directly to consumers. The initiative is aimed at creating 
stronger market linkages, improving visibility of local products, 
strengthening SHG institutions, and enabling women entrepreneurs 
to expand and scale their businesses. Government has announced to 
set up of SHE-Marts as community-owned retail outlets within the 
cluster-level federations in all the States and Union Territories, 
including Himachal Pradesh.

DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

  ANSWERED ON 21/07/2026 
 
LAUNCHING OF VB-GRAM-G 
 
235. Shri K Radhakrishnan: 
Shri Benny Behanan: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has launched Viksit Bharat-Guarantee 
for Rojgar and Ajeevika Mission (VB-GRAM-G) as a substitute for 
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme 
(MGNREGS) in any State/UT; 
(b)  if so, the details of objectives, funding pattern, and wage rates 
under VB-GRAM-G vs MGNREGS; 
(c)  whether Gram Panchayats have been directed to prioritize VB-
GRAM-G works over MGNREGS shelf of projects, if so, the details 
thereof; 
(d)  the number of households provided employment under VB-
GRAM-G vs MGNREGS in 2024-25 and 2025-26, State-wise; and 
(e)  whether the Government admits that VB-GRAM-G lacks legal 
guarantee of 100 days work unlike MGNREGS, if so, the details 
thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): A new Act titled the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and 
Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 has been enacted in December, 
2025. In compliance of the provisions of the Act all States/UTs have 
since notified  VB-G RAM G scheme and it has successfully been 
implemented in rural areas of the entire country with effect from 
01.07.2026.   
  

Page 2 of 6 
 
(b):    The core objectives of the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar 
and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB- G RAM G Act, 2025, are given at 
Annexure-I.  
  As per Sub-section (2) of Section 22 of the Act, VB- G RAM G shall 
be a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and the fund-sharing pattern 
between the Central Government and the State/UTs Government 
shall be 90:10 for the North-Eastern States, Himalayan States and 
Union Territory (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and 
Kashmir) and 60:40 for all other States and Union territories with 
legislature.  
    Vide notification dated 30.06.2026 Government of India has 
notified the wage rates payable under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee 
for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB- G RAM G Act, 2025 . 
The revised wage rate is effective from 1st July, 2026.  The main 
feature of the revised wage rate is the fixing of ₹300 as interim base 
wage rate.    
  Consequent upon fixation of interim wage rate under VB-G RAM G 
the average national notified wage rate has increased from ₹298.8 
per day under MGNREGS to ₹327.4 per day under VB–G RAM G, 
representing an average increase of ₹28.6 per day. The average 
percentage increase across the country exceeds 10 per cent.  
  State/UT-wise notified wage rates (in Rs.) for unskilled workers 
under the Mahatma Gandhi NREGS for financial year 2025-26 and 
under VB-G RAM G Scheme for the financial year 2026-27 are given at 
Annexure-II. 
(c):  Under, Section 4(3) of the Act rural works planning shall be 
undertaken through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans prepared by the 
Gram Panchayats from the approved Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan. 
    Further, as per para 8 of Schedule I of the act, at the time of opening 
new works, ongoing or incomplete works shall be prioritised for 
completion, subject to planning norms and the approved Viksit Gram 
Panchayat Plans. 
(d):    States/Union Territories-wise number of households who availed 
employment under the erstwhile Mahatma Gandhi NREGS in the 
financial year 2024-25 and 2025-26 is given at Annexure-III.  

Page 3 of 6 
 
  
With regard to Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika 
Mission (Gramin) VB-G RAM G Scheme , it is stated that the 
implementation of the scheme in rural areas of the entire country 
have started w.e.f. 1st July 2026 and over 3 crore Persondays have 
so far been generated under VB G RAM G Scheme.  
  
(e):     The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin) VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, provides for one hundred and twenty-
five days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every 
rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled 
manual work. Accordingly, the Act provides higher statutory 
guaranteed wage employment compared  to 100 days of guaranteed 
wage employment  available under now repealed Mahatma Gandhi 
National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005. 
The Act further strengthens the livelihood security framework by 
promoting the creation of durable and productive rural assets through 
a convergence-based planning framework anchored in the Viksit 
Gram Panchayat Plans, technology-enabled implementation, and 
transparent monitoring mechanisms, with the objective of enhancing 
sustainable rural livelihoods and rural infrastructure. 
***** 
  
  
  

Page 4 of 6 
 
Annexure-I 
Annexure referred to in the reply to part (b) of Lok Sabha Unstarred 
Question No. 235 dated 21.07.2026. 
i. The primary objective of this Act is to align the rural 
development framework with the national vision of Viksit 
Bharat @2047 by providing an enhanced statutory wage 
employment guarantee of one hundred and twenty-five days in 
each financial year to such rural households whose adult 
members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work, 
thereby enabling them to participate more effectively in the 
expanded livelihood security framework. 
ii. To focus on empowerment, growth, convergence and saturation 
through public works aggregating into forming Viksit Bharat 
National Rural Infrastructure Stack, with a thematic focus on 
water security through water-related works, core rural 
infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and special 
works to mitigate extreme weather events. 
iii. To facilitate adequate farm-labour availability during peak 
agricultural seasons, and, in view of the wage-employment 
guarantee for the rural workforce.   
iv. To institutionalise convergence, saturation-driven planning and 
whole of government delivery through Viksit Gram Panchayat 
Plans, integrated with the PM Gati Shakti to address the varying 
needs of Gram Panchayats, powered by geospatial systems, 
digital public infrastructure, district and State planning 
mechanisms, with such plans aggregated at the Block, District, 
State and National levels. 
v. To modernise governance, accountability and citizen 
engagement through a comprehensive digital ecosystem, 
including biometric authentication at various levels, global 
positioning system or mobile based worksite monitoring, real 
time management information system dashboards, proactive 
public disclosures and the use of Artificial Intelligence for 
planning, audits and fraud risk mitigation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 236 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
IMPACT OF EL NINO ON AGRICULTURE 
 
236.  SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE: 
 PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
 DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE: 
 SMT. SUPRIYA SULE: 
 SHRI MOHITE PATIL DHAIRYASHEEL RAJSINH: 
 SHRI SANJAY DINA PATIL: 
 SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has issued any advisory or contingency plans in view of 
possible El Nino conditions and their impact on the monsoon during 2026; 
 
(b) whether an assessment has been made regarding the likely impact on agriculture in 
Maharashtra, particularly in drought-prone regions such as Marathwada and Vidarbha; 
 
(c) the details of measures taken to safeguard farmers’ interests in Maharashtra, including 
provision of drought-resistant seeds, crop diversification, irrigation support and weather-
based advisories; 
 
(d) whether adequate funds have been earmarked for crop insurance, input subsidies and 
relief measures for farmers in Maharashtra; and 
 
(e) whether the Government Proposes to strengthen water conservation and climate-
resilient agriculture programmes in Maharashtra and, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare is continuously monitoring the 
evolving monsoon situation and the possible impact of El Niño conditions on agriculture in 
close coordination with the India Meteorological Department (IMD), various Indian Council of 
Agriculture Research (ICAR) institutions, ICAR- Central Research Institute for Dryland 
Agriculture (CRIDA), Central Water Commission (CWC), Central Ground Water Board 
(CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast Centre (MNCFC), the Department of Food and 
Public Distribution (DFPD), the Department of Fertilisers (DoF) and State Governments. 
Further, the Government has undertaken the following measures: 

1. District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) have been updated for 14 States 
covering 342 Districts which are likely to receive below normal rainfall by the ICAR 
Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (ICAR-CRIDA) in consultation with the 
States for implementation.  
2. Weekly meeting of the Crop Weather Watch Group (CWWG) is being held with the 
representatives of India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission 
(CWC), Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Mahalanobis National Crop Forecast 
Centre (MNCFC), Indian Council of Agriculture Research - Central Research Institute for 
Dryland Agriculture (ICAR - CRIDA), Department of Fertilizers, Department of Food & 
Public Distribution and the State Governments to review rainfall situation, reservoir 
storage, groundwater levels, crop sowing, input availability, market situation and pest/ 
disease incidence for timely intervention. Meeting with State Agriculture Secretaries 
and Relief Commissioners held under the chairmanship of Secretary (DA&FW) on 
27.04.2026 to review availability of inputs like seeds, fodder, drinking & irrigation water, 
fertilizers and general preparedness. Further, a meeting of the Crisis Management 
Group had been conducted on 17.06.2026 to assess and strengthen preparedness for 
the monsoon. In addition, the National Disaster Management Authority has also 
reviewed the preparedness of below-normal rainfall conditions emanating from the 
likely impact of the El Nino conditions on 19th June 2026. Review of the situation has 
been undertaken by the Agriculture Minister, Government of India with the State 
Agriculture Ministers for Kharif preparedness amid El Nino conditions on 23.06.2026. 
3. Interface meetings by ICAR have been conducted with 14 States, including 
Maharashtra, for operationalization of District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs). 
Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have also been issued by ICAR for Krishi 
Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) for mitigation of El Niño-related risks.  
4. Adequate availability of seeds has been ensured, against the demand of 172.80 lakh 
quintals from the States, there was availability of 192.25 lakh quintals of Kharif crop 
seeds. States have maintained 1% seeds i.e. 1.74 Lakh quintals as National Seed 
Reserve.  
5. Special emphasis has been laid on promoting crop diversification, promotion of short-
duration and drought-tolerant crop varieties, balanced use of fertilizers, water 
conservation practices, micro-irrigation, mulching, inter-cropping and practices of other 
climate-resilient technologies. Due to the delay as well as the likelihood on adverse 
impact of El Nino conditions, sowing is likely to be affected in respect of Tur, Soybean 
and Cotton and accordingly, the advisories to the farmers have been given to sow 
Maize, Bajra and Moong, and other short duration crops.  
6. A nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyaan was organised during 1-30 June, 2026 in which 
80,67,300 farmers participated in 1,14,567 programmes which were organised to 
promote water conservation, introduce efficient irrigation and climate-resilient farming 
practices. Simultaneously, an intensive Kisan Credit Card (KCC) saturation drive and 
awareness campaign under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is being 
implemented in the vulnerable districts.  
7. As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State Government is 
primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures at the ground level in the 
wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the 
wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the approved guidelines. Additional 
financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the National Disaster 
Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of disaster of ‘severe 
nature’, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central 
Team (IMCT). The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of 
relief and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed. 

The State of Maharashtra has been allocated Rs.5718.00 crore (Central Share 
Rs.4288.50 crore & State Share Rs.1429.50 crore) under SDRF during 2026-27. The 
details of funds allocated and released to Maharashtra under SDRF and NDRF during

as part of the climate resilient agricultural practices, the Department is also

National Food Security Mission (NFSM), Integrated Scheme on Oilseeds Mission and

Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any technical assessment regarding the suitability, 
performance and operational feasibility of electric vehicles supported under the PM E - DRIVE 
Scheme for deployment in hilly and mountainous regions, particularly Himalayan States 
including Himachal Pradesh;  
 
(b) whether the parameters such as battery performance, charging efficiency, vehicle range, 
durability and overall efficiency have been evaluated under challenging conditions including low 
temperatures, steep gradients and difficult terrain;  
 
(c) if so, the details of such assessments, including key findings regarding the performance and

incentives, charging infrastructure support or policy measures to promote faster adoption of 
electric vehicles in Himalayan and hilly States?

(a) to (c): No such technical assessment regarding suitability, performance, operational 
feasibility as well as battery performance, charging efficiency, vehicle range, durability and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 (a) to (d) The Government has undertaken various policy and facilitation measures to 
promote cross-border e-commerce exports, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs), startups, artisans and other small exporters. Key initiatives 
include: 
(i) The Export Promotion Mission (EPM), with an approved outlay of ₹25,060 crore 
for the period 2025–31, comprises sub-schemes Niryat Protsahan, aimed at 
improving access to trade finance for MSMEs, and Niryat Disha, focused on 
strengthening other export enablers. Interventions under EPM to specifically 
promote e-commerce exports include: 
 Provision of an Export Credit Facility for E-Commerce Exports to improve 
access to trade finance. 
 Facilitating Logistics, Overseas Warehousing and Fulfilment initiative to 
strengthen logistics and fulfilment capabilities of e-commerce exporters in 
overseas markets. 
 Partial reimbursement of mandatory international certifications required for 
exports to help MSMEs meet destination-country standards and technical 
regulations. 
(ii) Implementation of the E-Commerce Export Hub (ECEH) initiative on a pilot 
basis to create an integrated ecosystem for e-commerce exports by facilitating 
logistics, customs clearances and other export-related services. 

2 
 
(iii) Leveraging the Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative to promote greater 
participation of district-level producers, MSMEs and startups in global markets 
through digital channels.  
(iv) Enabling exports through courier mode to avail benefits under the Remission 
of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP), Rebate of State and 
Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) and Duty Drawback schemes vide CBIC 
Notification No. 60/2024-Customs (N.T.) and Circular No. 15/2024-Customs, 
both dated 12 September 2024. 
(v) The Government has undertaken the following reforms to facilitate exports 
through courier mode and simplify related procedures: 
 The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has relaxed export reconciliation 
requirements for small-value exports up to ₹10 lakh by permitting closure of 
export transactions in the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System 
(EDPMS) on the basis of declarations furnished by exporters and 
reconciliation undertaken by banks. 
 The per-consignment value limit of ₹10 lakh for exports through courier mode 
has been removed vide DGFT Notification No. 67/2025-26 and CBIC 
Notification No. 34/2026. 
 CBIC Notification No. 33/2026 has been issued to facilitate re-import of 
export rejects and returns, thereby simplifying reverse logistics for cross-
border e-commerce exports. 
The above initiatives are aimed at expanding participation of MSMEs and small 
exporters in cross-border e-commerce by reducing logistics and compliance barriers 
and improving access to export-related services. 
 
The Government is pursuing a multi-pronged strategy to promote cross-border 
ecommerce exports by strengthening export infrastructure, improving access to global 
markets and facilitating the integration of MSMEs and district-level producers into 
international value chains.

responsibility of the State/UT Governments. All PMGSY works are 
covered by initial five year maintenance contracts during the Defect 
Liability Period (DLP) as per the Standard Bidding Document. 
Maintenance funds to service the contract are required to be 
budgeted by the State/UT Governments and placed at the disposal of 
the State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDAs) in a separate 
account. On expiry of the 5 year, ie., during the post Defect Liability 
Period (post DLP), the roads are placed under Zonal maintenance 
contracts for a term of 5 year, which includes renewal and 
maintenance from time to time. The budget for the same is also 
allocated by the State/UT governments.

(e) & (f): The Government continuously monitors the progress of 
works sanctioned PMGSY-III. After careful examination of the 
prevailing circumstances, a proposal seeking extension of the 
implementation timeline was submitted to the Government.

timeline up to March 2028 for the completion of PMGSY-III works. 
To ensure completion of the balance works within the revised 
time frame, regular review meetings are conducted at the State/UT, 
Regional and National levels regularly and progress of 
implementation is closely monitored. Issues affecting project 
execution are reviewed on a case-to-case basis and necessary 
interventions are undertaken in coordination with all concerned 
stakeholders to facilitate their timely resolution.  
For ensuring timely completion with the prescribed quality 
standards, PMGSY follows a robust Three-Tier Quality Control 
Mechanism supported by the "Quality First" mobile application. The 
application serves as a digital inspection and monitoring platform 
that enables stage-wise quality inspections during construction 
phases, Geo-tagged photographic evidence, and digital stage-passing 
approvals during the execution of PMGSY works. It complements the 
overall quality assurance framework, which includes 4 internal 
inspections by the Programme Implementation Units (PIUs), 3 
independent inspections by State Quality Monitors (SQMs), and one 
inspection by National Quality Monitors (NQMs).

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
SOLAR POWERED COLD STORAGE FACILITIES 
 
242. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND: 
   
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE                                              
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the initiatives implemented/proposed by the Government for promoting solar-
powered cold storage, pack-house and cold-chain infrastructure for farmers 
cultivating vegetables, fruits, flowers and other perishable commodities in Vellore 
district of Tamil Nadu, where post-harvest losses and distress sales affect farm 
incomes; 
 
(b) the number, storage capacity and operational status of solar-powered cold-
storage facilities sanctioned and established in Vellore district and Tamil Nadu under 
the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agriculture Infrastructure 
Fund and other Central schemes; 
 
(c) the steps taken to encourage Farmer Producer Organisations, cooperatives 
and agri-startups to adopt decentralised solar-powered cold-storage solutions; 
 
(d) the funds allocated, released and utilised during 2020-21 to 2025-26, year-
wise; and  
 
(e) the details of the reduction in post-harvest losses, increase in shelf life of 
produce and enhancement in farmers' incomes achieved through these 
interventions? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The Government of India implements the Mission for Integrated Development 
of Horticulture (MIDH) for the holistic development of the horticulture sector, 
including the creation of post-harvest management and cold-chain infrastructure 
across the country, including Tamil Nadu.  
 
Under the scheme, famers/entrepreneur are allowed to use solar powered 
cold storage, pack house and cold chain infrastructure under MIDH thereby allowing 
farmers to store their vegetables and fruits at farm gate in controlled temperature 
before sending it to market and thus protecting them from distress sales.  
 
Further under the scheme, to strengthen the cold chain infra at primary side of 
the Cold chain which is managed by farmers and FPOs, Integrated Pack house 
(IPH) and Collection Aggregation centres (CAC) have been introduced as 
components which allows farmers, growers and FPOs to  grade, store in small micro 
solar based cold storages and transport their fresh produce to market without getting 
in distress.  These components also allow small 2 MT vehicles which allows farmers 
to collect and send their produce as per the market demand and thereby disallowing 
distress sales.  

 
Under AIF, there is provision for collateral free term loan upto Rs. 2.00 crore 
and interest subvention of 3% on the term loan availed for creation of post-harvest 
infrastructure including establishment of cold storages.  
 
(b): Under MIDH scheme, 10 numbers (9 under NHB and 1 under NHM) of cold 
storage with a total capacity of 0.68 lakh MT and under AIF scheme, 99 cold 
storage/cold chain projects have been sanctioned in Tamil Nadu. However, no 
proposal for establishment of solar based cold storage has been received from the 
State of Tamil Nadu.   
 
(c): The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare continuously encourages 
Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), cooperatives, Self Help Groups (SHGs), 
entrepreneurs and agri-startups to establish decentralized post-harvest infrastructure 
by providing financial assistance under MIDH. Assistance is also available for 
integrated post-harvest management infrastructure to improve storage, aggregation, 
value addition and marketing of horticulture produce. Capacity building, convergence 
with institutional credit and project-based support further facilitate adoption of such 
technologies. 
 
(d): Under MIDH, funds are released to the States for undertaking various 
horticulture-related activities, including the creation of post-harvest management 
infrastructure, as per the approved Annual Action Plan (AAP) of the concerned State. 
The year-wise details of funds allocated, released and utilised by the Government of 
Tamil Nadu during 2020-21 to 2025-26 are as under:

Farming (NMNF) during the year 2026, State-wise including Chhattisgarh and Pali Lok

(b)   the details of farmers, clusters, and the area covered under farming practices

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी                                       (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): The Union Cabinet approved the National Mission on Natural Farming 
on 25th November 2024 as a centrally sponsored scheme which is being implemented 
across the country including the States of Rajasthan, Karnataka and Chhattisgarh. 
State/UT wise details of number of farmers enrolled and area covered under the 
mission is given at Annexure - I. The details regarding the implementation of the 
Mission in Pali Lok Sabha constituency, Rajasthan is given at Annexure – II.   
 
(c): Under the Mission, 527 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), 76 Agriculture 
Universities (AUs), 194 Local Natural Farming Institutes (LNFIs) have been identified 
to support cluster level implementation of the scheme. 18 Centres of Natural Farming 
Institutes (CoNFs) have been identified to impart training of Scientists from these 
Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs)/ State Agriculture Universities (SAUs), Officials of 
State/Districts/Block level implementing the scheme and Farmer Master Trainers 
(FMTs). At a cluster level Community Resource Persons (CRPs) are deployed to 
handhold the farmers on the practices of natural farming. Such CRPs and farmers are 
trained by the Scientists and FMTs at KVK, SAU & LNFI. Natural Farming Certification 
System (NFCS) has been initiated as "Participatory Guarantee System (PGS)-INDIA 
NATURAL" for certification of natural farming produces to enable farmers to get 
premium price for Natural Farming produce. More than 22.39 lakh farmers have been 
registered under the natural farming certification system till date with more than 14.20 
lakh farmers issued natural farming certificates. Natural Farming certified products are 
available in the market as well as on Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) for 
Business to Consumer sales. 
 
(d): The Mission provides Output Based Incentive of ₹4000/- per acre, per year to 
a farmer for 2 years (up to 1 acre per farmer). The incentive support is for farmers to 
practice Natural Farming, to train more farmers, upkeep of livestock, preparation of 
natural farming inputs including purchase of mixing & storage containers or purchase 
of inputs from Bio-input Resource Centres (BRCs). NITI Aayog Assessment Report 

states that approximately 91.2% of farmers adopting natural farming experience 
increased crop productivity and significantly improved soil health. 90.1% of farmers 
reported that adopting natural farming has reduced input costs (production costs).The 
State/UTs wise physical and financial achievement of the implementation of scheme 
till 2025-26 including the State of Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan are given at Annexure

Shri Godam Nagesh: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the total length in kilometres of rural roads constructed and the 
number of habitations connected under the Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY-I, II, III and IV) till date during the 
Financial Year 2025-26, State, district and phase-wise including 
the States of Jharkhand, Gujarat and Rajasthan specially for 
Chatra, Pali and Dahod Lok Sabha Constituencies; 
(b)  the details of roads sanctioned, completed, under construction 
and proposed under PMGSY  along with the funds sanctioned, 
released and utilized during the last three years and the current 
year, year, State and district-wise including Chatra Lok Sabha 
Constituency; 
(c)  the details of the implementation plan for PMGSY during the 
Financial Year 2026–27 particularly for upgradation and 
maintenance of rural roads with special emphasis on roads in 
tribal areas, State-wise including Chatra and Dahod Lok Sabha 
Constituencies and Palghar district of Maharashtra; 
(d)  the targets fixed for construction and upgradation of rural roads 
under the Scheme, State-wise particularly in Chhattisgarh, 
Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat States including the current 
status of past targets along with the goals set for the future in 
Jabalpur, Shimla and Damoh Parliamentary Constituencies 
during the Financial Year 2026-27; 
(e)  whether the Government has adopted any mechanism for 
prioritising connectivity in Aspirational Districts, Western 
Ghats, Tribal and Remote areas, if so, the details thereof 
specially in tribal dominated districts of Dahod, Palghar, 
Kalahandi and Nuapada of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh 
and Odisha; and 
(f)  the details of planned investment, including the contribution of 
the Centre and the States including Gujarat, for implementation 
of the Scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a): The details of total length of roads constructed and number of 
habitations connected under all verticals of Pradhan Mantri Gram 
Sadak Yojana till 16.07.2026 since inception, including for the States 
of Jharkhand, Gujarat and Rajasthan, and specifically for Chatra, Pali 
and Dahod Lok Sabha Constituencies, are given at Annexure-I. 
  

Page 3 of 13 
 
Further, the phase-wise, state-wise and district-wise physical 
details of road length sanctioned, completed, under-construction, 
and habitations connected till date are available in the public domain 
via the Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System 
(OMMAS) portal and may be seen at https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb. 
  
 (b): The details of roads sanctioned, completed, under construction 
and proposed under PMGSY along with the funds sanctioned, 
released and utilized during the last three years and the current year 
(as on 16.07.2026), year-wise and state-wise are given at Annexure-
II. 
Further, the details of roads sanctioned, completed, under 
construction and proposed under PMGSY along with funds utilized 
during the last three years and the current year, year-wise, State-
wise and district-wise are available in the public domain via the 
Online Management, Monitoring and Accounting System (OMMAS) 
portal and may be seen at https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb. 
  
Further, year-wise details of roads sanctioned, completed, 
under construction and proposed under PMGSY, along with funds 
utilized during the last three years and the current year for Chatra 
Lok Sabha Constituency, are given at Annexure-III. 
(c) & (d): For the Financial Year 2026-27, physical targets for the 
construction and upgradation of rural roads under PMGSY are 
finalized in consultation with the respective State Governments 
during the Annual Action Plan (AAP) meetings, based on the balance 
of sanctioned works and the availability of budgetary resources. 
District-wise targets are subsequently allocated by the States/UTs 
within the state-wise targets allocated by the Ministry of Rural 
Development. The FY 2026-27 physical targets for various PMGSY 
verticals, including Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha 
Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) for connectivity to Particularly Vulnerable 
Tribal Groups (PVTGs) areas, are given at Annexure-IV. 
PMGSY roads are constructed by the State Governments with a 
design life of at least 10 years. As per PMGSY guidelines, 
maintenance of roads constructed under the programme is the 
responsibility of the State Governments. All PMGSY road works are 
covered by an initial five year maintenance contracts to be entered 
into along with the construction contract, with the same contractor, 
as per the Standard Bidding Document. Maintenance funds to service 
the contract are required to be budgeted by the State Governments 
and placed at the disposal of the State Rural Roads Development 
Agencies (SRRDAs) in a separate maintenance account. On expiry of 

Page 4 of 13 
 
this 5 year post construction maintenance, PMGSY roads are required 
to be placed under Zonal maintenance contracts consisting of 5 year 
maintenance including renewal as per cycle, from time to time. 
(e): The program guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana 
(PMGSY) incorporate dedicated relaxation parameters to ensure 
prioritized connectivity for special category areas, including 
Aspirational Districts, Tribal (Schedule-V) areas, Desert Areas, and 
Special Category areas. While eligibility criteria for other habitations 
for getting connectivity under the scheme is a population of 500 
persons (as per 2001 census under PMGSY-I and as per Census 2011 
under PMGSY-IV), for Tribal (Schedule V) areas and Selected Tribal 
and Backward Districts (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs 
and Planning Commission)  and for  North-Eastern and Himalayan 
States,  unconnected habitations with a population of 250 and above 
are eligible for providing all-weather road connectivity under the 
scheme. 
  
  Furthermore, under the recently launched PMGSY-IV, these 
relaxed population criteria (250+) continue to apply to Aspirational 
Districts/Blocks, Tribal Schedule-V areas, and Desert Areas based on 
Census 2011 data, with a further relaxation down to a population of 
100 or more in districts affected by Left Wing Extremism.  
  
Further, the Government has also integrated the road 
connectivity components of the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh 
Abhiyan (DA-JGUA) and the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday 
Yojana (PM-AJAY) through convergence with PMGSY-IV. This 
convergence framework applies to all States and Union Territories. 
Under this framework priority is given to unconnected habitations 
identified under DA-JGUA that have a population of 500 or more with 
at least 50% Scheduled Tribe population, or those in Aspirational 
Districts with a population of 250 or more including at least 50 
Scheduled Tribe members. Similarly, under PM-AJAY, priority is 
extended to unconnected habitations with a population of 500 or 
more and at least 40% Scheduled Caste population as per Census 
2011.  
  
In addition to the above, road connectivity component 
of  Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-
JANMAN)  is also being implemented as a separate vertical under 
PMGSY to provide connectivity to the habitations of Particularly 
Vulnerable Tribal Groups(PVTG).  
Under these systematic guidelines, eligible unconnected 
habitations falling within the tribal-dominated districts of Dahod 

Page 5 of 13 
 
(Gujarat), Palghar (Maharashtra), Kalahandi, and Nuapada (Odisha) 
are extended connectivity benefits under the relaxed norms. Project 
sanctions for these areas are processed based on the core network 
planning and Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) formulated and 
submitted by the respective State Governments in compliance with 
the programme frameworks. 
(f): The PMGSY was launched as 100% Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme. However, subsequently, on the basis of the 
recommendations of the Sub-Group of Chief Ministers on 
Rationalization of Centrally Sponsored Schemes the fund sharing 
pattern of PMGSY was changed in the ratio of 60:40 between the 
Centre and States for all States/UT including Gujarat except for 8 
North Eastern and 3 Himalayan States/UTs (with legislature) for 
which it is 90:10 with effect from 2015-16. The Central share for the 
UTs without legislature is 100%.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 245 
FOR ANSWER ON 21.07.2026  
 
 
FIRE ACCIDENT AT VISAKHAPATNAM STEEL PLANT 
 
 
 
245. DR. GANAPATHY RAJKUMAR P: 
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state: 
(a) the details and the total number of workers died and injured during the recent fire 
accident at the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP); 
 
(b) the details of the compensation paid to the family of those workers died and injured 
in the fire accident; 
 
(c) whether the Union Government has any proposal to offer any permanent job to the 
eligible family member of those workers died in the accident; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)to(d):  An accident occurred at Steel Melting Shop (SMS-2) of Steel Plant of 
Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL), Vishakhapatnam on 08th June, 2026, resulting in 
spillage of molten steel. In this accident, ten (10) workers comprising of five (5) Regular 
Employees and five (5) Contractual Workers lost their lives and four (4) Regular 
Workers sustained injuries. 
An ex gratia payment of ₹25 lakh, in addition to the admissible terminal benefits, 
has been made to the family of each deceased regular and contractual employee. 
Compensation of ₹10 lakh has been paid to each of the injured employees. In addition, 
an ex gratia payment of ₹2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund 
(PMNRF) has also been sanctioned to the next of kin of each deceased employee, 
while ₹50,000 has been sanctioned to each injured employee. Further, one (1) eligible 
dependent family member of each deceased regular as well as contractual employee 
has been offered compassionate appointment in RINL.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 246 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st July, 2026 
 
 HORTICULTURE PRODUCTION 
 
246.  SMT. MANJU SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान 
कʞाण मंũी be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the potential for horticulture production 
across all States; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the details of the area under horticulture, its productivity yield and potential, 
State/UT-wise, including Rajasthan; 
(d) the details of the funds allocated, released and utilized under the Integrated 
Horticulture Development Mission during the last three years along with State/UT and 
district-wise details thereof in Rajasthan; and 
(e) the steps taken by the Government to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for 
their horticulture produce? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
(a) & (b): According to the Working Group report on Crop Husbandry, Agriculture 
Inputs, Demand & Supply, 2024 by NITI Aayog, there is a vast potential to improve 
production of major food commodities including fruits and vegetables in the country by 
bridging the yield gaps.  
 
(c): The details of State/ UT-wise area, production and productivity/ yield of 
Horticultural crops in the country, including the State of Rajasthan, for 2025-26 
(Second Advance Estimates) has been given at Annexure-1. 
 
(d): The details of the funds allocated, released and utilized under the Mission for 
Integrated Horticulture Development (MIDH) during the last three years along with the 
details thereof in Rajasthan, State/Union Territory-wise are given in Annexure-2. 
However, district-wise allocation is being done by the States/UTs as per their 
requirement and potential. The District-wise expenditure reported by the State of 
Rajasthan is placed at Annexure-3. 

 
(e): Steps taken by the Government to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their 
horticulture produce are as under: 
 
i. Assistance is provided for development of infrastructure for post-harvest 
management and marketing such as storages, wholesale markets, rural 
primary markets, Kisan Mandies, etc.  
ii. National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) portal serves as a single window for 
creating an integrated national market for agricultural commodities, including 
horticulture commodities, providing better prices to the farmers through 
transparent auction processes and enabling farmers to sell their produce 
beyond local markets and reach buyers across the country. 
iii. Providing market information to farmers on prices and arrivals of agricultural 
commodities in regulated markets on AGMARKNET portal to enable the 
farmers to get better remunerative prices. 
iv. Market Intervention Scheme (MIS): Government is implementing the Market 
Intervention Scheme (MIS), as a part of the integrated scheme PM-AASHA, for 
protecting farmers from the distress sale of perishable agricultural and 
horticultural commodities, which are not covered under the Minimum Support 
Price (MSP). The Scheme has the following three provisions for supporting 
Horticulture Farmers whenever the prices are non-remunerative: 
 
• Procurement under MIS: On the receipt of request from the concerned 
State/UT Administration, Government gives sanction for the procurement of a 
predetermined quantity at the fixed Market Intervention Price (MIP) by the 
agencies designated by the State Government for a fixed period or till the prices 
are stabilized above the MIP whichever is earlier. Under Market Intervention 
Scheme (MIS), Central Share of losses, if any (at 50:50 basis for general States 
and 75: 25 basis for NE States), incurred in implementing MIS is released to 
the State procuring agencies as per the specific proposals received from the 
State Governments. 
 
• MIS-PDPS: This component of the Scheme provides for making Price 
Deficiency Payment for horticulture crops whenever the market prices fall below 
the Market Intervention Price, where the State Government does not have to 
do any physical procurement.  
 
• Transportation and storage subsidy for Tomato, Onion and Potato (TOP) 
crops: This component makes provision for providing transportation and 
storage subsidy to Central Nodal Agencies and State designated agencies for 
procurement of TOP crops from farmers where prices are below MIP and 
transport it to other locations where prevailing prices are high.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST JULY, 2026 
 
EXPANSION AND INTEGRATION OF e-ENAM AND ALLIED PLATFORMS 
 
247. Shri Kali Charan Singh: 
Shri Radheshyam Rathiya: 
Shri Chavda Vinod Lakhamshi: 
Shri Praveen Patel: 
Shri Arun Govil: 
Shri Shashank Mani: 
Dr. Nishikant Dubey: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण मंğी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of expansion and integration of Electronic-National Agriculture Market (e-
NAM) and allied platforms during 2026; 
 
(b) the number of mandis and States integrated under the platform; 
 
(c) whether inter-State trade and price discovery mechanisms have improved under the 
platform and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the details of measures taken to enhance farmers' access to remunerative markets and 
reduce dependence on intermediaries particularly for Meerut and adjoining areas? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी  (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a): The Government is implementing National Agriculture Market (e-NAM), a pan-India 
electronic trading platform, to facilitate transparent and competitive online trading of 
agricultural commodities. Integration of Mandis on e-NAM is done on the basis of proposals 
received from States/Union Territories (UTs).   From January to June, 2026, 134 mandis of 
5 States/UTs have been integrated with the e-NAM platform.   
 
(b):   As on 30th June, 2026, 1656 mandis from 23 States and 4 UTs have been integrated 
with e-NAM.  
 
  

 
 
 
 
(c) & (d):  The Government has taken several measures to enhance farmers' access to 
remunerative markets and reduce their dependence on intermediaries. Mandis integrated 
with the e-NAM platform provide farmers access to a larger pool of buyers, transparent 
online bidding, better price discovery and direct payment of sale proceeds into their bank 
accounts. The platform also facilitates inter-State trade by enabling buyers across the 
country to participate in transparent online bidding, thereby promoting competitive price 
discovery and better price realization for farmers.   
 
In Meerut and adjoining districts of Hapur, Ghaziabad, Bagpat, Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor 
and Amroha in Uttar Pradesh, 9 mandis have been integrated with e-NAM. 
 
 Till June, 2026, inter-State trade of 28,566 metric tonnes valued at approximately 
₹83.95 crore, has been recorded on e-NAM. 
 
 In addition, the Department is promoting Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) 
under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs to 
strengthen farmers' collective marketing, improve market linkages with value chain partners, 
organized retailers, institutional buyers and digital platforms, and enable aggregation of 
produce for better bargaining power and economy of scale. 
 
In Meerut, Hapur, Ghaziabad, Bagpat, Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor and Amroha, 62 
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been registered with 43,226 member farmers.

PRICE SUPPORT SCHEME IN TAMIL NADU 
248. SHRI C N ANNADURAI 
     DR. RANI SRIKUMAR 
     SHRI SELVAM G: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष और िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has implemented the Price Support Scheme (PSS) in Tamil 
Nadu for procurement of notified agricultural commodities at Minimum Support Price (MSP), 
if so, the details thereof; 
 
(b) the details of commodities covered under the Scheme, quantity procured and funds 
allocated, released and utilised in Tamil Nadu during the last three years and the current 
year, district-wise; 
 
(c) the number of farmers benefited under the Scheme in the State, commodity and year-
wise; 
 
(d) whether the Government has received complaints regarding delays in procurement, 
inadequate procurement centres and delayed payments to farmers in Tamil Nadu, if so, the 
corrective measures taken thereon; and 
 
(e) the steps taken to strengthen procurement infrastructure, expand coverage and ensure 
remunerative prices to farmers in Tamil Nadu under the Price Support Scheme? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी   (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (e) : The Price Support Scheme (PSS) under PM-AASHA is implemented on the request 
of State Government for procurement of Prescribed Fair Average Quality (FAQ) of notified 
pulses (Arhar, Moong, Urad, Gram and Masur), oil seeds (Groundnut, Soybean, Sunflower, 
Sesamum, Nigerseed, Rapeseed/Mustard-seed and Safflower) and Copra (Ball copra & 
Milling Copra) at Minimum Support Price (MSP) through designated Central Nodal 
Agencies(CNAs). During last three years, in Tamil Nadu, under PSS, Moong, Urad and Copra 
have been procured. MSP Payment is made directly to the farmers' bank accounts through 
the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism by CNAs. The losses, if any, incurred in the 
implementation of the Scheme are reimbursed to the CNAs in accordance with the Scheme 
guidelines. The details of commodities wise quantity procured, MSP value paid to farmers 
and the number of farmers benefitted in Tamil Nadu during the last three years and current 
year is placed at Annexure. As per Government of Tamil Nadu, no complaints have been 
received regarding delays in procurement, inadequacy of procurement centres or delay in 
payment to farmers under PSS. As per the Scheme guidelines, necessary publicity is 
undertaken by the State Governments, CNAs and State agencies regarding the prescribed 
FAQs specifications, procurement schedule and procurement centres to facilitate 
participation of farmers in the procurement operations.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COOPERATION 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 249 
 TO BE ANSWERED ON 21ST JULY, 2026 
  
Meri Samiti Mera Patal 
 
†249. Shri Miteshbhai Rameshbhai Patel: 
 
Will the Minister of COOPERATION (सहकारिता मंत्री) be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the objectives of the "Meri Samiti, Mera Patal" initiative; 
(b) the manner in which the recently launched "Meri Samiti, Mera Patal" digital portal will 
transform the functioning and public outreach of cooperative societies in North India;  
(c)  the plan being formulated by the Government to extend this portal to all cooperative 
societies across the country; 
(d) whether any tangible benefits in areas such as identity, transparency and digital adoption 
are expected in Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Self -Help Groups (SHGs); 
and  
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF COOPERATION 
सहकारिता मंत्री (SHRI AMIT SHAH) 
  
(a) The “Meri Samiti Mera Patal” is an initiative which has been independently 
conceptualized and launched by Regional Institute of Cooperative Management (RICM), 
Chandigarh under National Council for Cooperative Training (NCCT). The objective of the 
“Meri Sam iti – Mera Patal” is to empower and modernize Primary Agricultural Credit 
Societies (PACS) by addressing their training needs, improving governance, and enhancing 
visibility. 
 
(b) This initiative facilitates creation of digital profiling of PACS and centralized, 
transparent, real-time data system to support informed decision -making. The implementation 
covers the jurisdiction of RICM Chandigarh, covering Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pra desh, 
Jammu & Kashmir, Delhi, Chandigarh, and Leh-Ladakh by RICM Chandigarh. 
 
(c) At present there is no such proposal to expand this portal across the country. 
 
(d) & (e) The following tangible benefits are expected in the implemented areas for PACS / 
Multi-purpose Cooperative Societies (MPCS) under this initiative:  

 
• Identity and Transparency:  Each PACS/MPCS expects to have a digital profile 
showcasing its history, membership, services offered, schemes availed, and governance 
structure. 
• Public Visibility: The initiative expects to enhance the visibility of PACS/MPCS in 
the public domain. 
• Real-time Data Transparency:  The initiative expects to promote transparency by 
enabling access to real-time data.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 25 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
WELFARE OF MIGRANT WORKERS  
 
25. SHRI ATUL GARG:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
  
(a)whether the comprehensive implementation of the e-Shram portal 
has successfully integrated millions of unorganized and migrant 
workers from Uttar Pradesh into the formal social security net;  
(b)if so, the total number of agricultural labourers and out -of-state 
migrant workers successfully registered from the said State as of 
June 2026;  
(c)whether the said systematic database has enabled the seamless, 
direct transfer of emergency financia l assistance and accidental 
insurance benefits to daily -wage earners and if so, the details 
thereof;  
(d)the details of the proactive coordination with the State 
Government of Uttar Pradesh to ensure that registered workers 
easily access benefits under the  Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi 
Maandhan pension scheme (PM-SYM); and  
(e)the future steps planned by the Government to establish dedicated 
registration helpdesks at major railway stations to assist illiterate 
migrant workers originating from Uttar Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 th August, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal 
registers the unorganised workers including gig and platform workers 
and provides them a Univer sal Account Number (UAN) on a self -
declaration basis.  
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  As on 14 th July 2026, over 31.78 crore unorganised 
workers have already been registered on eShram portal. 
  Total number  of agricultural labourers and out -of-state 
migrant workers registered in Uttar Pradesh as on 14.07.2026 are 
4,08,19,704 and 2,51,376 respectively.  
 
  In keeping with the vision of the Budget Announcement 
2024-25 on developing eShram as a One -Stop-Solution for 
unorganized workers to have access to various social security 
schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram –
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram – “One-Stop-
Solution” entails integration of different social security/ welfare 
schemes at single portal i.e. eShram. This enable s unorganised 
workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and 
see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
  So far, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ 
Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram 
to extend benefits and access to social security, insurance or skill 
development programmes to eShram cardholders including Pradhan 
Mantri Street Vendors Atmanirbhar Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), Pradhan 
Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti 
Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit Bharat -Guarantee for Rozgar and 
Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB -G RAM G), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan 
Arogya Yojana (AB -PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One Nation One 
Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana 
(PMMVY), etc.

MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 26 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
SOCIAL SECURITY COVERAGE UNDER E-SHRAM PORTAL 
 
26. SHRI AZAD KIRTI JHA:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the number of gig and platform workers registered on the e-Shram   
portal as of September 2025 in the country, State/UT-wise;  
(b)the number of the said workers covered under any other so cial 
security scheme or insurance benefit;  
(c)whether the Government has fixed any timeline for rolling out 
social protection measures for platform workers; and  
(d)if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26th August 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
seeded with Aadhaar. eShram portal is meant to register and support 
the unorganised workers by providing them a Universal Account 
Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. 
  As on 14 th July 2026, over 31.78 crore unorganised 
workers have already been registered on eShram portal. 
  State-wise details of gig and platform workers registered 
on eShram Portal as of September 2025 is at annexure -I.  Details of 
gig and platform workers registered on eShram portal enrolled under 
various social welfare schemes is at annexure-II. 
  In keeping  with the vision of the Budget Announcement 
2024-25 on developing eShram as a One -Stop-Solution for 
unorganized workers to have access to various social security 
schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram– 
Contd..2/- 

 
:: 2 :: 
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram – “One-Stop-
Solution” entails integration of different social security/ welfare 
schemes at single portal i.e. eShram. This enables unorganised 
workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and 
see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
  So far, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ 
Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram 
to enhance social security coverage to unorganised workers, such as 
Pradhan Mantri  Street Vendors Atmanirbhar Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), 
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Pradhan Mantri 
Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit Bharat -Guarantee for 
Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Pradhan Mantri 
Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri 
Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 
(PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), 
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One Nation One 
Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradh an Mantri Matru Vandna Yojana 
(PMMVY), etc. 
  Apart from the above, eShram has linkages with National 
Career Service (NCS) for Job Opportunities, Skill India Digital Hub 
(SIDH) for Skill Development, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -dhan 
(PM-SYM) for Pension and convergence portal of MoHUA. 
  For the first time the definition of 'gig workers and 
'platform workers and provisions related to the same have been 
provided in the Code on Social Security, 2020 which has come into 
force on 21.11.2025.  
  The Code provides for framing of suitable social security 
measures for gig workers and platform workers on matters relating 
to life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection, etc. The Code provides for setting up of 
a Social Security Fund to finance these welfare schemes for which 
one of the sources is contribution from aggregators between 1 to 2% 
of annual turnover of an aggregator subject to the limit of 5% of the 
amount paid or payable by an aggregator to such workers. The Code 
also has provisions to constitute a National Social Security Board for 
the purposes of the welfare of gig workers and platform workers.  
 
Contd..3/- 

:: 3 :: 
  Further, the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, notified 
on 08.05.2026, mark a sign ificant step towards extending formal 
social protection to gig and platform workers. The Rules 
operationalize the provisions of the Code by mandating registration 
of gig and platform workers on the Central Government portal, 
requiring aggregators to share worker-related data through API or 
other electronic means, prescribing eligibility criteria for social 
security benefits, and strengthening accountability of aggregators in 
relation to welfare measures for such workers.  
  The Ministry of Labour & Employme nt has conducted 
multiple rounds of deliberations with Aggregators, Knowledge 
Partners, Platform Workers Associations, State Government/Union 
Territories and other organisations for social security framework of 
gig and platform workers to move forward for a comprehensive 
welfare scheme for platform workers across the country, as 
mandated under the Code.

(a)  whether the Government is considering setting up of a Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) in 
the Darbhanga Lok  Sabha constituency of Bihar to provide skill training to rural youth, women, 
traditional artisans and neo-literates/school dropouts, and if so, the details thereof;

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 29 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Increasing of Education Budget 
 
29. Shri Rajesh Naranbhai Chudasama: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the steps taken by Government to ensure that the increased spending on education leads to 
measurable improvements in learning outcomes across primary, secondary, and higher 
education sectors; 
 
(b) the extent to which the current education budget dire ctly address the needs of students 
from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and other disadvantaged backgrounds; 
 
(c) the details of Government's plan to strengthen public-private partnerships to bridge gaps in 
infrastructure and resource availability without compromising on the quality of education; and 
 
(d) the details of measures taken by Government to ensure access to quality digital education 
for students in rural areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a): Education is in the concurrent list and both the central government and State 
Governments work together for its improvement.  Central Government has constantly 
increased the Budget Allocation of the Ministry of Education from Rs.93,224.31 crore in F.Y . 
2021-22 to Rs. 1,39,289.48 crore in 2026-27.  
 
The PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan  (PRS) 2024 was conducted in December 2024 
to measure the baseline performance under NEP 2020 in the development of competencies 
among students at the end of Foundational, Preparatory and Middle Stages of Education i.e. 
Grades 3, 6 and 9 respectively. Over  21.15 lakh students and 2.70 lakh teachers and school 
leaders from more than 74,000 schools across 781 districts in all States and Union Territories 
participated in the survey 
 

In Higher Education, t o make the curricula relevant to contemporary industry 
demands and technological advancements, various initiatives / reforms have been carried out 
in higher education such as  National Credit Framework (NCrF); National Higher Education 
Qualification Framework  (NHEQF); Curriculum and Credit Framework for Undergra duate 
Programme; guidelines on Professor of Practice to enable HEIs to work with industry experts. 
Curriculum is also being  updated for academic programmes in alignment with ‘Future of 
Work’ job requirements in  the area of Agriculture, Health & Bio -electronics, Banking, 
Financial Services & Insurance  (BFSI), Energy, Logistics, Digital & Creative Economy, AI 
in Engineering and Manufacturing & Industry. 
 
With an objective of Research & Development driven integration of academic, 
industry 
and enterprise creation, Research Parks have been set up in premier HEIs including eight IITs 
and IISc Bengaluru to establish research ecosystem around these institutions. These research  
parks facilitate funded research from Industry, promoting Industry -Academia collaborations. 
To attract the best minds to pursue high - quality research in India's premier academic  
institutions, the Government launched Prime Minister’s Research Fellows (PMRF)  Scheme 
in 2018-19 with total financial outlay of Rs. 1650 Crores. The scheme was launched to attract 
the best and brightest minds to pursue high – quality research in India’s premier academic  
institutions with enhanced financial support which includes fellowship and research grant.  
Under PMRF, 3688 scholars have been admitted. The firs t phase of PMRF has led to better  
outcomes of research and thus, 10,000 fellowships have been announced under PMRF in  
Budget 2025-26 for technological research with enhanced financial support 
 
National Education Policy (NEP)  guided initiatives by Government of India have led 
to significant improvements in the performance of  Indian HEIs  in international rankings, 
including the QS World University Rankings (QS WUR). 54  Indian Institutions have been 
ranked in the QS WUR 2026. The number of Indian HEIs  featuring in  the QS World 
University Rankings has doubled in the past five years, rising from 27 in QS  WUR 2021 to  
54 in QS WUR 2026, thus underscoring sustained policy initiatives,  strengthened research 
and innovation capacity, and the steadily rising gl obal profile of  India’s higher education 
system. In QS  World University Rankings, Asia 2026 India has  second most representation, 
with 294 universities, up  from 163 in 2025 and 7 institutions in  the top 100. The QS Subject 
Rankings for 2025 included 79  Indian HEIs, an increase of 10  from the previous year's 69. 
India’s ranking in the Global Innovation  Index (GII) has also  propelled from 48 in 2020 and 
currently being ranked at 38th place in 2025. 
 
(b): The Government is implementing various scholarship sche mes for students, including 
those belonging to marginalized sections. The details of these schemes including the number 
of slots, assistance offered and eligibility criteria are available in the following websites: 
S.No. Ministry/Department Website Links 
1 Department of Higher 
Education 
https://www.education.gov.in/en/scholarships-
education-loan-0  

 
The scholarship schemes are spread across the country for all students, so that t he 
students can avail benefits of the scheme as per schematic norms, thereby reduce financial 
barriers for higher education aspirants. In the year 2024 -25, more than 95 lakhs students 
pursuing post-matric and higher education have received scholarships, am ounting to nearly ₹ 
10,913 crores. These schemes envisage that no deserving and meritorious student is denied 
the opportunity to pursue education because of financial constraints. As a result, the Gross 
Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education has increas ed to 30 in 2023-24 compared to 23.7 
in 2014-15. 
 
(c): As Education is in the concurrent list, the Centre and States are working together to 
increase the public investment in education sector to reach 6% of Gross Domestic Product 
(GDP) at the earliest.  
 
National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 calls for the rejuvenation, active promotion, 
and support for  private philanthropic activity in the education sector. In particular, over and 
above the public budgetary support which would have been otherwise provided to them, any 
public institution can take initiatives towards raising private philanthropic funds to enhance 
educational experiences. 
 
In pursuance of the budget announcement 2025 -26, Government has approved

education for additional 6,500 students.

National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) including platform 
workers, migrant workers etc. The e -Shram porta l registers the 
unorganised workers including gig and platform workers and provides them 
a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis.

Constituency in Odisha.

details of unorganised workers registered on eShram portal including in 
Pali and Shahdol districts is at annexure-I,II and III.

State/UTs on 29th January 2025 to empower them with their own dedicated 
eShram Microsite to address unique local requirements and challenges 
effectively. These Microsites are designed to tailor services of eShram to 
align with unique State /UTs needs, simplifying worker registration, data 
updates, verification and providing State specific analytics.

25 on developing eShram as a One -Stop-Solution for unorganized workers 
to have access to various  social  security  schemes,  Ministry of   Labour

and Employment launched the eShram –“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st

unorganised workers registered on eShram to ac cess social security 
schemes and see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram.

been introduced via Common Service Centres (CSCs), State Sewa Kendras

and locally tailored communication efforts. To further strengthen outreach, 
the Ministry leverages social media channels to disseminate videos, 
tutorials, and other informative content, making the initiative more

extensive network of skill development centres  under various schemes, viz. Pr adhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country  including the Ganjam and 
Gajapati districts of Odisha. The SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future -ready, 
equipped with industry-relevant skills.

covering the entire value chain of textiles, excluding Spinning and Weaving in organized sector. 
Samarth is being implemented on PAN India basis.
