GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.79 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
ASSESSMENT OF INDIA'S TOURISM SECTOR 
 
79. SHRI BAJRANG MANOHAR SONWANE: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that despite substantial 
expenditure on tourism promotion and infrastructure, India's 
tourism sector has not achieved its full potential compared to 
several other countries; 
(b) whether the Government has conducted any comparative 
assessment of India's tourism sector with leading global tourist 
destinations to identify gaps in infrastructure, connectivity, visitor 
facilities, promotion and ease of travel; 
(c) whether the Government proposes to formulate and implement a 
comprehensive strategy to enhance domestic and international 
tourist arrivals by adopting global best practices; and  
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the timeline for implementation 
and the expected outcomes?             
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM      (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Tourism maintains the data on International 
Tourists Arrivals (ITAs) and Domestic T ourist Visits (DTVs) as provided 
by the Bureau of Immigration (BoI ) and State/ UTs, respectively. The 
ITAs increased from 1.31 crore in 2014 to 2.06 crore in 2024 registering 
a growth of 56.93%. Similarly, the DTVs have also increased from 128.28 
crore in 2014 to 294.53 crore in 2024 thereby registering a growth of 
129.60%. The data indicates substantial improvement in tourist footfall 
during the last decade.   
 
According to the latest UN’s World Tourism Barometer, India's 
global share of International Tourist Arrivals has seen an increase from 

1.15% in 2014 to 1.41% in 2024. The International Tourists Arrivals of 
top 5 countries, in terms of ITAs, is at ANNEXURE. 
 
Further, in the World Economic Forum's (WEF) Travel and Tourism 
Development Index (TTDI) 2024, India improved its position 
significantly, ranking 39th globally out of 119 countries (up from 65th in 
2013) and holding the 1st position among SAARC countries. 
 
To conduct comparative assessments and identify structural 
barriers, the Ministry of Tourism has undertaken a detailed analysis of 
the TTDI 2024 edition to identify data gaps, methodological limitations, 
and areas requiring policy and institutional interventions.  
 
Additionally, this Ministry has also developed a competitive "State 
Tourism Performance Framework" allowing the States and Union 
Territories to objectively identify gaps in their tourism sector and 
inducing healthy competition to improve infrastructure, connectivity, 
and visitor facilities, which will ultimately further improve India's overall 
position in global rankings. 
 
(c) & (d): The Ministry of Tourism is undertaking various initiatives 
with the objective to promote tourism to the country in association with 
the Indian Missions, State Governments and Union Territory 
Administrations and the travel trade industry.  The Ministry is 
undertaking several activities such as participation in various global 
travel trade exhibitions and Marts, organization of familiarization tours 
for the foreign tour operators, media personnel, social media 
influencers, organization of India Food Festivals o verseas, organization 
of trade events with the local tour operators and industry stakeholders, 
promotion of tourist destinations, products and festivals through social 
media outreach, etc.

Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Youth Affairs 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 8 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
NYV Scheme and NYKS Programmes in Himachal Pradesh 
 
8. MS KANGNA RANAUT: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the long-term outcomes 
of programmes under the  National Youth Volunteers (NYV) Scheme 
and Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) in Himachal Pradesh; 
 
(b) if so, the key findings regarding their impact on youth 
participation, skills and community engagement; 
 
(c) the details of number of volunteers who secured employment, 
pursued higher education or took up leadership roles thereafter; 
 
(d) whether any third-party evaluation has been conducted; and 
 
(e) if so, the details of its findings and action taken thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS 
[DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA] 
 
(a) &  (b) The National Youth Corps (NYC) Scheme aims to engage 
disciplined and dedicated youth volunteers in nation -building 
activities while providing them opportunities for personality 
development, skill enhancement, community engagement and 
exposure to public service. MY Bharat (erstwhile NYKS) implements 
various youth development and community service programmes 
across the country, including Himachal Pradesh.  
 

Page 2 of 3 
 
 
The Ministry periodically reviews the implementation of the Scheme 
through reports submitted by MY Bharat, review meetings and 
monitoring mechanisms. Apart from these, the third-party evaluation 
of the schemes is done at regular frequency. 
 
The volunteers under NYC Scheme have played an important role in 
mobilizing youth, strengthening Youth Clubs and Mahila Mandals, 
disseminating information on Government programmes, and 
supporting awareness campaigns on health, education, environment 
and other flagship i nitiatives, thereby promoting active youth 
participation at the grassroots level. 
 
The programmes under MY Bharat (erstwhile NYKS) have contributed 
to promote youth participation in community development and 
nation-building activities, while enhancing lead ership qualities, 
communication skills, teamwork, social responsibility and 
community engagement among youth. 
 
(c) The primary aim of the National Youth Corps (NYC) scheme is to 
empower young men and women to serve up to two years in nation -
building activi ties while developing their leadership qualities and 
facilitating social and economic development. 
  
The NYC Scheme does not maintain a centralized database regarding 
the employment, higher education or leadership positions attained by 
volunteers after completion of their tenure. However, volunteers who 
complete their tenures are advised to get involved in community 
development/social service activities at their own level using the 
acquired leadership qualities. 
 
(d) & (e) Yes, a Third Party Evaluation of t he Rashtriya Yuva 
Sashaktikaran Karyakram (RYSK), involving the evaluation of its sub-
schemes including National Youth Corps (NYC), has been carried out 
during FY 2025 -26 by the National Institute of Public Finance and 
Policy (NIPFP), New Delhi. 
 

Page 3 of 3 
 
The evaluation records that volunteers under the NYC Scheme play a 
significant role in the grassroots implementation of flagship 
government programmes, including Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, 
plantation drives and health and road -safety campaigns. Volunteers 
contributed d uring emergencies such as floods and the COVID -19 
pandemic, and functioned as a link between Youth Clubs, MY Bharat 
and district administration, strengthening institutional linkages and 
community trust. 
 
The report suggests the increase in sanctioned stren gth for better 
outreach and recommends that the honorarium be increased to a 
reasonable amount, ensuring that volunteers are adequately 
compensated for their workload and encouraged to perform their 
duties effectively at the grassroots level. The suggestio ns of the 
third-party evaluation, to the extent possible, has been incorporated 
in the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) Memorandum for the 16th 
Finance Commission cycle.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 80 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
LiFE Movement and Climate Action Initiatives 
 
80. SHRI ANANTA NAYAK; 
SHRI LUMBARAM CHOUDHARY; 
SHRI VIJAY KUMAR DUBEY; 
SHRI NALIN SOREN; 
DR. NISHIKANT DUBEY; 
SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY; 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the progress made under the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) Movement since its launch and the 
major activities undertaken thereunder; 
(b) the key achievements in climate action, including progress towards Nationally Determined 
Contributions (NDCs), expansion of renewable energy capacity and reduction in emission intensity; 
(c) whether any projects or awareness programmes under the LiFE Movement or other climate 
initiatives have been implemented in Keonjhar Lok Sabha Constituency, Odisha, if so, the details 
thereof and the funds allocated therefor; and 
(d) the manner in which these initiatives are contributing towards the objective of becoming a 
developed nation and achieving net-zero emissions by 2070? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) and (c): Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) aims to nudge individuals and communities to 
practice a lifestyle that is synchronous with nature through Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-
Society approach focusing on seven themes viz., Save Energy, Save Water, Reduce Waste, Reduce 
E-Waste, Say No to Single Use Plastic, Adopt Healthy Lifestyles and Adopt Sustainable Food 
Systems. The major activities undertaken under Mission LiFE since its launch in October, 2022 
include the following : 
 
 Nationwide mass mobilization campaigns such as “One Nation One Mission: End 
Plastic Pollution”, “Harit Yoga” (on the eve of International Day of Yoga 2025), Swachhata Hi Sewa 
campaigns, World Environment Day pre-campaigns, etc have been undertaken to create awareness 
on Mission LiFE. The flagship “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative has resonated with one and all and 
over 272 Crore saplings have been planted under the same. 

 Mission LiFE principles added to India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) 
under the Paris Agreement. 
 Under the Ministry’s Environment Education Programme, students actively participate in 
workshops, nature camps, exhibitions, competitions, and summer programmes promoting sustainable 
habits. The Environment Information, Awareness, Capacity Building and Livelihood Programme 
(EIACP) Centres under the Ministry also organize mass outreach and capacity-building activities on 
various themes of Mission LiFE.  
 Large scale youth mobilization initiatives through campaigns such as Ideas4LiFE, e-waste 
awareness and reduction campaign, and various other large-scale awareness activities through MyGov 
portal, etc. are also being undertaken.  
 A10-day Experiential Learning Program on Mission LiFE on My Bharat portal of 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports was successfully completed to provide hands on learning 
experience to youth. 
 Over 12 lakh Eco-Clubs for Mission LiFE have been promoting behavioural change 
among children and youth by promoting environmental awareness and sustainable lifestyle practices 
in schools.  
 Two dedicated digital platforms have been launched by the Ministry – the Mission LiFE 
Portal as a knowledge repository and the Meri LiFE Portal for structured reporting and monitoring of 
LiFE events and activities. So far, over 7.3 crore people participated in more than 40 Lakh LiFE 
events across the country, which includes 100279 participants in 3428 LiFE related awareness and 
action events in Keonjhar in Odisha during the last 2 years.  
 Mission LiFE has been showcased through dedicated LiFE pavilions featuring interactive 
digital displays, Virtual Reality experiences, and live demonstrations at major national events 
including Bharat Parv, Swachh Vayu Diwas, India Water Week, G20 ECSWG meetings, Maha 
Kumbh Mela, and World Environment Day 2025, etc.  
 India has also played a pivotal role in advancing the global discourse on sustainable 
lifestyles through key international milestones.  
 At the Sixth Session of the United Nations Environment Assembly (UNEA-6) held in 
Nairobi, Kenya on 1 March 2024, India’s resolution on “Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles”, co-
sponsored by Sri Lanka and Bolivia, was unanimously adopted.  
 India's resolution on “Promoting Sustainable Lifestyles for the Wise Use of Wetlands”, 
was adopted at the Ramsar 15th Conference of Parties held in Zimbabwe on 30 July 2025. 
 India also secured a position on the Board of the 10-Year Framework of Programmes on 
Sustainable Consumption and Production Patterns (10YFP) for the term 2024-26 and again for 2026-
28. India has also assumed the role of the Co-chair at the Board further strengthening its global agenda 
of promoting sustainable lifestyles. 
Over the years, Mission LiFE has evolved into a major platform for international cooperation on 
sustainable lifestyles, which has been acknowledged at major global forums including the Sharm El-
Sheikh Implementation Plan (COP27), the G7 Communiqué, and the G20 New Delhi Leaders’ 
Declaration, reaffirming India’s global climate leadership and the Mission’s universal relevance. 
 

(b) and (d)   India has made significant progress in climate action and is steadily advancing towards 
achieving its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. The details 
are as given below: 
 As reported in India's First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR-1) submitted to the 
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the emissions intensity of 
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) declined by 37.38 per cent in 2022 compared to the 2005 level.  
 Forest and tree cover has also expanded consistently, resulting in the creation of an 
additional carbon sink of 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent between 2005 and 2022.  
 India has also achieved the milestone of meeting more than 50 per cent of its cumulative 
installed electric power capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy sources, five years ahead of the 
2030 target.  
 The Government has implemented several flagship initiatives and schemes such as PM 
Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, National Green Hydrogen Mission, promotion of nuclear energy, 
domestic manufacturing of solar photovoltaic (PV) modules and batteries, and the Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) to strengthen India's clean energy ecosystem and supporting low-carbon industrial 
growth. 
 The Government is also promoting Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) 
technologies for hard-to-abate sectors. 
 India has further strengthened global climate action through initiatives such as the 
International Solar Alliance (ISA), Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), Global 
Biofuel Alliance, and Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT).  
 To mobilize climate finance and support low-carbon development, measures such as 
Sovereign Green Bonds, the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, etc. have been introduced.  
 On the adaptation front, the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and the 
aligned State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs), along with programmes for climate-
resilient water and agriculture sectors, heat action plans, and improved disaster early warning systems, 
are enhancing resilience and strengthening water, food and livelihood security while reducing 
climate-related losses. 
The above climate initiatives are strategically aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and the 
commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070. Guided by the principles of equity and common 
but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC), these measures—
formalized in the Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS)—
simultaneously drive economic growth, energy security, and industrial competitiveness. By fostering 
technological innovation and strengthening the resilience of communities and infrastructure, these 
initiatives reduce climate vulnerability and safeguard development gains, facilitating India's transition 
into a developed nation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 81 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Water Pollution by Industrial Effluents 
 
81. SHRI KULDEEP INDORA: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the industrial waste emitting from textile and steel units is flowing into Sutlej, Luni, 
Jojri and Bandi rivers; 
(b) whether complaints have been received regarding illegal discharge of untreated chemical waste 
bypassing Common Effluent Treatment Plants situated at Punjab (particularly Ludhiana), Balotra 
and Pali; 
(c) whether any scientific assessment of Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) and level of heavy metals in 
ground water has been carried out in more than Fifty affected villages of Sri Ganganagar-
Hanumangarh and Jodhpur-Barmer region; 
(d) the action taken under the "Polluter Payment Principle" against the violating units in the recent 
inspections; and 
(e) the time bound action plan of the Government for river rejuvenation and long-term 
environmental protection? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a): The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) regulates air and water 
quality by enactment of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, the Air 
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and 
notified Rules, Regulations based on the said acts. 
 
The MoEFCC vide G.S.R. 978(E), dated 10.10.2016 notified standards for treated effluent for 
integrated textile units, units of Cotton / Woollen / Carpets / Polyester, Units having Printing / 
Dyeing / Bleaching process or manufacturing and Garment units. The environmental standard for 
integrated iron and steel plants was notified vide G.S.R. 277(E), dated 31.03.2012. The concerned 
State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Pollution Control Committees (PCCs),  in respective States 
ensure the implementation and compliance of these standards. 
 
SPCBs/ PCCs, through Consent mechanism under the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981, 
monitor the establishment and operation of industries as well as polluting activities through 
prescription of pollution control measures and monitoring the compliance of environmental 
standards. 
 

(b): Complaints regarding untreated effluent bypassing Common Effluent Treatment Plants 
(CETPs) are examined through the concerned SPCBs and/or Central Pollution Control Board 
(CPCB) or through Hon’ble National Green Tribunal (NGT) also to assess the adequacy of treatment 
facilities and compliance status of Consent conditions issued by concerned SPCBs/PCCs and for 
taking appropriate action. 
 
In order to strengthen self-regulation, CETPs are mandated to install Online Continuous Effluent 
Monitoring Systems (OCEMS), for real-time monitoring and alert system with connectivity to the 
server of SPCBs/PCCs and CPCB. 
 
(c) and (d): As per the information provided by Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) regional-
scale groundwater-quality monitoring and scientific studies in accordance with the approved 
Standard Operating Procedure are undertaken by CGWB which is available in the Annual Ground 
Water Quality Report 2025. Further, it is conveyed that Environmental Compensation, as per 
Central Ground Water Authority Guidelines, has been imposed on 205 units in Sri Ganganagar, 
Hanumangarh, Jodhpur and Barmer districts for illegal extraction of ground water. 
 
(e): Steps taken by the Government for river rejuvenation and long-term environmental protection 
prevention and control of water pollution are given below-  
 
 The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), in coordination with SPCBs/PCCs, currently 
monitors water quality at 4,922 locations across the country, including 2,265 river locations.  
 The CPCB has identified polluted river stretches based on the water quality data for rivers with 
respect to Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) parameter. The PRS are classified under 
Priority Class I to V, Priority I being most polluted with BOD value of more than 30 mg/l and 
Priority V least polluted with BOD ranging between 3 – 6 mg/l.  
 Based on the identified PRS and for the rejuvenation of these PRS all State Governments and 
UT Administrations have formed River Rejuvenation Committees (RRCs) of the concerned 
states/ UTs.  
 The RRCs are responsible for developing action plans for the rejuvenation of the PRS identified 
by CPCB for their respective states/ UTs. The action plans including Industrial pollution control 
were prepared for bringing the water quality of polluted river stretches to the quality level fit for 
bathing purposes (i.e. BOD ˂ 3 mg/L). Progress of implementation of action plans are  reviewed 
by the RRC at State level and Central Monitoring Committee (CMC) constituted under the 
Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Jal Shakti at Central Level.  
 The Government notified general discharge standards and industry specific effluent discharge 
standards under Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986 with an aim to prevent pollution in the 
water bodies.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 83 
ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
Decreasing Enrolment of Students with Disabilities 
 
†83.  Shri Tanuj Punia:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the gross enrolment of students in primary and secondary education is decreasing 
and a large number of these children include children with disabilities in the country and 
if so, the efforts bei ng made by the Government to increase the enrolment of children 
with disabilities alongwith details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to provide free transport facility alongwith the 
recruitment of special educators and provision of ramps, lifts and  wheelchairs in all 
Government schools to increase the enrolment of children with disabilities; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c):  The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 in consonance with the provisions of the 
Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, envisages equitable and inclusive quality 
education for all children, including Children with Special Needs (CwSN). To achieve universal 
access to edu cation from pre -primary to Class XII, the Department of School Education & 
Literacy is implementing the centrally sponsored Samagra Shiksha scheme, which includes a 
dedicated component on Inclusive Education for CwSN. 
As per UDISE+, the overall enrolment of CwSN and enrolment at the secondary stage have 
shown a consistent increase over the last three years.  
To promote enrolment, retention and participation of CwSN, the Government has undertaken the 
following measures under Samagra Shiksha and other initiatives: 
1. Financial assistance of ₹3,500 per enrolled CwSN per annum , including children 
receiving home -based education, is provided for identification and assessment camps, 
aids and assistive devices, transportation, esco rt and scribe allowance, Braille and large -
print books, teaching-learning materials, and other support services.  

2. A stipend of ₹2,000 per annum (₹200 per month for 10 months) is provided to CwSN girl 
students through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to encourage school attendance.  
3. Samagra Shiksha provides financial support for creation of barrier -free infrastructure, 
including ramps and CwSN-friendly toilets.  
4. The Department has notified the Accessibility Code for Educational Institutions  on 10 
January 2024, which was incorporated under the Rules of the RPwD Act, 2016 on 20 
June 2024, to ensure accessible physical, information and communication infrastructure 
in educational institutions.  
5. To facilitate universal early screening and identification, the Department has developed 
PRASHAST (Pre -Assessment Holistic Screening Tool), a digital platform designed to 
screen all school-going children in the age group of 3–18 years for the early identification 
of 21 disabilities, including benchmark disabilities not ified under the Rights of Persons 
with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016. The platform serves as a critical first step towards 
ensuring timely support and appropriate educational planning for children requiring 
additional assistance. The application has been u pgraded through integration with 
UDISE+, enabling automatic onboarding of schools and key stakeholders, including 
Heads of Schools, teachers, special educators and students, thereby eliminating the need 
for manual data entry and significantly reducing the administrative burden on teachers. 
6. Since education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, recruitment and 
deployment of teachers, including special educators, in Government schools are 
undertaken by the respective States/UT s as per their requirements and applicable norms. 
The Department of School Education & Literacy has notified the Pupil -Teacher Ratio 
(PTR) for special educators in general schools vide Notification No. S.O. 4586(E) dated 
21.09.2022, prescribing one special educator for e very 10 CwSN at the primary level and 
one special educator for every 15 CwSN at the upper primary level. States and UTs 
undertake recruitment and placement of special educators in accordance with these 
notified norms. 
7. NCERT has developed accessible digital  learning resources on the DIKSHA platform in 
accordance with Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles, including Indian Sign 
Language (ISL)-based content, multilingual resources and assistive learning materials. A 
dedicated PM eVidya DTH Channel (Ch annel No. 31) telecasts educational content in 
Indian Sign Language for children with hearing impairment.  
8. CBSE promotes inclusive education through teacher capacity -building programmes, 
manuals and the Handbook on Inclusive Education. CBSE has also issued  guidelines 
mandating barrier -free infrastructure in affiliated schools and provides examination -
related exemptions and concessions to CwSN in accordance with the RPwD Act, 2016.

TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
WELFARE OF UNORGANISED WORKERS IN SIDHI AND 
SINGRAULI DISTRICTS 
 
†84. DR. RAJESH MISHRA:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the total number of unorganised workers registered so far on the 
e-Shram portal in Sidhi and Singrauli districts;  
(b)whether the registered workers are receiving the benefits of social 
security and schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi 
Maandhan Yojana and if so, the area -wise details of the 
beneficiaries;  
(c)the special measures taken by the Government for housing and 
healthcare of migrant labourer's working in industrial areas s uch 
as Singrauli district;  
(d)whether there is any proposal under consideration to establish an 
Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Hospital or Dispensary in 
Singrauli district, and if so, the details thereof; and  
(e)the number of workers currently covered under ESI Scheme in the 
Sidhi Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (e): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 th August, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) 
including platform workers, migrant workers etc. The eShram portal 
registers the unorganised workers including gig and platform workers 
and provides them a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self -
declaration basis.  
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
  Over 31.78 crore unorganised workers have already been 
registered on eShram portal including over 4.29 lakhs registrations in 
Sidhi district and 3.89 lakhs registrations in Singrauli district. 
  Details of unorganised workers registered on eShram 
portal enrolled under various social security schemes in Sidhi and 
Singrauli districts is annexed. 
  
  In keeping with the vision of the Budget Announcement 
2024-25 on developing eShram as a One -Stop-Solution for 
unorganized workers to have access to various social security 
schemes, Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram –
“One-Stop-Solution” on 21st October 2024. eShram – “One-Stop-
Solution” entai ls integration of different social security/ welfare 
schemes at single portal i.e. eShram. This enables unorganised 
workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and 
see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
  So far, fifteen (15) schemes of different Central Ministries/ 
Departments have already been integrated/ mapped with the eShram 
to extend benefits and access to social security schemes to eShram 
cardholders including Pradhan Mantri Street Vendors Atmanirbhar 
Nidhi (PMSVANidhi), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), 
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Viksit Bharat -
Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB -G RAM G), 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Ayushman Bharat – 
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), Pradhan Mantri Awas 
Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana 
(PMMSY), Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM -KISAN), One 
Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandna 
Yojana (PMMVY), etc. 
 
  Apart from the above, eShram has linkages with National 
Career Service (NCS) for Job Opportunities , Skill India Digital Hub 
(SIDH) for Skill Development, Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan -dhan 
(PM-SYM) for Pension and convergence portal of MoHUA. 
 
  In order to safeguard the interest of the Migrant workers, 
Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and 
Conditions of Services) Act,1979 provided for registration of certain 
establishments employing Inter-State Migrant Workers and licensing 
of contractors. Workers employed with such establishment were to 
be provided payment of minimum wages, journey allowance, 
displacement allowance, residential accommodation, medical 
facilities and protective clothing etc. 
Contd..3/- 
 

 
:: 3 :: 
  This Act has now been subsumed in the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020. The OSH 
Code, provides for decent working conditions, minimum wages, 
grievance redressal mechanisms, toll free helpline, journey 
allowance, protectio n from abuse and exploitation and social 
security to all categories of organized and unorganized workers 
including migrant workers. With expanded social security, stronger 
protections and nationwide portability of entitlements, the codes 
place workers, esp ecially migrant workers firmly at the centre of 
labour governance.  
 
  The provisions of OSH Code applicable for migrant 
workers are detailed as under:   
 
  It shall be the duty of every contractor or the employer, of 
an establishment employing inter -State migrant workers in 
connection with the work of that establishment- 
 
(a) to ensure suitable conditions of work to such worker having 
regard to the fact that he is required to work in a State different from 
his own State;  
 
(b) in case of fatal accident or serious bodily injury to any such 
worker, to report to the specified authorities of both the States and 
also the next of kin of the worker;  
 
(c) to extend all benefits to such worker which are available to a 
worker of that establishment including benefits under the Employees' 
State Insurance Act, 1948 or the Employees' Provident Funds and 
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 or any other law for the time 
being in force and the facility of medical check -up as available to a 
worker under clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 6. 
 
(d) the employer shall pay, to every inter -State migrant worker 
employed in his establishment, in a year a lump sum amount of fare 
for to and fro journey to his native place from the place of his 
employment, in the manner taking into account the minimum service 
for entitlement, periodicity and class of travel and such other matters 
as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government.  
 
  Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has also 
launched Affordable Rental Housing Complexes  (ARHCs) a sub -
scheme of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -Urban (PMAY-U) to Address 
the accommodation needs of migrant workers. 
Contd..4/ 
 

:: 4 :: 
  A proposal regarding setting up of ESI Hospital in Singrauli 
District of Madhya Pradesh has been received from Smt. Radha Singh, 
Hon'ble Minister of State for Panchayat and Rural Development of 
Madhya Pradesh vide letter dated 26.06.2026, which has been 
received on 07.07.2026, for consideration. 
 
  The number of wo rkers currently covered under ESI 
Scheme in the Sidhi Lok Sabha Parliamentary Constituency is 26,335.

85. SHRI PARSHOTTAMBHAI RUPALA: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the details of the measures taken by Government to facilitate the 
implementation of higher pension benefits for eligible employees of 
exempted establishments under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 
1995 in accordance with the judgment of the Supreme Court of 
India in the Sunil Kumar (2022) case;  
(b)whether the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation has been

implementation of higher pen sion benefits in exempted 
establishments and if so, the features thereof;

(a) to (d): EPFO has taken action to implement the directions 
contained in the Hon'ble Supreme Court Judgment dated 04.11.2022 
in a time-bound manner. An online facility was provided for 
submission of applications by eligible pensioners/members for 
validation of Joint Options.

Teacher Vacancies in Government Schools 
 
87.  Dr. Amar Singh: 
 Shri Aashtikar Patil Nagesh Bapurao: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the shortage of teachers in Government schools in 
the country, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the total number of sanctioned and vacant teaching posts in Governmen t schools in the 
country, State/UT -wise and level -wise (Primary, Upper Primary, Secondary and Higher 
Secondary); 
(c) the number of teachers recruited during the last three years, year-wise and State/UT-wise; 
(d) whether the Government has assessed the impa ct of teacher vacancies on the quality of 
education and learning outcomes, particularly in rural, tribal and aspirational districts and if 
so, the details thereof; 
(e) the details of steps taken by the Government to assist States and Union Territories to 
improve teachers training and filling vacant teaching posts within a time-bound manner; and 
(f) whether the Government proposes to introduce any national framework or incentive 
mechanism to address persistent teacher shortages in Government schools and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (f): Education being a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution, the majority of 
schools in the country are under the administrative control of the respective State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Accordingly, the recruitment, service  
conditions and deployment of teachers fall within the administrative domain of the concerned 
States/UTs. Teacher vacancies arise from time to time due to factors such as retirement, 
resignation, creation of new posts, rationalisation of teacher deployment  and changes in 
enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts . The data relating to sanctioned 
strength, teachers in position, vacant teaching posts and recruitment of teachers, including 
State/UT-wise and level-wise details, is maintained by the respective State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations. 
 
 

 
 
As per the UDISE+ 2025-26, the State/UT-wise details of teachers in position in Government 
schools across the country are placed at Annexure,   
The Central Government periodically advises States/UTs to fill vacant posts through 
transparent and merit -based recruitment processes, including through autonomous teacher 
recruitment boards or similar mechanisms. The progress of recruitment is regularly reviewed 
through meeting s and advisories, with emphasis on competitive selection, consistency and 
technology-based teacher requirement planning and forecasting. 
Further, the Central Government provides financial assistance to States/UTs under Samagra 
Shiksha to maintain appropria te Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) at various levels of schooling in 
accordance with the norms prescribed under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory 
Education (RTE) Act, 2009. 
Para 2.3 of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020 emphasises maintaining a  PTR of 
under 30:1 in each school and under 25:1 in areas with a high proportion of socio -
economically disadvantaged students. As per UDISE+ 2025-26 report , the PTR at the 
national level stands at 19 at Primary level, 17 at Upper Primary level, 15 at Secon dary level, 
and 23 at the Higher Secondary level which is within the norms envisaged under NEP 2020. 
In order to attract and retain qualified teachers across the country, including in rural areas, a 
number of initiatives have been undertaken by the Governm ent to strengthen the quality of 
teacher education and professional development. These include the introduction of the four -
year Integrated Teacher Education Programme (ITEP); development of the guidelines on the 
National Professional Standards for Teacher s (NPST) defining competencies of teachers at 
different stages/levels; development of the guidelines on the National Mission for Mentoring 
(NMM) to strengthen mentoring and professional support for school teachers; ensuring 
continuous professional development of in-service teachers through the National Initiative for 
School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement (NISHTHA); and providing high -quality 
digital learning resources and e -content through the Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge 
Sharing (DIKSHA) platform.

DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 88 
ANSWERED ON 20/07/2026 
 
Inadequate Availability of UGC Research Fellowships 
 
88. Dr. Shashi Tharoor: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of candidates qualifying the UGC -NET examination, the number of Junior  
Research Fellowships (JRFs) awarded and the proportion of qualified candidates awarded 
JRFs during the last five years, year-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government ha s taken note of the increasing disparity between the number of  
candidates qualifying the UGC-NET examination and the number of JRFs awarded each year, 
if so, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to increase the number of JRFs or revis e the eligibility  
criteria, including the existing percentage -based cap, in order to accommodate the growing  
number of research aspirants, if so, the details thereof; and  
 
(d) whether the Government has also taken note that the amount of the UGC Non -NET 
Fellowship has remained unchanged at Rs. 8,000 per month since 2006 and if so, the steps  
taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to revise the fellowship along with the 
expected timeline for such revision? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (d): The University Grants Commission (UGC) provides the Junior Research Fellowship 
(JRF) based on the National Eligibility Test (NET). Six percent of the candidates who appear in 
the NET are qualified for Assistant Professor and out of these qualified candidates, UGC 
awards JRF for 11,750 slots per year. In addition, fellowships are also offered by different 
Ministries and Organizations to support the scholars pursuing Ph.D.  Special fellowships are 
provided for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Persons with 
Disabilities and Single Girl Child. The Ph.D. scholars are eligible to join research projects 
sanctioned by various funding agencies to the Universities and to avail of funding t o support 
their research, leading to the award of a Ph.D. 
Further, some students are admitted to Ph.D. courses by the Universities without 
financial support from any source. To enlarge the scope, UGC decided to partially support 
such students by providing a stipend in the form of non -NET Fellowships. These Non -NET 
Fellowships have been benefitting M.Phil./Ph.D. students enrolled in various Central 
Universities across the country, especially the students of Universities located in the remote 
areas and North-Eastern regions of the country.

MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 9 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 20.07.2026 
 
FOUR LABOUR CODES 
 
9.  SHRI K C VENUGOPAL:  
ADV DEAN KURIAKOSE:  
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state:  
 
(a)the current status of the implementation of the four Labour Codes; 
(b) whether there is any concerns regarding the same and if so, the 
details thereof addressed by the government with the  
stakeholders;  
(c) the details of the policy formulated by the Government to 
guarantee minimum wages, health insurance and strict social 
security benefits for the millions of gig and platform workers 
currently operating outside formal labour protections; and  
(d) the details of formal jobs created versus jobs lost in the 
manufacturing and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) 
during the last five years? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) & (b): The Government of India has implemented four Labour 
Codes, namely, the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations 
Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with 
effect from 2 1st November, 2025. The Central Rules under the said 
Labour Codes have been notified on 8th May, 2026. 
 
  Since ‘Labour’ falls under the concurrent subject, the 
States/UTs are also required to frame Rules under the Labour Codes. 
Accordingly, most of the States/UTs have already taken measures & 
have finalised or published/pre-published the Rules under the Labour 
Codes and a few are pre-publishing/finalising the Rules. 

(c) & (d): The Labour Codes were enacted to meet need for 
comprehensive labour reforms that  formalize employment, simplify 
compliance through digital integration, strengthen social Security 
and ensure workplace safety and equality. The Codes will provide 
universal minimum wages and social security benefits for workers.  
 
  The gig workers and th e platform workers have been 
defined for the first time in the Labour Code for the purpose of 
formulating schemes to provide social security benefits relating to 
life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity 
benefits, old age protection etc. 
 
  The Labour Codes have several enabling provisions which 
will promote formalisation and employment generation including 
social security and welfare of the workers. Such provisions include, 
formalization of employment through mandatory issue of appointment 
letter, universalisation of social security by extending coverage to 
organised, unorganised, gig and platform workers to strengthen their 
protection against employment -related vulnerabilities and enabling 
greater adaptability to new forms of wo rk like gig & platform work 
and technology-driven employment models.

92. Md. Rakibul Hussain: 
       
Will the MINISTER OF CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed financial assistance provided for major cultural 
festivals, fairs and traditional events in Assam during the last five years; 
 
(b) whether any reduction in allocation has been observed in recent years; 
 
(c) the impact of such reduction on local artists, performers and cultural workers; and 
 
(d) the details of the measures proposed to ensure sustained livelihood support for cultural 
practitioners? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) The Ministry of Culture provides financial assistance across the country, including the 
state of Assam, through various scheme components of Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana 
(KSVY),for the promotion, preservation and dissemination of art and cultureand periodically 
reviews the financial assistance provided under schemes via Expert/ Evaluation/ Steering 
Committee constituted under the respective schemes. The committees examine and reviews 
eligible proposals received for financial assistance under the various schemes, based on the 
past cultural performances/ activities undertaken by the applicants and other relevant factors, 
subject to scheme guidelines. 
 
(b)  As such, no specific State-wise allocation is earmarked for cultural festivals, fairs and 
traditional events. Funds are sanctioned/ recommended under the various scheme components 
of KSVY on the basis of number of eligible proposals received from organizations and the 
subsequent recommendations of the Expert/Evaluation/Steering Committee thereon, in 
accordance with the scheme guidelines. Funds released during last three financial years under 
KSVY is as under:

2023-24 218.36 
2024-25 201.67

continues to support artists, performers and cultural workers through various schemes and 
programmes implemented directly and through its autonomous organizations, including 
grants for cultural organizations, repertories, fellowships, scholarships and other promotional 
initiatives, subject to eligibility and availability of funds. 
 
(d) The Government supports the livelihood of cultural practitioners through financial 
assistance released under various schemes under Kala Sanskriti Vikas Yojana. Further, to 
protect, promote and preserve various forms of folk/ tribal art & culture throughout the 
country, the Government of India has set up seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) and 
various Akademieswhich organize various cultural activities and programmeson regular basis 
all over India. These ZCCs provide a platform to cultural practitioners by engaging them in 
various cultural programmes, festivals, workshops and exhibitions organized across their 
member States. These engagements enable artists to showcase their talent, gain wider 
exposure and preserve and promote traditional art forms. The artists are also provided 
honorarium, TA/DA, boarding and lodging, local transport etc. which help supplement their 
income and encourage them to pursue their art as a sustainable livelihood, thereby 
contributing to their self-reliance.

PM-USHA Support for Universities and College 
 
93. Shri Balashowry Vallabhaneni: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the aims and objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA) 
and the manner in which the scheme is supporting universities and colleges in the areas of  
education, research and infrastructure development; 
(b) whether it is a fact that Krishna University, Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, has been  
identified under PM -USHA and if so, the details of components under which funds are  
sanctioned, released and utilized along with the present status of the same; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that some proposals submitted by the Government of Andhra  
Pradesh under PM -USHA are under consideration of the Union Government and if so, the  
present status of such proposals; and 
(d) whether any proposal pertains to Krishna district and if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(Dr. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a): Education being in the Concurrent List, enhancing the quality of education is the 
responsibility of both the Central and State Governments . However, recognizing the need for 
central assistance, the Department of Higher Education, Government of India is 
implementing Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme 
aimed at funding specific State government universities  and colleges, so as to improve its 
quality by ensuring their conformity to prescribed norms and standards.  
The government  has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan 
(RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM -USHA), 
with an outlay of Rs. 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phases 
of RUSA , to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/ underserved areas.  Under the 
Scheme, support is provided to States/UTs for strengthening infrastructure, including 

construction of hostels, academic and administrative buildings, laboratories and other 
facilities required for improving access and quality in higher education.  
(b): Under the scheme, Krishna University, Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh has been 
approved under the Grants to Strengthen Universities (GSU) component of PM -USHA with a 
total approved amount of Rs. 20.00 crore. The approved proposal includes sub -components 
relating to infrastructure construction, infrastructure renovation, equipment procurement and 
soft components. 
(c): All the proposals submitted by the State of Andhra Pradesh on the PM -USHA Portal 
under various components were examined and placed before the Pr oject Approval Board 
(PAB) for its consideration and approval. Under the scheme, all the units have been 
approved and there are no pending proposals from the State.  Under the scheme, in the State 
of Andhra Pradesh, a total of 33 units have been approved for an amount of Rs. 378.75 
crore, including 7 Universities (1 under Multi-Disciplinary Education and Research 
Universities (MERU)  component and 6 under Grants to Strengthen Universit ies (GSU) 
component), 21 colleges under Grants to Strengthen Colleges (GSC) component and 5 
districts under Gender Inclusion and Equity Initiatives (GIEI) component.  
(d): Under PM -USHA, a total of four proposals pertaining to Krishna District of Andhra 
Pradesh were received on the PM -USHA portal. Out of these, three proposals have been 
approved under various components, including Krishna University, Machilipatnam (GSU 
component) for a total amount of Rs. 20.00 crore, Government Degree College, Bantumilli 
(GSC component) for a total amount of Rs. 5.00 crore  and the Krishna district for a total 
amount of Rs. 10.00 crore under GIEI component.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO 99 
ANSWERED ON 20/07/2026 
  
ESTABLISHMENT OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT CENTRES IN TAMIL NADU 
  
99.       SHRI THARANIVENTHAN M S: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the details of Skill Development Centres established, operational and upgraded across the 
country during the last five years and the current year, State/UT and year-wise, including Arani Lok 
Sabha Constituency of Tamil Nadu; 
 
(b)  the details of funds allocated, released and utilised for establishing and strengthening such 
Centres, along with the number of candidates trained, certified and placed therein, year-wise; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment of the effectiveness of such 
Centres in improving employability, addressing industry skill gaps and promoting self-employment 
and if so, the findings thereof;  
 
(d)  whether any vacancies of trainers, infrastructure deficiencies or implementation delays have 
been reported in such centres and if so, the corrective measures taken by the Government; and 
 
(e)  the steps taken by the Government to expand industry partnerships, modernise  training 
infrastructure, enhance digital and emerging technology courses and ensure equitable access to 
quality skill training, across the country, particularly in Tamil Nadu and other underserved regions?  
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b):  Under Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an extensive network 
of skill development centres  under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and 
Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections 
of the society across the country, including women in rural areas. SIM aims at enabling youth of 
India to get future ready and equipped with industry relevant skills.  
 
The schemes of MSDE are demand driven and training centres  under these schemes are set up 
or engaged on need basis. State-wise details of the number of training centres, including those in 
the Arani Lok Sabha Constituency (Tiruvannamalai and Viluppuram districts) of Tamil Nadu, 
engaged under the schemes of MSDE a re at Annexure-I. Year -wise detail of the candidates 
trained/certified under various schemes of MSDE is at Annexure-II. 
 
Amongst the schemes of MSDE, placements were tracked under the Short -Term Training 
component of PMKVY in the first three versions (PMKVY1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0) 
implemented from 2015-16 to 2021-22. Under PMKVY (1.0 to 3.0), 1.72 lakh candidates have been 
reported placed in Tamil Nadu.  In the current version of the Scheme i.e. PMKVY 4.0, the focus is 
to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career path and they are suitably oriented 
for the same through industry relevant skill courses that include On-the-Job Training (OJT). 

(c):  The Government undertakes periodic reviews of skilling initiatives under the Skill India 
Mission, assessing enrolment, certification, placement, self -employment outcomes and employer 
feedback to gauge their effectiveness in strengthening employability and future skills. These 
reviews support continuous curriculum updates, industry collaboration and improvements in 
implementation modalities, ensuring that skilling programmes remain aligned with evolving 
technology trends and labour-market requirements. The effectiveness of broader skill development 
schemes is also evaluated through MIS-based monitoring, third-party assessments and beneficiary 
feedback. 
 
PMKVY 4.0: An independent third-party impact evaluation of the PMKVY 4.0 has been conducted 
by Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM), an autonomous Institution of 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India in 2025. As per the report, PMKVY t raining has 
contributed to a measurable shift in employment outcomes for short term training (STT) candidates. 
The combined share of employed and self-employed STT respondents increased from 26.6% prior 
to training to 45.4% after PMKVY training, reflecting  an 18.8 percentage point increase. 41.4% of 
STT candidates and 48.9% of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) candidates reported an increase 
in income following training and certification. Overall, PMKVY 4.0 has significantly expanded 
access to formal skill training and certification and has generated measurable improvements in skill 
confidence, employment participation, and income outcomes for a substantial proportion of 
beneficiaries. 
 
JSS: A third-party evaluation of the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme was conducted by the 
Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJ NIFM), an autonomous Institution of 
Ministry of Finance, Government of India, in 2025 to assess the scheme’s outreach, effectiveness 
and livelihood outcomes. The evaluation highlighted significant achievements of the scheme, with 
33.94 lakh individuals enrolled, of whom 32 lakh  were trained and 31.52 lakh certified, reflecting 
an overall success rate of 99 percent. Women constituted a dominant 82 percent share of total 
participants, while 73 percent beneficiaries belonged to marginalized sections, including SC/ST (36 
percent) and OBC (37 percent). The livelihood impact has been noteworthy, with 90 percent alumni 
utilising acquired skills for income generation, 82 percent becoming economically engaged within 
six months of training, and 60 percent of previously non -earning individuals starting to earn post -
training. 
 
NAPS: A third -party evaluation study of Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Promotion 
Scheme (PMNAPS-2) from 2022-23 to 2025-26 (Data up to 30th November 2025) was conducted 
by the Arun Jaitley National Institute of Financial Management (AJNIFM. As per the r eport, 
PMNAPS-2 achieved significant scale during the evaluation period, engaging 34.69 lakh 
apprentices against a cumulative target of 46 lakh, translating into an overall achievement of 
approximately 75 percent. The institutionalization of Direct Benefit  Transfer (DBT) has improved 
financial transparency and predictability.  
 
(d): Training of Trainers (ToT) under PMKVY is need-based and organized from time to time to 
enhance trainer capacity, certify new trainers, up-skill existing trainers, or align trainers with revised 
Qualification Packs (QPs), National Occupational Standards (N OS), and industry requirements. 
The objective is to ensure the availability of competent and certified trainers for effective delivery 
of skill training programmes under PMKVY while optimizing resources and addressing sector -
specific demand. Since ToT under PMKVY is need-based, requirements for trainers are addressed 
based on demand and scheme-specific needs. 
 
Infrastructure gaps or implementation delays, if identified during monitoring, inspections or 
grievance redressal mechanisms, are addressed promptly. Corrective measures include 
empanelment of qualified trainers, strengthening of training infrastructure, r egular monitoring 
through technology-enabled platforms, periodic inspections, and ensuring compliance with quality 
standards. These measures are aimed at ensuring effective delivery of quality skill training and 
minimizing disruptions in training operations. 

(e): To expand industry partnerships, modernise training infrastructure, enhance digital and 
emerging technology courses and ensure equitable access to quality skill training, the following 
specific steps have been taken by MSDE across the country including Tamil Nadu: 
 
▪ National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. NCVET recognises the 
industry bodies as the Awarding Bodies (ABs) and/or Assessment Agencies (AAs). 
▪ The Awarding Bodies are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry demand 
and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of 
Occupations, 2015 and obtain industry validations. NCVET has approved 10209 
qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of which 2975 qualifications are valid and 
active, and 7234 qualifications are archived. 
▪ Under PMKVY, the new age/future skills job -roles have been specially aligned with Industry 
4.0 requirements in areas like AI/ML, Robotics, Mechatronics, Drone Technology, etc.  for 
upcoming market demand and industry requirements. 
▪ Directorate General of Training (DGT) is implementing Flexi MoU Scheme and Dual System 
of Training (DST) in collaboration with industries to provide training to ITI students in real 
industrial environment. 
▪ DGT has signed MoU with IT Tech companies like IBM, Microsoft, Autodesk, AWS, Shell, etc. 
to ensure industry linkages for the institutes at the state and regional levels. These 
partnerships facilitate the provision of technical and professional skills trai ning in modern 
technologies. 
▪ DGT has introduced new age /future skills courses under CTS to provide training in emerging 
areas such as 5G Network Technician, AI Programming assistant, Cyber Security Assistant, 
Drone Technician etc. 
▪ Two (02) Indian Institute of Skills (IIS) have been established at Ahmedabad and Mumbai, in 
Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode, with an aim to align industry -ready workforce to 
emerging economic opportunities. 
▪ 36 Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry leaders in the respective sectors, have been 
set up which are mandated to identify the skill development needs of respective sectors as 
well as to determine skill competency standards. 
▪ Further, Rozgar Melas and Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas (PMNAMs) have 
been organized by the Ministry to facilitate the placements opportunities to the certified 
candidates across the country. 
▪ MSDE has launched Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a unified platform that integrates skilling, 
education, employment, and entrepreneurship ecosystems to provide a life -long array of 
services. Through Skill India Digital Hub, candidates can have access to s kill training, jobs 
and apprenticeship opportunities. The details of the trained candidates are available on SIDH 
portal for connecting with potential employers. 
▪ To enhance the overall quality and relevance of vocational training in the country, Pradhan 
Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM SETU) scheme 
inter-alia aims to upgrade 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub 
and Spoke model, wherein upgradation includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital 
content, and new courses aligned to industry needs. Also, it aims to augment capacity of five 
NSTIs located in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and  Ludhiana, including 
setting-up sector-specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, with focus on advanced 
training of trainers with global partnership.
